title: Human 3.0 – A Map To Reach The Top 1%
body:
As corny as this may sound, I've always wanted to become an absolute unit of an individual.

Not just having a nice and muscular body, but to be fully developed in every domain of life.

I wanted to become multidimensionally jacked. I wanted to max out all of my stats. I didn't want to be an NPC. I wanted to be a level 100 player. All areas of the map unlocked. Maxed out physicality, intellect, and professions. Bank overflowing with gold. I wanted to do it all. Mind, body, spirit, relationships, money.

This desire has drastically influenced my life.

As a teenager, I became obsessed with fitness. Then, I wanted to absorb as much knowledge as possible. Then I wanted to be free, so I failed at various business models until I finally made one work. I've had various spiritual and philosophical stints that I believe have helped me see “superficial pursuits” like money and fitness in a completely different light than the average person.

Over the past 15 years, I've researched the depths of psychology, personal development, philosophy, social dynamics, technology, the internet, startups, money, religion, and meaning.

After writing about my findings online for the past 6 years, I've noticed critical overlapping patterns that have begun to form a new philosophy for today's world. My personal philosophy, that is, but some may resonate with it.

That's where HUMAN 3.0 comes in.

I want to synthesize everything I've learned into one comprehensive map to navigate the modern landscape. I want to provide you with the knowledge, skills, and principles that help you escape mediocrity and actualize your highest potential. I will attempt to make this as non-dogmatic and science-backed as possible, but I also want to get the point across with clarity and conviction. I plan to write this for today's world using clear, natural language while simplifying these concepts as best I can so that this doesn't turn into a forgotten textbook. For that reason, I am going to speak how I speak and pass the nuance off to you. The nuance and critical thinking always lie with the reader.

Much of it will be wrong, and I encourage you to question what I say. In fact, I hope that you can build this out with me. If you talk about HUMAN 3.0 in your own writing or content, I'd love to see it. Take these ideas and build on them. If you like the H3.0 model, use it.

Now, there are plenty of incredible models already out there.

Spiral Dynamics (psychology), Buddhism & Christianity (meaning), Materialism and Mentalism (nature of reality), eCommerce & consulting (business), Red Pill & Feminism (social dynamics), and so on. Anywhere you look, you can find hundreds of models that promise you the answer to all your problems.

All have their truths, but the critical flaw is that they are often isolated to one domain or perspective of life. We learn math, English, and science as singular, siloed classes when knowledge is an infinite set of nested webs. We dissect frogs in a lab and draw conclusions without considering the entirety of the ecosystem and interconnected relationships from which they come. Beyond that, and for some this is hard to swallow, many spiritual teachers have frail bodies. Many businessmen can't maintain relationships. Many “alpha males” are emotionally unaligned. While these are incredible accomplishments in their own regard, it is rare that one is truly self-developed.

Even if these models or gurus do connect multiple domains, like Ancient Greek philosophies, they were often prevalent before the internet, technology, and AI started to change everything. On a more important note, very few touch on areas such as work and money, which is surprising, as those dominate most people's minds and lives.

Today, we will lay the foundation of HUMAN 3.0.

Over the coming months (maybe years), we will uncover what it truly means to live life to its fullest. I will not be able to cover all of the details that this model contains in this introduction.

> Note: I have created a HUMAN 3.0 Knowledge Base with nuances of the model, civilizational impact, historical context, scientific foundations, and my personal principles weaved in. If you want a comprehensive and skimmable breakdown of the entirety of the model, read it here or paste it into AI to explore it. I’ll also link it at the end (I’d recommend reading this first).

## HUMAN 3.0 – A Model To Maximize Your Potential

I created an AI Prompt to help you map your own development, find your Metatype, and identify the next core problem to solve in your life. I will include a link to it below as well. I would recommend reading this article first so you understand what’s going on.

This model offers the big picture. It is not a dogmatic set of actionable steps, but a set of guidelines for reaching your maximum potential and bust through mental, physical, spiritual, and vocational plateaus faster. It orients patterns found across human development and builds on top of various scientific, psychological, spiritual, and vocational models that have already done a lot of the heavy lifting.

My goal is to take the best parts of the world's greatest theories and apply them to the life of the individual.

> Once you understand this model, you can begin to map where your current level of development lies within each quadrant (your Archetype) and what your overall development looks like (your Metatype). Then, you can attempt to move further toward a 3.0+ Level Metatype - one who has maximized all areas of life.

We will discuss those later in this letter, but for now, let's understand the foundation.

1) Quadrants

The foundation of Human 3.0 is four quadrants that represent the four domains of life.

- Mind (Personal Mental World) – Your thoughts, emotions, beliefs, and internal world. How you interpret the world.

- Body (Personal Physical World) – Your behavior and physical appearance. How the world interprets you. Includes nutrition, training, hobbies, habits, grooming, communication, apparel, etc.

- Spirit (Collective Mental World) – Your relationship to your environment, community, culture, family, friends, colleagues, and reality. How you derive meaning and connection.

- Vocation (Collective Physical World) – Your relationship to systems, structures, and social institutions like education, career, and the economy. How you fit into and contribute to society.

Adapted from Ken Wilber's AQAL model, the quadrants represent the four fundamental perspectives, creating a generalized map of all knowledge and experience.

> This map of reality prevents partial thinking and doesn't reduce problems to one perspective. An internal mental problem may not be best solved by vocational means like getting a new job. A spiritual problem may not be best solved by bodily means like nutrition. A capitalist and Christian are developed in their respective domains, but will experience unnecessary pain when trying to apply their model to problems within other domains. Money often doesn’t solve for meaning and vice versa, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t intimately connected. All of these domains overlap, and by developing yourself in all of the above you begin to live a life where you become in control of your future.Since life, development, and evolution follow a general unfolding toward more chaos or complexity, and ordered structures are created to contain that chaos, we can call the process of life, especially your personal life, "problem solving."

A seed unfolds until it becomes a flower. A flower is many times more complex than a seed, and to reach that state, it needs resources from its environment to self-develop. The seed has the natural desire to grow, and through many courses of evolution, it has solved the problems that have led to many other species of plants dying off.

One may not think the seed is consciously trying to grow or solve problems. Still, through observation and connecting patterns to our personal life, that's what we would call it, since we have created language. We can start to understand that there is a natural flow of life toward greater complexity. Complexity introduces problems, and to constrain the entropy that stems from complexity, an ordered structure must emerge through creation.

In your own personal evolution, you have the desire to reach your potential → you take a step into the unknown and are introduced to complexity → you acquire knowledge and skill to solve problems that prevent forward movement (or stagnate and let chaos consume you) → your identity expands and ascends to a new level → the process repeats unless you get stuck.

This pattern can be noticed across all planes and domains of reality. I encourage you to think through more examples, but for the sake of brevity, let's move on.

2) Levels

Within each quadrant, there are 3 macro levels of development that represent low consciousness (1.0), mid consciousness (2.0), and high consciousness (3.0).

These levels are adapted from various models in developmental psychology, such as Spiral Dynamics and the 9 Stages of Ego Development, which are already well-researched overlays of many psychological theories. In short, these have shown that our mind (our values, beliefs, and worldview that influence how we think and make decisions) evolves through predictable stages over time.

- Human 1.0 (The Conformist) – Values established authority and traditions. Characterized by narrow-mindedness, black and white thinking, and believing there is only "one right way," which often stems from childhood conditioning.

- Human 2.0 (The Individualist) – Rejects the norm and pursues their own goals. Has the desire to acquire status and be perceived as valuable. They are less narrow-minded, but now believe that their way is the one right way.

- Human 3.0 (The Synthesist) – Able to adopt multiple perspectives, connect various patterns of reality, and strategize new paths. They understand that all perspectives hold truths that can be synthesized for more holistic and mutually beneficial results. They can display what some may perceive as level 1 traits, such as narrow-mindedness, but it is an intentional choice to tune out noise.

In a model like Spiral Dynamics, the "spiral" describes how individuals shift focus throughout their development between self and other (like rejecting the community of religion and embracing individual atheism). In Human 3.0, this happens when one reaches a new level in a specific quadrant. Someone can become an Individualist in Mind, which may cause a shift in focus toward Spirit, where they are still at the Conformist stage and submit to authority.

The descriptions of each level take different shapes in each quadrant, like how a 3.0 Synthesist in the Vocation quadrant (Lower Right) can effectively leverage AI to pursue their life’s work, while a 1.0 Conformist believes AI is purely evil due to a lack of knowledge, skill, and experience.

In the Body quadrant (Upper Right), a low consciousness individual has no understanding of the nutrition they put in their body, leading to obesity and sloth, because they haven't acquired the Traits to make better decisions, while a high consciousness individual understands how various nutrients interact with their body and can tweak their diet to help serve their goals.

> These levels reflect your complexity of self in any given domain. The entire Human 3.0 graph represents you. The more complex you are (by cultivating perspective and expanding consciousness), the more interesting life becomes, because you can choose the challenges you wish to take on. Like a video game: Level 1 is similar to an NPC or non-player character running on a script, Level 2 is the main character choosing their storyline, and Level 3 is the programmer who can create new games that others also enjoy playing.Note: Lower or higher levels are not “bad” or “good,” they are points along someone’s individual journey. A person who is “high consciousness” is not better, just more developed, and that development has it’s obvious perks.You do not leave any given level. You transcend and include the one before it. You acquire a greater perspective that allows you to leverage the knowledge, skill, and tools that you acquired during the lower stages.

We will discuss more examples in depth below.

If you're enjoying this, join here if you want these articles sent directly to you, just in case the algorithm doesn't show you them.

3) Phases

Within each level, there are 3 phases of development that one must go through to reach the next level. Phases represent vertical development, moving up a level or regressing back down.

There are 3 general patterns that we can observe when an individual goes through a profound change:

- Dissonance (Phase 1) – Once an individual has "gotten their taste" of their current stage of life, and if they do not get numbed by narrow-mindedness and comfort, they will feel tired of where they are, but unsure of what kind of life comes next.

- Uncertainty (Phase 2) – If that individual becomes aware enough of their distaste, they take an uncertain step into the unknown and open themselves up to new knowledge and skill.

- Discovery (Phase 3) – Like navigating a map, they discover the education, tools, resources, and insights that allow them to reach the next level of development.

For terminology's sake, we can map specific areas of one's life by appending the phase they are in to the level they are in within a particular domain.

As an example, "Vocation 2.1" (Level 2, Phase 1) would represent the development of collective exterior consciousness (relationship to systems, structures, and social institutions). The "2" represents the Individualist level, and ".1" represents that they have almost exhausted that stage and must take an uncertain step toward level 3 to discover what lies in their next chapter. For the Vocation quadrant, this could mean that they have pursued a new career, but realized they were climbing the wrong ladder, and need to make a shift toward discovering their calling.

> Individuals can easily experience False Transformation during this process. They may feel as if they've advanced through each phase to reach a new level, but they are simply imitating what that level of development would look like without the required trait development. This is self-deception and traps people in their current stage, preventing them from progressing further until they solve the remaining problems that exist at their current level.This False Transformation can happen when one develops themself in one domain (like the domain of mind) and they assume they have advanced in another (like the domain of spirit or vocation).Individuals can also regress to a lower level during a temporary period of stress or when a problem outside their current level comes into their life. This explains why you may look back to a time where "things felt better" and you yearn to bring that sensation back to the present.

An enjoyable life, as shown in flow psychology and the musings of many philosophers such as Nietzsche, resides in the progression through these phases by overcoming resistance. Profound change rarely happens by accident. When you are intentional about your vision, goals, and priorities without regressing by nature of distractions and comfort, the chaos that would consume most people during these phases becomes tolerable and often the most fulfilling parts of life that you hold close to your heart.

At level 3 and beyond, individuals can pursue more complex challenges and simulate these phases for the love of the game (like a CEO who sells their company, becomes depressed, and starts another one from a more enlightened point of view), and since they create the game, it becomes infinite.

4) Traits

Within each phase, there is a threshold of knowledge, experience, and skill that must be acquired before the next level reveals itself to you. While phases represent vertical development, traits represent horizontal development, or navigating the unknown until you have discovered enough to reach the next phase.

Each quadrant, level, and phase presents different challenges that demand a certain level of skill. That skill requires experimentation and education.

> One can be knowledgeable in fitness, but without practice and experience, they become the fat personal trainer archetype. Their knowledge is admirable, but few people take them seriously, which has it’s pros and cons.

The trap with both vertical (phases) and horizontal (traits) development is boredom and anxiety. If you attempt to jump to a new level of development without the skill and experience to do so, you will become anxious and fail. If you do not attempt to move up a level at all, you will grow bored and resort to comfort and distraction.

Both boredom and anxiety lead to disorder in the mind and remove you from the unfolding flow of evolution. Your life may seem okay, but everything feels dull and meaningless.

That leads us into Channels – a way to combat disorder and make substantial progress.

5) Channels

When you reach the Dissonance Phase of any Level, you gain the ability to leverage a “Channel.”

Think of a Channel as an exciting quest in a video game. A rabbit hole of knowledge or skill. When you can’t stop researching a topic or working on a project and time passes by surprisingly quick.

On the Human 3.0 Graph, you can see that one end of the Channel is in the knowledge Trait while the other is in the skill Trait. Usually, a person becomes “obsessed” with learning or building, and that results in rapid experience gain moving them quickly toward their next Level of development within a specific quadrant.

A few examples would be:

- Mind – Becoming immersed in a deep meditative state (skill) or following a line of thought that keeps you up at night, resulting in a plethora of ideas that light up your brain (knowledge).

- Body – You find a new diet, supplement, or methodology and binge-watch all possible content you can about it (knowledge). You become obsessed with running or lifting for a 3-month period, making more gains than you ever have before (skill).

- Spirit – Mystical experiences. Honeymoon phases. Intimate moments. Finding a philosophy that “clicks” with your current phase of life. And so on.

- Vocation – Reaching a point of maximum clarity that quickly leads into an exciting career change, product launch, or creative stint (skill). You find the perfect opportunity and can’t stop learning the required skills to start a business (knowledge).

The process for entering a Channel is as follows.

First, you must reach the Dissonance phase after you fully acclimate to the Level you are in. Once you grow tired of where you are, and if you don’t become numb to your problems, you use your distaste as fuel to push into the unknown. You create an aim or vision or goal within a specific quadrant (like Body). You begin acquiring knowledge and skill. You learn and do. You make mistakes and refine your aim. You experiment enough until you find the Channel that you get sucked into.

You can tell someone is in a Channel by how excited they are when they talk about it, like someone who has reached the point of writing a book where the words can’t stop flowing. They have vision. Their skill and knowledge provide a sense of clarity that allows them to shoot forward in progress.

When you are in the Dissonance phase, the best advice I can give is to search for excitement and enthusiasm and pursue that without shame, because that shame signals a lower Level of Mind, and you can develop the skill of confidence during that process.

> On “Glitches:”
There are certain tactics to force yourself into a Channel or bust through a developmental plateau that we will call “Glitches” – like a glitch in the matrix, if the matrix were the boundaries of Level 1 and 2 until you create your own in Level 3.Psychedelics can force someone into a mystical experience. PEDs can accelerate fitness progress. Moving into an apartment you can’t afford can provide a real deadline, forcing you to learn and do until you make your side business work.AI is the most recent and widely available Glitch that crosses into all domains. It can be used to self-develop or self-destruct rapidly. Taste and discerment is required. AI is only pure good or pure evil from a limited perspective.Be careful with these, as while they accelerate progress, they increase in risk at lower levels of consciousness. If you take psychedelics without prior experience to interpret that altered state, you may go insane. AI psychosis and outsourcing your mind to AI is becoming more prevalent, not because AI is bad, but because it’s like taking steroids. If you haven’t built a base, extensively studied all domains of nutrition, understood all potential interactions, and been training for 5+ years (metaphorically), the AI will have nasty side effects. Even then, many high reward mechanisms in reality come at a cost no matter how careful you are. For certain people with certain goals, one can make a conscious decision to take that risk despite the consequences. For most people, especially in Level 1, they are death sentences.Max out your “natural” potential so you have ample experience and don’t get one-shotted. Knowledge and skill decrease risk.

If you feel lost, you are probably in a Dissonance phase, and if you stick it out, you can find your next Channel and fall back in love with life.

## Archetypes & Metatypes

In future letters and videos, we can use the Human 3.0 Graph to understand people (like Jordan Peterson, Andrew Tate, or Alan Watts), or to overcome problems in your life, like not being able to make money or find a partner.

If you have a specific request for a problem you're facing or a person you want to understand, reply to this letter.

In this model, I've included what are called Archetypes and Metatypes.

- Archetypes – patterns of people that show up in specific quadrants and levels within those quadrants.

- Metatypes – the synthesis of a single person's four archetypes within each quadrant.

Think of Metatypes as a sort of personality test, but for one’s self-development.

I created a prompt to identify your Metatype, map your development across all quadrants, and find the core problem in your life here.

In the example above, I am only showing 3 archetypes within each quadrant. There are many more than that, so please understand that these are not set in stone. I’m just having fun with these.

You'll notice that there is a general progression from low consciousness to high consciousness as someone develops themself within a quadrant:

NPC → Player → Creator in the Mind quadrant describes someone who stops living by the script they were assigned at birth, starts playing their own game, then creates new games to play (similar to "construct-level" awareness).

Incel → Chad → Sigma or Beta Male → Alpha Male → Sigma Male in the Body quadrant are common archetypes we see in today's world that you can observe in one's behavior and appearance. This can correspond with other areas on the graph or have further causes within the same quadrant. Like how an Incel typically has higher estrogen levels from diet and environment, and how social structures in the Vocation quadrant have led to processed food and microplastics, which further exacerbate that problem on a mass scale.

Job → Career → Calling is one of many progressions in the Vocation quadrant. Relating to work, this can start with anything nowadays. Some people may not even have a job, or they go into their calling early in life. The key insight about the progression through each level is that they start with low consciousness (Conformist) and have the ability to progress to high consciousness (Synthesist).

Religion → Atheism → Mysticism in the Spirit quadrant is a common pattern (not the only pattern) that we see in those raised in a strict religious household, leading to rebellion. Then they rediscover a new perspective on God and loop back around to the truths that were contained in Level 1.

> Ken Wilber's "pre-trans fallacy" occurs when people confuse pre-rational (Conformist) states with trans-rational (Synthesist) states because both appear "non-rational" from a conventional rational (Individualist) perspective. This can happen both ways.One can elevate a Level 1 primitive state to Level 3 status, and some often reduce genuine Level 3 development to being primitive thinking.In other words, a "bible thumper" with lack of knowledge and experience beyond their childhood conditioning finds it difficult to take a mystic seriously, when the mystic often holds the same truths, but from a more comprehensive perspective.If it helps, think of the IQ bell curve meme.

Of course, this is only one minor example of how developmental progression can play out in the Spirit quadrant. There are various patterns across personal relationships, sports, families, scientific or metaphysical beliefs, and more.

There are dozens to hundreds of archetypes within each quadrant, not just the three I displayed in each.

Now, for the example given above, when we plot points of development within each quadrant, level, phase, and trait, we gain a comprehensive understanding of where a certain individual lies. (You can see this in the opaque white shape on the map.)

This specific example of a person would be at Human 2.0.

How do we come to that?

For every point in Level 1, they receive 1 point.

For every point in Level 2, they receive 2.

For every point in Level 3, they receive 3.

Then, we can divide by the total amount by 12 (the total number of developmental slices on the graph), resulting in 2.0.

In this example, we can create a description for their development within each quadrant as follows:

- Mind – No longer lives by a script and is close to construct level awareness.

- Body – Ungroomed and has poor habits, but occasionally exudes confidence.

- Spirit – Believes in the literal interpretation of God, but is tolerant of atheist friends and peers.

- Vocation – Has a valuable set of education and skills, but is focused on a safe and fulfilling career.

If we were to map more than just 3 Archetypes per quadrant, this would become a lot more complex and comprehensive, but we will save that for future letters.

Now, if we take those descriptions and merge them into one, we get their Metatype. I plan to use AI for this because I don't want things to be a static "personality test" that puts you in one of 16 generalized boxes.

In this case, we can consider this person's Metatype to be "The Outlier." In brief, this is someone who has drifted away from mainstream patterns without rebellion, operating from a countercultural lens. They don’t care about their appearance, but this may be False Transformation, as they lack experience in the Body quadrant.

## The 3.0 Lifestyle

“How does one balance development in all quadrants? Especially if one quadrant exhausts a lot of time, focus, and energy?”

The ultimate goal is to create a lifestyle where all quadrants are accounted for through problem-solving.

If your Vocation consumes too much of your time so that your Mind is distraught, you are too drained for your Body, and cannot entertain Spirit, that is an obvious problem that you must attempt to solve through knowledge and skill acquisition, creating the chance for a Channel. In this case, one may study business opportunities for an hour every day and make some time for practice. It may take longer than someone else, but once you begin moving through the Phases, you feel more confident that you can decrease or completely eliminate the current job that is taking up your time.

That shift may make another problem more apparent, like having low energy or not being respected by potential clients and customers. Reaching the next level of business may not require more development in business, but in solving problems related to the body, mind, or spirit. Even then, you may build an incredible business and have all the money in the world, but you can have a hole in the middle of your chest due to a lack of meaning in your Vocational pursuits.

By the simple nature of problem-solving (and staying vigilant of distractions that prevent you from noticing them), you create a lifestyle where work becomes play, health is your default state, meaning is abundant, and your mind is on your side.

If you actually read all the way to the bottom, nice.

title: How to become disgustingly self-disciplined
body:
Tell me if this sounds familiar.

You want to change your life.

Like really bad.

You’re tired of where you are. You’re tired of your physique, or how your mind is not your friend, or how you have to stress over not being able to pay the bills each month, or how you’re going to end up alone.

You finally gain the motivation to start in the gym, start the business, start talking to more people, you know the drill.

Fast forward 2-4 weeks and nothing has changed.

You don’t even know how it happened... you just ended up back in your old life without making any progress.

And this isn’t the first time. You lock in, fall off, lock in again, fall off, and 10 years go by (for some people, their entire life goes by) without breaking the habit of being your worst self.

It sucks.

It’s like you never even tried to change.

Because, well, frankly, you didn’t.

You didn’t actually try.

So what do you do?

If you look at the top athletes, startup founders, visionaries, and strategists who seem to work 16 hours a day without breaking a sweat, do you think they struggle to do that?

Or is that what they want to do?

Is it actually hard for them? No. In fact, it’s extremely hard for them to do what the average person does. It’s a living hell for them to even sense that they’re devolving into a mediocre life.

Why? Because that’s who they are.

How do we replicate this in our own life?

Buckle up.

It gets bumpy.

## Become so disgusted with where you are, you have no option but to win

Rockets use 85% to 90% of their total mass as fuel during launch and acceleration, whereas coasting requires zero fuel once orbital or escape velocity is reached.

In other words, what gets you started isn’t what keeps you going.

It’s counterintuitive, as most of life’s truths are, but if you want sustainable change, then you have to brute-force your way into it.

That’s stage one.

The launch fuel. Motivation, pain, a win, a loss, or a burst of willpower. Something that launches you into an intense period of change.

There have been many times in my life when I have used what I call tactical stress.

I move into an apartment I can’t afford so I’m forced to make my business successful enough to afford it, or I go homeless, as one example. I wouldn’t go homeless of course, but I believed I would have. I’ve done that multiple times, and it’s the single greatest “business growth hack” I’ve found. It sounds extreme, and that’s the point. It’s not for everyone, it’s only for those who believe in themselves.

About 5 years ago, I would intentionally go to raves, drink, and party every 2 months or so as a form of glitch in my overly optimized lifestyle. I also enjoyed doing it. It was a nice little shock to the system. The next morning, as you would guess, I would feel horrible. I felt my progress in business and health slipping, and since those goals mattered to me, I usually woke up the next morning with renewed motivation to push as hard as I could.

That leads to the second most potent fuel I’ve found, which is a strong disgust for the life I do not want to live. That’s what almost anyone can take advantage of if they want to change. Waking up with a bad hangover is one way to do it (if you actually have a goal that makes the hangover a bad thing), but there’s another way if that’s not your cup of tea.

For the entirety of this week, here’s what I want you to do:

Observe society and see where most people end up. It’s not pretty. Usually broke, overweight, married to someone they grow to hate, and drowning in financial responsibilities that take advantage of their situation making it nearly impossible to get out. That’s the default end state of the average person’s life. Thanks, entropy.

If thinking about that for a week doesn’t light a fire in your belly (it does for me every time I think about it), the next option is to simply let yourself go until the pain is so great that you never want to experience that life again.

For many people, that's not far off. The problem is that they numb the pain. They shove it in the back of their mind because it would be too painful to face.

If you can face it for a week, that will do the trick.

But now that we have the launch fuel, how do we actually turn that into something sustainable?

## You aren’t disciplined because you aren’t the person who doesn’t view it as discipline.

> At this point in our history it should be possible for an individual to build a self that is not simply the outcome of biological drives and cultural habits, but a conscious, personal creation.

– Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi

I’m begging you to understand this.

Do you think Elon Musk lies around in bed when he wakes up, dreading the day ahead? Do you think he hits snooze 5 times, dreaming of not having to go to work?

Do you think Arnold Schwarzenegger had to trick himself into eating healthy and training twice a day?

Do you think that high performers of this caliber consider it “hard” (in your sense of the word) to do hard things? Or do they love it?

It’s just what they do. It’s automatic.

If I am laser-focused on a goal, like cutting weight while hitting my macro targets, a cheat meal at McDonald's doesn’t sound tasty to me. It sounds fucking disgusting. You would have to pry me from my chair to get me to even lick a double quarter pounder with cheese. It would take an immense amount of discipline for me to eat mediocre food.

That sounds pretentious, I’m aware of that, but it’s going to be far easier for me to drop 10-20 pounds than it is for the person who can’t stop thinking about the next time they get to drown in grease.

People who cannot fathom this will then say, “Why don’t you have a little fun! Lighten up!” as a defense mechanism to protect their identity, but what they do not understand is that I am having more fun now than I would be going with you to eat your entire daily caloric allowance in 15 minutes just to go into a food coma and sloth around the rest of the day. Yes, so fun!

It is one of the greatest feelings in the world to be in pursuit of your potential, with little to no gap between who you are and who you want to be. You live in the flow state, a video game, taking on a string of challenging quests you choose to accept, and being rewarded amply for doing so. Maybe not in the form of money, but insight, experience, and direct feedback from reality.

But identity change is so abstract.

You can’t see your identity.

It’s not like a business where you have a direct and rapid feedback mechanism like money - if you aren’t making any, reality is telling you you’re doing something wrong, and if you are making money, reality is telling you you’re exactly where you should be revenue-wise.

So what do we do? How do we take the dirty launch fuel and turn it into a sustainable system that eventually becomes “just who I am?”

## Give me 10 minutes and I’ll show you how to become someone entirely new

> You should be far more concerned with your current trajectory than with your current results.

– James Clear

You are the statistical sum of what you repeatedly do.

And what you do is more than the physical decisions you make.

You are the accumulated result of everything that flows through you, in both directions, input and output.

Input = everything you’re exposed to. Every book you read. Every post you glance at for a split second. Every person you call a friend. Every belief your parents and teachers installed before you even had a chance to consent. The news you read to stay informed. The conversations you overhear. The people whose lives you watch from a distance.

Output = everything you produce in the world. Your decisions, actions, works, and work. What you do when no one is watching and what you do when everyone is.

That is literally the entire equation.

Input shapes the mind that perceives situations and makes decisions. Output shapes the life that presents the next input. It compounds.

To change who we are we must change this flow of information and action.

For input, the rule is simple.

Curate and protect everything your mind is exposed to on a daily basis. You must immerse yourself in stimuli that match the person you want to become and starve the person you used to be. The old you must die.

Some may see what’s below and think “Oh I already knew that.” or “That’s just basic self-help.”

But if you actually knew it, you wouldn’t be in this situation, would you? Writing it off as “basic” keeps you from seeing how simple this all is. You are not special, and you do not need something novel to change your life. You need what’s been proven to work for the entirety of human existence.

First, choose your information diet.

Most people are intellectually obese. Unfollow, mute, and unsubscribe from anything that lowers your standards or wastes your attention. Follow and read the people and ideas that raise it. Your social timeline is an environment just like any other. You live in it, and it influences you.

Second, choose the people you surround yourself with.

Their values, fears, and assumptions about what’s normal and possible leak into you even if you think they don’t. This is the most difficult part. You can try to bring your friends along with you, but it is extremely difficult to help people who don’t want to be helped.

Third, interrogate your mind for beliefs that do not serve you.

Most of your beliefs about money, what you deserve in this life, and what’s possible to achieve were determined before you could even understand the language you speak. If you haven’t become aware of these beliefs, then it’s unlikely that they have shifted. You cannot change what you have not examined.

Fourth, exchange passive for active consumption.

The difference between reading ten posts fast and one book slowly is drastic. I bet you can’t tell me about even 2 of the social posts you read yesterday. But a life changing YouTube video, podcast, book chapter, or Substack article that is created with care by someone who is passionate about what they do is something that sticks with you, and influences you for the better.

## Make it so easy succeed you’d look stupid if you fail

I forgot to mention something important.

This is the second stage of change.

The first is the launch. You know, using a dirty fuel to gain the motivation to make the change in the first place. Because frankly, without it, you probably aren’t going to change your inputs, and you won’t be able to break through the atmosphere and coast with the sustainable system we are about to create.

Your outputs, or decisions and actions, occur as a four-part feedback loop:

Environment → Signal → Behavior → Payoff

This is essentially the habit loop from B.F. Skinners operant conditioning, which went on to be popularized by Charles Duhigg (The Power of Habit) and James Clear (Atomic Habits).

Cue → response → reward is textbook behavioral psychology. It works.

The first step is making the desired output the path of least resistance, and the undesired output incredibly inconvenient.

The second is creating a trigger, or signal that starts the behavior that leads to the desired output, preferably on a daily basis.

The third is reducing success to the minimum recognizable version of the output (not a great workout, but stepping into the gym).

The fourth is the reward. Something enjoyable delivered right after the behavior, every single time, until the behavior is the reward itself.

This feedback loop is best illustrated with examples:

Goal 1 = Gaining muscle in the gym.

First, you curate your inputs. Follow two to three sources of inspiration and education so your feed reminds you of your goal as you make this change. Unfollow the fitness content that sells insecurity and acceptance of mediocrity. Surround yourself with at least one person who already trains, because their normal becomes your normal. Examine the beliefs installed in you about your body and what you’re capable of.

Then engineer your outputs.

Environment - Set your clothes out the night before, remove all junk food from your cabinets, and study the exercises you’re doing in tomorrows workout so you have clarity, and maybe a bit of excitement, to try them out.

Signal - Go at the same time every day. For me, that time is around 11am. If you’re just starting, set an alarm for that time, and make the alarm a distinct tone that represents going to the gym.

Behavior - Show up and only promise yourself you’ll do the minimum. One hard set. Chances are you’ll want to keep going since you’re already there.

Reward - Stop at the local smoothie place or even a gas station to get a protein shake. This was my reward when I first started. Sure, they’re probably not that great for you, but big picture the end state you are pursuing outweighs any minor damage it does.

Goal 2 = Turning your interests or writing into a business

We talk about this a lot here, so it’s a worthy example.

Inputs - Follow the creators you want to model and the thinkers who sharpen your ideas. Starve yourself of everything else, let your algorithm become a source of inspiration. Read books and long form content from people who have achieved what you want, they are your mentors. Create a new digital friend group of people who are doing the same thing - you could probably meet them in the comments of this article. Examine your beliefs about money, whether you believe it’s difficult to make, and whether wealth generation is luck or skill.

Environment - Add your idea capture app as a shortcut on your phone. Have your writing/scheduling app open so articles, posts, and newsletters write themselves. Batch your highest priority, highest leverage, and most difficult tasks in the morning.

Signal - Your first coffee in the morning at your desk, a specific song to start off the writing session, something like that, but never only relying on inspiration as a signal to create.

Behavior - Post the minimum amount of content necessary. One post a day, one newsletter a week, with the minimum quality. You just need it to go out, you don’t need it to be perfect or brilliant. Consistency both outruns and creates taste.

Reward - For me, I enjoy walks. I always want to be outside. Once I finish my 2-3 main priorities in the morning, the walk is my reward. For you it could be tracking a streak and seeing the number go up. Eating breakfast (I also like “fasting” while I work, although it’s not long enough to be considered intermittent fasting. Helps with focus.)

I think you get the point.

Launch the rocket. Become heavily inspired or heavily disgusted with where your life is. Whichever fuel you thrive on, neither is bad when channeled toward something meaningful.

Do not waste that beautifully potent fuel. Use it to create the system. Make the behavior automatic, and eventually it will become “just what I do.”

And finally, if that last example is something you resonate with, you can now sell digital products in Eden.

Not just a course or ebook, but a better way to monetize your interests and knowledge.

Think of it like a course you can talk to, or an ebook you can talk to, or even an article that helps you implement what’s inside (I could quickly turn this article into a product and sell it for $10 and link it here).

It’s your own AI, with your knowledge inside.

You no longer need to build or maintain your own AI app, and you don’t need to worry about AI costs. We handle that for you.

So, if you sell an ebook or course, or if you give out prompts or Custom GPTs, or you have something valuable that would be worth selling - you will make more money (and your product will be perceived as more valuable) if you sell it on Eden.

Info products are not even close to dead, they just haven’t evolved to live in the AI age.

It’s your knowledge, and other people can chat with it without needing you there.

Learn more about it here.

Or use this custom AI to help you come up with a profitable digital product idea. It also helps you build it.

Thank you for reading.

Talk soon.

– Dan

title: 子供を産んだ私から、産まないと決めていた私へ
body:
その河には、一度だけ渡れる橋がある。向こう岸に着いたら、もう戻れない。

　結婚8年目にして子供を産んだ。と言うと、だいたい不妊治療をしていたと思われる。違う。子供はいなくていいと自分の意志で持たなかった。

　いまはこの文章を、赤子を抱きながらスマホで打っている。秋雨の音とミルクの匂いに包まれた我が子は途方もなく愛おしいけれど、それでもなお、私は「子供を持つ」が当たり前の世界に首を傾げている。まとまらない思考を、そのままに書く。

　 仕事は順調で、夫とも仲が良い。お金を貯めて海外旅行することもあるし、夜中までおいしいものをたらふく食べて昼まで眠る日もある。至上の日々を出来るかぎり続けられれば、それでよかったはずだった。

　はずだったのに、33歳ごろから頭の中にはいつもあの問いがあった。子供を持たなくて、ほんとうにいいの？子供が産めない年になってから後悔しない？

　30代の女は生きてるだけで、産んだ人、産めなかった人、産まなかった人それぞれの本音が流れ込んでくる。子供がいる人、欲しい人のほうが、いない人より何倍も大変そうだ。なのに、目には見えない何かが「本当に子供を持たなくていいの？」と耳元で囁き続けた。その正体が社会的圧力なのか、単に未来の可能性がひとつ減ることへの恐れなのか、未だわからない。

　でも、同時に自分に問う。こんなにも子連れが歓迎されない国で産んでいいの？ 何台も優先エレベーターを見送らないと、ベビーカーが乗せてもらえない東京で？

　そんな「産むか、産まざるべきか」の反復横跳びの果てに、なぜ産むことにしたのか。申し訳ないけど、この先に役に立つ話はない。すごく曖昧な、捉えどころのない言葉の連なりでしかない。

　私が子供を持とうと思った理由のひとつは、夫となら大丈夫だと思えたから。

　当初、夫には「一緒に苦しんでくれるなら子供を考えてもいいよ」と話していた。子供と引き換えに私が失う睡眠や自由を、あなたも等しく失ってください。子育てのベストパートナーとは、一緒に地獄に堕ちてくれる人だと信じていたから。

　しかし夫が私にした提案は、二人で地獄から逃れる方法を探して徹底的に足掻くことだった。

　私の妊娠中、夫は二人とも睡眠時間が取れるシフト制の育児スケジュールを作成し、健診に毎回付き添い、役所に保活について聞きに行き、私が床に落としたものを片っ端から拾い（そう、お腹が大きくなるとしゃがむことすらままならない）、長谷川あかりのレシピを作りまくり、有象無象の育児便利グッズから最適なものを選び、複雑怪奇な作りのプーメリーを組み立て、赤子の服を水通しし、出生届をはじめとする全ての書類仕事を担い、いつのまにか「赤ちゃんのための家」を完成させていた。

　出産の主体者が私なら、育児の主体者は完全に夫だった（夫は夫で「父親＝子育てに消極的」というステレオタイプに苦しめられるのだけど、それはまた別の話）。

　おかげでまだ3時間おきにミルクを欲しがる赤ん坊を育てながら、夫婦共にがっつり寝て、私は本を読み、編み物をし、この文章を書いている。今のところは、自分の人生を子育てに全て捧げずにいられる。逆に言えば、ここまでしないと女性は強制的に母親に転生させられてしまうのだと、強烈な現実があることを実感した。

　もうひとつの「子供を持とうと思った理由」は、シンプルに悩み続ける体力が尽きたからだ。情けないことに。

　子供を持たないというのは、あえてそう選択した人として扱われる。

　友達が産み、同僚が産み、後輩が産む。みんなが「お母さん」になっていく中で、自分だけがならない理由を持ち続けるのは意外と辛い。かと言って周りに流されて産もうというのは、あまりにも命に対して無責任な気がした。

　果てのない迷いの中、いつも思い浮かぶのは大きな河のイメージだった。

　泳ぎきれないほどの大きな流れに、一度だけ渡れる橋がある。両岸には子供がいない私と、子供がいる私がそれぞれ暮らしている。橋の真ん中で立ち尽くした私は、両岸の自分をじっと見つめている。

　どっちの人生を選べば、失敗しないのか。自分なりの正解を見つけたくて橋の真ん中で立ち続けた。子供がいて幸せな自分、子供を産んで後悔する自分、望んでも授かることができない自分、二人暮らしを満喫する自分、歳をとってから子供が欲しかったことに気づく自分。まるで映画の「エブリシング・エブリウェア・オール・アット・ワンス」のマルチバースの世界のように、あらゆるパターンの人生を心の中で生きた。

　そんなふうに橋の真ん中で立ち尽くし疲れて果て、どうせなら自分たち「人間」という種族がどういう生き物なのか、ゼロからしっかり見届けてやろうじゃないかと子供を持つことにしたのだった。

　こうして流れ着くように　「子供がいる人生」の岸に行ってしまったけれど、いざ暮らしてみたら案外楽しい。すくすくと成長する赤ん坊は見てて飽きない。人間って面白い生物だなと素直に思う。

　私が子供を抱きしめたり、ミルクを作ってたりする合間に、ふと対岸を見れば、子供のいない私がのんびり美術館をはしごしたり、仕事の締め切りに追われていたりする。「子供のいない私」は消滅したのではなく、どこかでちゃんと生きていて、達者にやっている気がする。

　限界まで向き合ったからこそ、子供がいる自分も、いなかった自分もぜんぶ抱えて生きていける。

　子供がいる、いない。その間に流れる河はなくならない。橋も、一度しか渡れない。それでも、向こう岸にいる自分に手を振ることはできる。そんなふうに生きていけたらと思う。

　なんてここまで書いたけれど、これってぜんぶ今現在のポジショントークでしかない。

　子供を授かれるのか、無事に産めるのか、キャリアへの影響、無痛分娩へのアクセスのしやすさや金銭状況などなど。運がよかったからこんな呑気なことを言ってられるだけだ。この先はどうなるかわからない。

　だって出産も子育ても、一度テーブルについたら絶対に降りられない博打だから。

　そんな賭けを片方の性別だけに押し付けようとする世界はやっぱり異常だ。この気持ちは子供を産んでも変わらない。母親になっても、どんなに我が子が愛しくても、この違和感に馴染みたくないという今の私を、ここに置いておく。

title: A harness for every task: dynamic workflows in Claude Code
body:
Last week, we released dynamic workflows in Claude Code. Claude can now write its own harness on the fly, custom-built for the task at hand.

While the default Claude Code harness is built for coding, it is also useful for many other types of tasks because, as it turns out, many tasks resemble coding tasks. But there are certain classes of tasks where we have had to build custom harnesses on top of Claude Code to achieve peak performance such as Research, security analysis, agent teams, or Code Review.

Workflows allow you to dynamically create harnesses that enable Claude to solve all of those problems and more natively inside of Claude Code. You can also share and re-use these workflows with others.

In this article, I’ll cover my initial workflows experiences and learnings so you can take full advantage. 

That said, best practices are still developing! Dynamic workflows often use more tokens, so think carefully about when and how to use them.

Note: this post is also available on the Claude Blog

## Example prompts

Before diving into the technical details, I’d like to start with some example prompts to get you thinking about the possibilities with workflows:

- "This test fails maybe 1 in 50 runs. Set up a workflow to reproduce it, form theories and adversarially test them in worktrees /goal don't stop until one theory works."

- "Using a workflow, go through my last 50 sessions and mine them for corrections I keep making and turn the recurring ones into CLAUDE.md rules"

- “Use a workflow to dig through #incidents in Slack for the past six months and find recurring root causes where nobody has filed a ticket."

- "Take my business plan and run a workflow where different agents tear it apart from an investor's, a customer's, and a competitor's perspective."

- "Here's a folder of 80 resumes, use a workflow to rank them for the backend role and double-check the top ten. Interview me using the AskUserQuestion tool for a rubric."

- "I need a name for this CLI tool. Use a workflow to brainstorm a bunch of options and run a tournament to pick the top 3."

- "Use a workflow to rename our User model to Account everywhere."

- “Go through my blog post draft and using a workflow verify every technical claim against the codebase, I don't want to ship anything wrong."

## How dynamic workflows work

Dynamic workflows execute a javascript file with a few special functions that help spawn and coordinate subagents:

Dynamic workflows also include standard JavaScript functions like JSON, Math, and Array, to help process data.

It’s particularly useful to know that dynamic workflows can decide which models an agent uses and whether subagents are run in their own worktree, allowing Claude to choose the intelligence level and isolation needed.

If a workflow is interrupted, for example by user action or quitting the terminal, resuming the session will allow the workflow to pick up where it left off.

## Why dynamic workflows

When you ask the default Claude Code harness to do a task, it needs to both plan and execute in the same context window. For many coding tasks, this is highly effective, but it can sometimes break down over long-running, massively parallel and/or highly structured adversarial tasks.

This is because the longer Claude works on a complex task in a single context window, the more it becomes susceptible to a few specific failure modes:

- Agentic laziness refers to when Claude stops before finishing a particularly complex, multi-part task and declares the job done after partial progress, for example addressing 20 of the 50 items in a security review.

- Self-preferential bias refers to Claude’s tendency to prefer its own results or findings, especially when asked to verify or judge them against a rubric.

- Goal drift refers to the gradual loss of fidelity to the original objective across many turns, especially after compaction. Each summarization step is lossy, and details like edge-case requirements or "don't do X" constraints can get lost.

Creating a workflow helps combat these by orchestrating separate Claudes with their own context windows and focused, isolated goals.

## Dynamic vs static workflows

You may have previously created a static workflow using the Claude Agent SDK or claude -p to coordinate multiple instances of Claude Code together.

But because static workflows need to work for all edge cases, they are usually more generic. With Claude Opus 4.8 and dynamic workflows, Claude is now intelligent enough to write a custom harness tailor-made for your use case.

# Helpful patterns when using dynamic workflows

You can start using dynamic workflows just by asking Claude to make one, or by using the trigger word “ultracode” to ensure that Claude Code creates a workflow.

But building a mental model for how dynamic workflows work will help you understand when to use them and how you might nudge Claude via prompts.

There are a few common patterns that Claude might use and compose together when building workflows:

Classify-and-act

Use a classifier agent to decide on the type of task, and then route to different agents or behavior based on the task. Or, use a classifier at the end to determine output.

Fan-out-and-synthesize

Split up a task into many smaller steps, run an agent on each step and then synthesize those results. This is particularly useful for when there are a large number of smaller steps, or when each step benefits from its own clean context window so they don't interfere or cross-contaminate. The synthesize step is a barrier—it waits for all the fan-out agents, then merges their structured outputs into one result.

Adversarial verification

For each spawned agent, run a separate spawned agent to adversarially verify its output against a rubric or criteria.

Generate-and-filter

Generate a number of ideas on a topic and then filter them by a rubric or by verification, dedupe duplicates and return only the highest quality, tested ideas.

Tournament

Instead of dividing the work, have agents compete on it. Spawn N agents that each attempt the same task using different approaches. Prompts or models then judge the results in a pairwise fashion using a judging agent until you have a winner.

Loop until done

For tasks with an unknown amount of work, loop spawning agents until a stop condition is met (no new findings, or no more errors in the logs) instead of a fixed number of passes.

# Use cases

Think creatively of when and how to ask Claude Code to make dynamic workflows. I’ve found that workflows are sometimes even more useful for non-technical work.

## Migrations and refactors

Bun was rewritten from Zig to Rust using workflows. You can read more about how that was done in Jarred’s X thread.

The key is to break down the task into a series of steps that need to be operated on for example callsites, failing tests, modules, etc. Spin off a subagent for every fix in a worktree to make the fix, then have another agent adversarially review, and merge them. Consider telling the agent not to use resource intensive commands so that you can maximally parallelize without running out of resources on your machine.

## Deep research

We published a deep research skill (/deep-research) inside Claude Code that uses dynamic workflows. Specifically, it fans-out web searches, fetches sources, adversarially verifies their claims, and synthesizes a cited report.

But you may do this sort of research for more than just web searches. For example, asking Claude to compile a status report from context in Slack or to research how a feature works by exploring a codebase in-depth.

## Deep verification

On the other hand, if you have a report where you want to check and source every factual claim that it references you may want to generate a workflow which has one agent identify all of the factual claims and then spin off a subagent to check each one in-detail. You could also have a verification agent check the source subagent to make sure its source is high quality.

## Sorting

You may have a list of items that you want to sort by some qualitative measurement that you believe that Claude Code is good at evaluating, for example: support tickets sorted by severity of the bug. But if you try to sort 1000+ rows in one prompt, quality degrades and it won't fit in context. Instead run a tournament, a pipeline of pairwise-comparison agents (comparative judgment is more reliable than absolute scoring), or bucket-rank in parallel then merge. Each comparison is its own agent, so the deterministic loop holds the bracket and only the running order stays in context.

## Memory and rule adherence

If you have a particular set of rules that you find Claude misses or struggles with, even when put into the CLAUDE.mds, create a workflow with a list of rules that must be checked by verifier agents—one verifier per rule. Creating a skeptic persona subagent to review the rules to make sure they are in line will help avoid too many false positives.

The reverse direction works too: mine your recent sessions and code review comments for corrections you keep making, cluster them with parallel agents, adversarially verify each candidate (would this rule have prevented a real mistake?), and then distill the survivors back into a CLAUDE.md.

## Root-cause investigation

Debugging works best when you come up with several independent hypotheses and test them, but if you’re only using one context window, Claude can run into self-preferential bias.

A workflow can structurally prevent this by spinning up agents to generate hypotheses from disjoint evidence. For example, separate agents for logs, files, and data. Each hypothesis can then face a panel of verifiers and refuters.

This isn't just for code. Workflows can be used for sales (why did sales drop in March?), data engineering (why did this pipeline fail?), or any post-mortem exercise.

## Triaging at scale

Every team has a support queue, bug reports, or some other backlog that cannot be fully processed by humans.

A triage workflow classifies each item, dedupes against what's already tracked, and takes action. This could mean attempting the fix or escalating to a human user.

A useful pattern for triage workflows is quarantine. This involves barring the agents that read untrusted public content from taking high-privilege actions, which are instead done by the agents in charge of acting on the information.

Pair triage workflows with /loop to have Claude do this continuously.

## Exploration and taste

Workflows can be useful when exploring different approaches to a solution, especially when it is taste based, like design or naming, and would benefit from a rubric.

Try asking Claude to explore a bunch of solutions, and give a review agent  a rubric for what a good solution looks like. The task is complete when the review agent feels like it has met the criteria. Solutions can also be ordered or selected via a tournament based on the rubric.

## Evals

You can run lightweight evals for particular tasks by spinning off separate agents in a worktree and then spinning off comparison agents to compare and grade the specific outputs against a rubric. For example, evaluating and then refining a skill you’ve created against a particular criteria.

## Model and intelligence routing

Create a classifier agent tuned to your tasks that decides which model to use. This can be helpful when your task will involve many tool calls and conducting research prior to execution can identify the best model for the job.

For example, the best model for the task “explain how the auth module works” depends on how many files in the auth module there are and the shape of the codebase. A classifier agent can do this research and then route to Sonnet or Opus based on the expected complexity of the task.

## When not to use dynamic workflows

Workflows are new. While there are many use cases where it will create outsized results, they are not needed for every task and may end up using significantly more tokens.

It’s best to use workflows creatively to push Claude Code in ways that you haven’t previously. For regular coding tasks, try and ask yourself does it really need more compute? For example, most traditional coding tasks do not need a panel of 5 reviewers.

# Tips for building dynamic workflows

Prompting

Detailed prompting, using the specific techniques we described above, for dynamic workflows creates the best results.

Workflows are not just for large tasks. You can prompt the model to use a “quick workflow.” For example, you can create a quick adversarial review of an assumption.

Combine with /goal and /loop

When using workflows that can be repeated, for example triage, research, or verification, pair them with /loop to be run at regular intervals, and /goal to set a hard completion requirement.

Token usage budgets

You can set explicit token usage budgets for dynamic workflows to limit how many tokens a task uses. You can prompt it with a budget like: “use 10k tokens,” which will set the cap.

Saving and sharing dynamic workflows

You can save workflows by pressing “s” in the workflow menu. You can check these into ~/.claude/workflows or distribute them via a skill.

To share them via a skill, put your JavaScript workflow files in the skill and folder and reference them in the SKILL.MD. To allow for more flexibility, you may want to prompt Claude to think of the workflows in the skill as a template instead of a script that needs to be run verbatim.

## A whole new world

Workflows are a helpful new way to extend Claude Code. I encourage you to think of this as a starting point, there's still much to discover in how to use them best. Let us know what you find.

Thariq Shihipar and Sid Bidasaria (@sidbid) are members of technical staff at Anthropic, working on Claude Code.

title: We are in the middle of the digital renaissance, please take advantage of it
body:
There will be 3 types of people in the future.

And the divide between them is growing larger every day.

If you want to win in the next 5-10 years, it is critical that you avoid becoming number 1 or 2.

1) The Purists

“We’re the ones who stayed clean.”

The ones who rejected AI and retreated into nature, simplicity, and screen-free living.

It’s a peaceful existence, until they come across someone who uses any form of technology, then they have an uncontrollable violent reaction because it threatens their identification with this new religion.

When you look at a purist, you can’t tell if they’re being serious or if they’re just doing it because it’s the rebellious and cool thing to do.

2) The Automatons

The ones who outsource every decision.

They’re allergic to friction and addicted to optimization. If their eyes aren’t glued to a screen, they feel as if they are losing an imaginary race. Every thought they have runs through Claude.

They don’t know where AI ends and where life begins.

Most people think they have to pick a side.

But I like to be different from most people. Maybe it’s a character flaw. Maybe it sounds cringe. But I find joy in it. It’s a creative challenge to live a life that very few people live, but I’ve found that growth (and therefore meaning/fulfillment) does not come from following the herd.

I’m convinced both sides are wrong.

The Purists reject an entire portion of reality (external progress), demonize it, and assume that it can’t be healthily integrated with prioritization and effort.

There are 4 quadrants of reality.

Like a skill tree in a video game.

You put points in each as you gain experience and increase your level. They interconnect. You can try to max out your money, but if you haven’t improved your mind, body, or spirit at all... money can only go so far. The greatest fruits of life await those who accept the challenge of continuous development in all domains of life.

The Purists treat their internal world (mind and spirit) as the highest truth and reject the external world.

This is a recipe for disaster.

It does not matter how enlightened you are. If your body is frail, health is at stake, and you don’t have any money to your name - you will suffer unnecessarily, and the solution to your problems is something you consider evil, so you have no choice but to play victim.

The Automatons, on the other hand, do the complete opposite. They obsess over money and progress until their humanity is nowhere to be found.

There is a 3rd option, however.

It sounds crazy and impossible to those who can’t think for themselves, but the future belongs to those who become multi-dimensional.

Here is how you win in the next 10 years:

## The Digital Renaissance Man: Why Polymaths Win In The AI Age

> We’re in the middle of the second renaissance where proof of work replaces the resume, an audience replaces the employer, and taste replaces credentials.

The greatest tragedy of our times is that we were fooled into believing that the Mechanical Life is the only path to success.

You were told to pick a lane.

You were convinced that having multiple interests was a character flaw.

Become a designer. Become a writer. Become an engineer, a marketer, a salesman, or just get whatever high-paying job you can because that’s how you become respected and live a good life.

And that seemed reasonable, but now you feel replaceable.

Because that was never how humans were meant to live.

The modern version of a “job” is only about 250 years old.

Before it, the ideal was a free person who did many things throughout their life (compared to a slave who did one specialized task... sounds familiar). The artisan, farmer, and pirate are all examples of those who knew how to run an entire operation, not just one piece of it. They were both the thinker and the maker, the artist and the scientist, they understood that in order to live a good life, they could not be limited to one area of study.

Leonardo Da Vinci walked into Verrocchio’s workshop to learn painting and left knowing anatomy, engineering, optics, and bronze casting. Nobody told him these were separate things that were supposed to be learned as their own credential or degree.

In The Renaissance, nobody gave a shit about your niche. They gave a shit about what you were capable of.

During Industrialization, the factory model wasn’t meant to destroy education, critical thinking, individual agency, and taste, but that’s exactly what it did. It steered us away from the Renaissance ideal. Education became training instead of discovery. Employment and repetitive tasks kept us dumb to the entire entrepreneurial process, so we didn’t develop the experience or agency to do our own thing.

The unfortunate reality is that this is normal to us.

The linear career instead of the exponential.

The masses don’t question it.

And now that AI is on our doorstep, only those with an open mind (who do not identify with the “team” that fully rejects or embraces the next phase of evolution) will take advantage of this shift.

One person can now do what a 10-50 person team used to do, depending on the task. One person now has any and all known information at their fingertips. One person has access to social media (free distribution of their work).

If you are a true New Renaissance Man, this is the greatest time to be alive - and many people will try to convince you that the world is doomed.

AI can now handle the machine-like repetitive tasks that, for the past two centuries, used to be our entire way of life. People are so worried that AI will ruin our thinking and make us more like machines, when they’ve already been living like machines for the whole of their lives.

To those who join this Second Renaissance, your job is to choose your craft, leverage AI so that you can manage the entire operation, and focus on taste, direction, and judgment - because the output of AI does not have perspective. AI is simply that, artificial intelligence. Like a bag of water that you must mold.

## Become a multi-dimensional, irreplaceable, walking contradiction

The most interesting people are walking contradictions.

Jacked intellectuals. Casual billionaires. Spiritual warriors.

Life is better when you can’t be shoved into a box that others can easily make sense of.

In the future, the most interesting person will be the one who lives between two extremes. Pure creativity and pure productivity. They seamlessly balance the analog lifestyle (no screens, no urgency, pure life enjoyment) and the AI-native lifestyle (leveraging technology to do what used to be impossible).

Meaning and fulfillment are not found in a flat “balanced” lifestyle. They are found in contrast. If you were happy all the time, you wouldn’t consider it happiness. You would consider it normal. Honestly, a bit boring. You would need greater euphoria to feel what you think happiness is (hence why people can’t get off their phones today. A normal happy life is too boring for them). But when you fail, struggle, and suffer for something you care about, you learn what true happiness is on the other side.

Those who win will lean into that contrast. They work and rest deeply. Intense bursts of focus on their craft and life’s work followed by periods of complete rest - just like the world’s most successful creatives.

Charles Darwin wrote 19 books in his lifetime.

His morning routine would surprise people for that level of output:

7:00 AM - Short walk, then breakfast.

8:00 - 9:30 AM - First work session in his study. This was his most productive block.

9:30 - 10:30 AM - Break to read letters and spend time with family.

10:30 AM - Noon - Second work session. By this point, Darwin considered himself to have “done a good day’s work.”

After noon - Second walk of the day around the Sandwalk, a famous quarter-mile gravel path he built specifically for thinking and reflection.

After lunch - Read the newspaper, then rest while his wife read aloud to him.

4:00 PM - Third walk of the day, usually around the Sandwalk again, sometimes with company.

Darwin worked roughly 3 hours of focused, creative work per day across two sessions.

I believe those who will thrive in the future will have a similar routine, but with the output of 10-20 people, and be able to single-handedly build their life’s work.

They will have a One-Human Business (will break down in another letter).

> There are almost 7B people on this planet. Someday, I hope, there will be almost 7B companies. – Naval Ravikant

Before factories and industrialization, you worked until the task was done, not until your 8 hour shift was over. You worked according to the rhythm of seasons, sunlight, and energy.

More importantly, you didn’t learn how to become valuable through a standardized curriculum and meaningless memorization tests.

You learned by doing.

You learned in the workshop from apprentice to journeyman to master, imitating someone who knew what they were doing until your own taste and judgment were formed.

The question now is just that.

How do you become a New Renaissance Man?

## How to Become a Digital Renaissance Man

Do it all.

Become a writer, designer, marketer, filmmaker, bodybuilder, runner, or whatever your curiosity desires.

But channel your focus and attention into one vessel.

One craft. One thing that you choose to become known for, and your multi-faceted development will only contribute to your ability to get ahead of everyone else.

Here’s what you do.

## Choose your craft, become irreplaceable

Most artists, writers, and creatives are revolting against AI right now because they identify with their skill, tool, or specific way of working.

I don’t care about the argument of whether or not AI art is real art or AI writing is real writing because that seems like a great distraction that prevents you from doing anything with your life (outside of complaining for views and likes, reinforcing the identity that isn’t going to serve you well in the coming years).

You need a craft, but you need to choose your craft wisely.

Your craft lives at the intersection of what you care about, what you can uniquely do, and what others are willing to pay you for.

There are 3 layers to building an irreplaceable skill stack.

Layer 1 is a foundation of human nature.

Marketing, sales, writing, speaking, psychology, etc. It’s understanding the mechanics of human attention and how what people perceive as valuable is highly subjective and changes as the world does.

Every single person who wants to succeed on their own, in any form, must master this domain.

This is the “what others are willing to pay you for” part.

Layer 2 is your domain obsession and unique interests.

Philosophy, fitness, design, coding, nutrition, or anything else. None of these are going away, they are simply evolving.

The combination of these interests is where your uniqueness lies. The jacked philosopher is far more valuable than the armchair philosopher who only grows their mind without direct experience to test their theories, and it is far more interesting. People will come to you over the next guy.

This is the “what you care about” and “what you can uniquely do” part, and it is the thing that other people come to you for. The human nature foundation is what helps you make it appealing to those people.

Layer 3 is technical skill.

Email marketing software. Photoshop. No-code website design. Social media management. Typing the physical code on a screen.

This used to be the most important, because it took time and effort to learn these tools, but now AI does it all with ease. You should not bank your future on mastery of a tool.

The pattern of every technological shift is the same. The mechanical part of the skill gets automated, and the human role moves up a layer. The scribe became the editor, and the hand-weaver became the machine operator.

We’ll discuss this more in a second.

## How to become dangerously self-educated

Schools teach you how to operate within society.

Which is fine and necessary to some extent, but they do not teach you how to navigate your own path. Public schools are filtering and conditioning mechanisms more than anything.

True education is discovery.

It is the process of learning what’s necessary to achieve self-generated vision and goals, not the process of hoarding knowledge or memorizing facts to do well on a test that does not map to reality.

Even worse, most people stop learning after graduation.

They turn 20-25 and repeat the same day for the rest of their life. They do not pursue a creative challenge that demands unique knowledge.

So how do you actually learn?

You follow the apprenticeship model.

The beautiful thing about today is that you can find mentors and masters by simply picking up a book or opening YouTube on your phone.

I don’t care if you use AI to get information.

I don’t care if you get all your advice from one YouTube guru.

What I do care about is if you have a vision, have a goal, work toward that goal, and apply what you learn to problems that come up along the way. That is how you test what you learn to verify its validity for your specific situation.

Whether AI hallucinates or not, there are still plenty of profoundly stupid humans that you probably shouldn’t listen to. You need to question and test and experiment either way.

Don’t learn and then do, that’s how you get stuck in tutorial hell.

You do the thing first, or attempt to do the thing, and only then is your mind primed to receive the lesson that allows you to make forward progress.

## The one-human business (and how to join the new economy)

Creators are replacing institutions.

I know that sounds silly, but can you not see it?

Creators are the new education system - do you not learn most of the things that are actually useful in your life on Substack, YouTube, podcasts, or niche accounts on X?

Creators shape culture, culture shapes behavior - do you not trust a creator whose thoughts you’ve spent time with over politicians who obviously have their own self-interest in mind?

The internet is permissionless leverage - you don’t need approval to build an audience, start a business, or sell a product. It is the high-agency path.

AI accelerates the generalist and polymath - you can become a one-human business. Content on social media to attract an audience around your life’s work, code to build the product, funnel, and digital real estate, and domain specific knowledge that makes what you do valuable over the next person.

Now when I say creator, you probably think of an influencer or “personal brand.”

That’s not exactly what I mean.

I mean someone who creates value. They solve problems, create solutions, and help others do the same. And since value exchange is the crux of human relationships, they return the favor, often in the form of money.

James Clear has a personal brand, yes, but he is really just using newsletters, books, content, and other media to get eyes on his life’s work and earn an independent income.

I believe most ambitious individuals will take this route in the future, even if what we know as social media today isn’t where you put your work in front of other people. In the past it was newspaper and radio, now it’s social media, who knows what it will be in the future, but starting on social media puts you ahead of everyone else. That’s where the attention is.

A personal brand is just the highest leverage vessel to be a creator right now. It’s unfortunate it’s turned into a marketable “content creator” identity, but that’s the world we live in. That doesn’t mean you have to conform to what you think a content creator should be.

We will break down the one-human business in a future letter, but the next Creator Bootcamp starts September 9th. If you want to learn irreplaceable branding, unique content, and non-gimmicky social growth strategies, consider joining here.

## How to achieve the impossible with AI

Most people do not realize that AI is more than a slop generator and a new-age search engine.

They do not realize that they can quite literally ask it to build a software, landing page, funnel, app, tool, or whatever else they need to do anything on the internet.

“But Dan, that just leads to AI slop!”

Correct. And that’s where most people stop.

They don’t realize iteration exists. And that your first iteration would suck with or without AI.

The landing page starts as a rough draft, then it’s up to you to make micro adjustments until it’s actually effective.

The software is extremely buggy and looks horrible until you fix the bugs over and over again until it’s better than 99% of apps on the market.

In short, people don’t understand that they can just ask “How can I do this?” And continue asking questions until a clear plan is formed, then have the AI execute on your vision that you choose and control, not a random guess, and proceed to iterate until it is valuable.

It still takes quite a bit of time, and those who are only there for a quick dopamine hit will fizzle out.

Here is a quick start guide on how to do anything with AI:

1) Know what you want and what good looks like

For most of you, you are going to use AI to build a one-person business.

And if you don’t know how to build a business, then you’re going to expect the AI to do it perfectly for you without knowing what you need.

It still takes years of iteration to see any form of success, nothing has changed in that regard.

But if you know what you want, what you need, and what good looks like, then you can simply ask the AI how it can help you accomplish those goals and go from there.

The best place to start is by simply using AI as a learning tool.

Offer creation. Copywriting. Social media. You can’t have AI do something that you don’t even think to ask about.

2) Have absurdly high standards

The reason every response you get from AI is slop is that you treat the first draft as the final draft.

You don’t understand that you still have to tweak every little design, feature, word, sentence, or whatever else you are having AI do.

What you create with AI sucks because you see AI as this thing that should just be an absolute genius rather than seeing it as a tool that meets your level of intelligence and ambition.

3) Try to replace yourself with AI.

The best way to learn AI is to try to automate everything that you do.

You will quickly learn what can and can’t be automated.

Only then can you choose what parts of your business and craft you want AI to touch.
