緊張状態が続いているとき、体は手足の先の血流を絞り、中心に血を集めようとします。手足が冷たいまま眠れない夜があるのはこのためです。ふくらはぎや足首を動かすと血流が促され、手足の先が温まっていきます。

手足の先が温かくなることは、体が休息モードに入っていくときに見られる変化のひとつです。順番としては、⑤で体をゆるめてから①の呼吸に戻るのもおすすめです。

■ 5つ全部より、1つを毎晩

自律神経は、一度の特別なケアで大きく変わるものではありません。毎日の小さな合図の積み重ねが、数週間後の眠りや朝の状態につながっていきます。

そして大切なのは、眠れない夜に自分を責めないことです。「早く寝なきゃ」と焦ること自体が、緊張側のスイッチになります。眠れなくても、横になって呼吸をゆっくりしている時間は、体にとって無駄ではありません。

なお、眠れない状態が長く続く場合や、日中の生活に支障が出ている場合は、自己判断せず医療機関に相談することも大切です。ここで紹介した5つは、あくまで毎日のセルフケアの範囲のものです。

今夜はどれか1つ。できそうなものから試してみてください。

title: ADHDがすぐ動き出せるTips10選
body:
ADHD気質の人が困っているのは、作業の途中ではなく「最初の数秒」です。取りかかってしまえば人並み以上に没頭できるのに、その入り口だけが異様に重い。

僕自身ずっとそうで、今も油断すると午前中が丸ごと消えます。だから今回は、根性論ではなく「入り口を軽くする」ためだけの小技を10個まとめました。どれも僕が実際に使っているものです。

１つ目は「５秒数えて体を先に使う」。やろうと思った瞬間に５・４・３・２・１と数え、１でパソコンを開くなり立ち上がるなりする。考える時間を脳に与えないのがコツで、迷った瞬間に「その前にコーヒーでも」という脳内会議が始まり、だいたい負けます。

２つ目は「スマホは電源を落として別の部屋へ」。机に伏せておく程度では足りません。あると知っているだけで注意の一部が持っていかれるので、物理的に手が届かない場所まで遠ざけるのが正解です。

３つ目は「最初の１手目だけを決めておく」。ToDoが20個並ぶと、どれから手をつければいいか分からなくなって固まります。「今日はまずファイルを開く」「まず名前を書く」くらいまで小さくしておくと、選ぶ負担が消えます。

４つ目は「前日、あえて途中で止めておく」。文章なら文の途中、資料なら見出しだけ書いたところで切り上げる。翌朝ゼロから始めるより、途中のものを続ける方が圧倒的に楽で、僕はこれで朝の立ち上がりがかなり変わりました。

５つ目は「座らずに始める」。椅子に深く腰かけてから「さて」と思うと、そこで一呼吸置いてしまってスマホを触ります。立ったままパソコンを開き、１文だけ打ってから座る。妙なことに、これだけで始まります。

６つ目は「すでにある習慣の後ろにくっつける」。歯を磨いたら机に座る、コーヒーを淹れたらノートを開く、というように、もう体が勝手にやっている行動の直後に作業を連結させる。新しい習慣をゼロから作るより、既存の流れに便乗する方がADHD脳には向いています。

７つ目は「終わる時刻を先に決める」。「11時までやる」ではなく「11時になったらやめる」と決める。終わりが見えていると入り口の重さが軽くなるし、時間感覚が薄い僕らには「区切り」そのものが助けになります。

８つ目は「最悪やめていいと自分に許可する」。「５分やってダメなら閉じていい」と決めてから始めると、不思議と安心して手をつけられて、結局５分で終わることはほとんどありません。

９つ目は「一番ダサいレベルでやる」。きれいに書こう、ちゃんとやろうと思った時点で足が止まります。誤字だらけでいい、下書き以下でいい、と質を地面まで下げる。質はあとから追いつきます。

10個目は「今日はやる気がないと声に出して認める」。認めたうえで「じゃあ資料を読むだけ」「前日の原稿を読み返すだけ」と、やる気がないなりの作業をあらかじめ用意しておく。ゼロの日を減らすと、自分を責める時間も減ります。

全部やる必要はありません。

それでも「気合いで頑張る」より、こういう小技をいくつかストックしておく方が、１日の生産量がまるで違ってきます。

title: how to ACTUALLY get a j*b (no bs)
body:
most people who are really good engineers dont realize that being good =! getting hired. as some guy said, "a focused fool will accomplish more than a distracted genius". you can literally be good at what you do and still get ignored if your application looks exaclty like other 500 people applying for the same job. In big 26 being skilled is still the baseline but knowing how to make people notice that matters just as much. 
“applying for jobs is a skill by itself”


## Pre requisites :

even before i expain how to get a job, i want to share few pre req which ive learnt over time from people who i look upto in tech 

- do engineering for the love of the game, not because your parents told you to, or because you had nothing else to choose

- be good at some domain fundamentally : ai, backend whatever

- have a very good proof of work: resume, portfolio, projects etc

# The Game : 

there are a lot of ways of getting hired, but these are the things i've either personally used, or seen people waste way too much time in 2026

## 1. Corporate Stalking : 

this is probably the most effective thing ive personally done while applying for jobs. 

i used to keep a notion page where i tracked companies i wanted to work for, what they are building, whether they were hiring, what roles were open, whether they mentioned a stipend, application links, emails, and even why i got rejected(if i applied) 

every morning and night, id spend 15 mins checking hiring sites. for each company, i used to compare JD with my resume and find skill gaps and tried to close them

i once applied for an AI health tech startup three times, i got rejected twice, the third time i built a small POC related to one of their products and applied, that literally got me to the interview. i cleared three rounds but lost in the final one, but you get the point 

pick a list of companies that you want to work and stalk the hell out of them

## 2. Cold Mailing :

cold mailing STILL works

i used to find startups on hiring platforms, check what they were building and reach out direclty instead of waiting for the application. 

ive sent a multiple cold mails and got a decent amount of callbacks, the important part is not to send the same generic mai to all of them, make it relevant to their product and give them a reason to reply

you can even cold mail companies you;ve already applied to, sometimes it makes you stand out from everyone 

- soham parek's cold mail template : 
https://x.com/lochan_twt/status/2016366372784369843?s=20

## 3. Application maxxing : 

this is the most desperate and ineffective way of applying jobs

they apply to literally every random job they see on any website, that too with the same resume, even though the role barely matches what they know, and they blame the market for not getting callbacks 

when it comes to job applications quality of application matters way more than no.of applicaions. ten well-targeted applications can be worth more than 200 random drunk applications

## 4. Referrals : 

i've actually never tried getting a job through referrals, ive had chances to ask,  but personally i never liked referrals 

but referrals clearly work for a lot of people

the only thing is if someone is putting their name behind you, be good enough to not make them regret it 

- only take referrals if you are confident enough
https://x.com/kmeanskaran/status/2067575219242574214?s=20

## 5. Showcase in public :

this is the coolest way of getting hired 

post whatever you’re building, whatever you’re learning, projects, experiments, mistakes anything that shows what you can do

ive seen a lot of unexpected oppurtunites come just from people consistently sharing their work online, you dont need to become an influencer just make your work visible 

- creating applications like these :
https://x.com/VinnyMadaan3/status/2055656744123293929?s=20

# The Forbidden Technique : 

the most effective ones for me are still stalking and cold mailing, but you can literally combine everything 

stalk the company, understand what they are building, cold mail them, try getting a referral keep fixing gaps all while posting your work online 

## Tips : 

these are few things ive picked up from people i lookup to in tech

- the market is disrupted but there are still jobs 

- only foucs on what you can control like skills, projects, applications and keep working and stop being too much desperate about jobs

- if you apply exaclty like everyone else, you'll obv get results like everyone else

- own the fu*king application

at the end of the day, being good is just half of the game, getting noticed by right people is the other half

you dont need to become some insane networking machine or spam 500 applications everyday, just stop treating job applications like lottery tickets

applying jobs is a skill, Get good at that too.

there are definitely more ways to get hired which i didnt mention here, you can experiment it and find what works for you

title: The Principles of Getting Ahead.
body:
Two people can start from almost the same place. Same age. Similar intelligence. Same 24 hours in a day. Five years later, their lives can look completely different. 1

1. One has built valuable skills, a strong network, a reputation, and opportunities that seem to appear out of nowhere.

2. The other has worked just as hard, but somehow hasn't moved nearly as far. Five years passed, but very little actually changed.

It's easy to explain the difference with luck, talent, or discipline. But that's only part of the story. Some actions simply move you further than others.

One conversation can introduce you to your future business partner. One skill can completely change what you're able to earn. One article can put your work in front of a million people. One small project can turn into a company.

None of these outcomes are guaranteed.

But they all have something in common. The potential upside is much bigger than the effort required to try.

That's one of the biggest differences between people who move ahead quickly and those who stay in roughly the same place.

They don't just work hard. They get better at recognizing where their time, skills, relationships, and effort can create disproportionate returns. 

And once you understand that, getting ahead becomes less about doing more and more about doing the right things.

That's what this article is about.

# I. Seek Asymmetric Opportunities

Not all opportunities are created equal. Some have a very predictable exchange: 

- Work one hour, get paid for one hour. 

- Do twice the work, get roughly twice the result.

Others work completely differently. 

1. You can spend five hours writing an article and get 500 views. 

2. Or the same five hours can produce an article that reaches a million people, brings thousands of followers, and puts your work in front of someone who later becomes a client.

The effort barely changed. The range of possible outcomes did. 

This is asymmetry. Situations where what you can gain is disproportionately larger than what you have to risk.

Venture capital works on a similar principle. An investor can lose at most the money invested in a startup, but a rare winner can return many times that amount. That's why a portfolio doesn't require every company to succeed. A small number of exceptional outcomes can offset many failures.

Your career has asymmetric opportunities too.

- Publishing your work. 

- Starting a small business. 

- Learning an emerging skill early. 

- Reaching out to someone far ahead of you. 

- Moving into a growing industry. 

- Building something on the side.

Most attempts won't change your life. But importantly, they don't have to.

If ten experiments cost you a few weekends and nine go nowhere, the tenth can still make the entire equation worth it. That's the advantage of playing games where being wrong is cheap, but being right can change your trajectory. Compare that with spending years optimizing something with a tightly capped upside. You can execute perfectly and still only move so far. 

You don't need extraordinary results from everything you do. You need enough exposure to things capable of producing extraordinary results.

# II. Build Leverage

For most of human history, there was a fairly tight relationship between how much you worked and how much you could produce.

- A farmer could only work so much land. 

- A craftsman could only make so many products. 

- A teacher could only teach the people who fit in a room.

The internet changed that.

Today, the same hour of work can produce radically different amounts of value depending on what you build with it.

- A developer can write software once and have a million people use it.

- A creator can make one video and reach more people than a television network could reach decades ago.

- An author can write a book once and sell it for decades.

- A founder can build a system that continues operating while they're asleep.

This is leverage. Using something beyond your own time to multiply the output of your effort.

Code is leverage. Content is leverage. Capital is leverage. Products, systems, distribution, and teams can all be leverage. Without leverage, your output is limited by your time. Stop working, and the output stops too.

With leverage, the relationship starts to break.

One hour can create ten hours of value. One decision can affect thousands of customers. One piece of work can continue producing results years after you made it.

This is why two people can work equally hard and get completely different results. One keeps selling their hours. The other spends some of those hours building things that multiply them.

# III. Get Closer to Opportunity

Opportunity isn't evenly distributed.

Some cities produce more startups. Some companies produce more founders. Some communities produce more collaborations, investments, ideas, and careers. Silicon Valley is an obvious example.

For decades, ambitious founders moved there even though companies could technically be built elsewhere. The value wasn't only the location itself. It was the concentration of engineers, investors, founders, talent, knowledge, and capital.

Put enough ambitious people in the same environment and opportunities begin colliding.

One conversation becomes an introduction. An introduction becomes a job. A side project becomes a startup. Someone else's idea changes what you decide to build.

The same thing happens on a much smaller scale.

Spend your time around twenty people building companies, and you'll constantly hear about new tools, industries, jobs, customers, and problems worth solving.

Spend it around twenty people who aren't interested in any of those things, and many of the same opportunities may never even enter your field of view.

The internet has made proximity less geographic than it used to be. A niche X community, group chat, Discord, startup, or online network can put you around people you would have had almost no chance of meeting twenty years ago.

And this creates an important advantage. You can't act on an opportunity you never encounter.

Getting ahead therefore isn't only about becoming more capable. It's also about putting yourself in environments where useful information, ambitious people, and unexpected opportunities pass through more often.

Sometimes changing your trajectory doesn't require working harder. It requires getting closer to where things are happening.

# IV. Become Easy to Bet On

A surprising number of opportunities come from someone deciding to take a chance on you.

- A founder hires you. 

- A client gives you a bigger project. 

- An investor writes a check. Someone recommends you to a friend. A person you've met twice introduces you to someone important.

In every case, they're making a small bet. And when people make bets, they look for evidence. Imagine two developers with roughly the same level of skill.

1. One has spent years quietly getting better. 

2. The other built 3 products, contributed to open-source projects, written about what they've learned, and has people willing to recommend them.

They might be equally capable. But they're not equally easy to bet on. The second person has reduced uncertainty.

You can see what they've built. You can see how they think. You can see that they finish things. Other people can verify that they're good. This is one reason reputation becomes so valuable over time. 

Every successful project, recommendation, useful piece of work, and promise you keep becomes another piece of evidence about what someone can expect from you.

Eventually, people don't have to take as much of a risk. Your previous work starts making the case for you. 

That's also why quietly becoming good at something isn't always enough. The world can't reward skills it doesn't know you have.

1. Build things. 

2. Publish your work. 

3. Keep your promises. 

4. Help people. 

5. Develop a track record that makes the next person feel comfortable putting their name, money, or opportunity behind you.

Being good creates value. Making it easy for others to see that you're good creates opportunity.

# V. Play Games That Compound

Some games make you start from zero every morning. You do the work, get the result, and tomorrow you have to do roughly the same thing again.

Other games are different.

Yesterday's work makes today's work more valuable. An audience works this way. Your first article starts with nobody reading. Years later, you can publish the same quality of article to hundreds of thousands of people.

Knowledge works this way too. The more you understand, the easier it becomes to connect and understand new ideas.

- Relationships compound. 

- Reputation compounds. 

- Capital compounds. 

- Skills compound.

The interesting part is that compounding doesn't only increase what you have. It changes how easily you can get more of it.

- A strong reputation makes the next introduction easier. 

- A larger audience makes the next piece of content easier to distribute. 

- More knowledge makes the next skill easier to learn. More capital creates more opportunities to invest.

The advantage begins feeding itself.

This is why two people making similar amounts of effort can slowly move further and further apart. One person's work disappears when it's finished. The other's becomes an asset that makes future work more effective.

At first, the difference can look tiny. Over enough time, it becomes difficult to catch. The best games get easier to win the longer you play them.

# VI. Combine Skills Instead of Competing

You probably won't become the best writer in the world. You probably won't become the best marketer, salesperson, designer, or programmer either.

Fortunately, you don't need to.

Scott Adams popularized the idea of a talent stack. 

Instead of becoming world-class at one thing, you can become good at several useful things whose combination is unusually valuable.

Imagine you're in the top 10% at writing. That's useful, but there are plenty of great writers.

1. Now add marketing.

2. Then sales.

3. Then an understanding of AI.

4. Then the ability to build an audience and distribute your ideas.

Individually, none of those skills makes you particularly rare. But finding someone who can do all five becomes much harder.

The combination becomes the advantage. This is especially powerful because skills can multiply each other rather than simply add together.

A developer who understands sales can build things people actually want. A founder who can write can attract customers, employees, and investors. A designer who understands psychology can make products easier to understand and use.

Each additional skill changes what you can do with the ones you already have. And this creates another way to get ahead.

Instead of entering the most competitive game and trying to become number one, you can create a combination where there are far fewer people to compete with.

You don't always need to become the best. Sometimes you need to become difficult to compare.

# VII. Increase Your Surface Area for Luck

Luck is random. But your exposure to luck isn't. 

Every time you publish something, meet someone new, build a project, enter a new community, or try an experiment, you create another opportunity for something unexpected to happen. Most of these attempts will lead nowhere.

But that's the point. You don't need all of them to work. You need enough exposure for a few unusually valuable opportunities to eventually find you.

From the outside, those moments often look like luck. What you don't see are all the actions that increased the probability of that luck happening.

I've written an entire article about How to Increase Your Luck., so I won't go too deep into it here.

The principle is simple:

You can't manufacture luck on command. But you can give luck more chances to find you.

# Now here's what I actually want you to take away from all of this.

Getting ahead isn't about working harder than everyone around you. It's about putting your effort in places where it can create disproportionate returns. You don't need every decision to change your life.

You just need a few that change your trajectory. ❤️

title: Improve your cognitive skills.
body:
## what’s the point of having money if you’re going to be so burned out that you won’t even be able to enjoy it?

There’s something I think we’ve all noticed about this world: when you spend so many hours intensely focused, whether it’s on crypto or perhaps on some business venture outside of it, you start to feel kind of “dizzy.” As time goes by, you begin to notice the effects: your memory starts failing you, maybe socializing becomes harder, and so on.

And I understand it. But the problem isn’t what you do. It’s your habits.

We can all agree that the narrative or simply the way this world works pushes you, to some extent, toward a disorganized lifestyle.

A friend might message you at 4 AM saying there could be a play. Maybe you have a call with someone from another country at some random hour. Maybe several problems come up at once and you have to spend hours and hours solving them, or whatever else it may be.

But that’s not an excuse for making destroying your brain the norm in your life.

Throughout this article, I’d like to go over a few things that can help improve your cognitive abilities and are perfectly compatible with this lifestyle.

## Be as Consistent as Possible With Your Sleep.

Don’t underestimate how important it is to sleep well. Try to keep relatively consistent times for going to bed and waking up, even on weekends. You don’t have to be perfect, but there should be some level of consistency.

Sleep shouldn’t be the first thing you sacrifice when you have things to do. If you constantly sleep less so you can work more, study more, or stay on your phone, sooner or later you’ll pay the price in concentration, energy, memory, and discipline.

Try to create a routine before going to bed as well: put your phone away, avoid unnecessary stimulation, and give your mind some time to slow down and wind down. Reading would be an excellent option, which I’ll explain in more detail later.

You don’t need to turn sleep into another obsession or become one of those people who track their sleep in detail. Just understand that sleep is not wasted time.

Sleeping well is an investment in all the hours that come afterward.

Get your sleep in order, and you’ll notice that many other things in your life start falling into place as well.

## Learn Languages.

People who speak two languages tend to have brains that are estimated to be six years “younger” than would be expected for their age; those who speak three languages, seven years younger; and those who speak four languages, thirteen years younger.

The protective effect of multilingualism appears to be dose-dependent: the more languages a person speaks, the greater the potential benefits. This effect has been linked to several factors, including greater overall cognitive stimulation, increased brain plasticity from learning different linguistic structures, and the social and cultural factors associated with using multiple languages.

One of the main mechanisms behind this may be that when a person knows several languages, they all remain active in the brain at the same time, even when only one is being used. The brain has to keep them “switched on” while continuously inhibiting them to prevent them from getting mixed up.

That constant control creates an additional cognitive load which, when sustained over many years, has been associated with a stronger cognitive reserve.

Long-term use of multiple languages may strengthen the brain networks involved in executive control, attention, and memory through continuous cognitive challenge. Interestingly, these same networks are among those most vulnerable to age-related decline, mild cognitive impairment, and dementia, which makes multilingualism a potential protective factor for brain health throughout life.

Studying a language doesn’t take that much time, and it fits perfectly into the life of an investor. It doesn’t just provide cognitive benefits; it also allows you to connect with people who speak that language in this incredibly interconnected world.

Learning your first foreign language can be a little tedious at first, but eventually you unlock a kind of boost, and everything you learn after that tends to come much faster.  Top 5 Most Spoken Languages (If you don’t know which one to choose, pick one of these).

> English — ~1.5 billion speakers

> Mandarin Chinese — ~1.1 billion speakers

> Hindi — ~610 million speakers

> Spanish — ~560 million speakers

> French — ~320 million speakers

## The power of reading.

Reading is extremely beneficial for us. It doesn’t really matter what you read. Just read!

Don’t wait until you find the perfect book. Just try to read something.

To be more specific, if you’re not used to reading, it might be a good idea to start with anything related to topics you’re genuinely passionate about. That way, you can build the habit in a more enjoyable way.

A good time to do it is after dinner, since it also helps you slow down before going to bed.

It doesn’t have to take a lot of time. Even 30 minutes a couple of times a week can make a difference. And if you combine it with a book about something you’re currently studying, you’re essentially killing two birds with one stone.

Benefits of Reading

> Improves concentration: Reading requires you to maintain your attention for extended periods, which is especially valuable in an era of constant stimulation.

> Improves reasoning: Following arguments, connecting concepts, and evaluating what you’re reading exercises critical thinking.

> Expands your vocabulary: Repeated exposure to new words improves your ability to understand and express ideas.

> Stimulates imagination: Especially with fiction, your brain has to mentally construct scenarios, characters, and situations.

> Improves memory: Remembering characters, concepts, arguments, and connections between chapters actively engages your memory.

JUST READ!

## Creatine.

Although creatine is strongly associated with the gym and fitness world, it is also one of the most extensively studied and well-researched supplements, with a strong safety profile, and there is substantial evidence supporting its potential cognitive benefits.

Whether you train or not, take the right amount per day may be beneficial for your brain.

> Improves sleep-related cognitive performance: Recent clinical studies suggest that creatine can help mitigate some of the decline in mental performance caused by insufficient sleep. In people experiencing severe sleep deprivation, creatine supplementation has been shown to help maintain processing speed, decision-making, and reaction time.

> Reduces mental fatigue: When you’re faced with tasks that require intense and prolonged mathematical, logical, or attentional effort, the brain’s energy demands increase. Consistent supplementation may help reduce that feeling of having a “burned-out brain” or mental fog, potentially supporting clearer thinking.

Before finishing the article, I wanted to highlight a few things:

> Traveling helps you think more clearly and realistically, while also giving you the chance to practice the local languages.

> Studying: Studying in 2026 is easier than ever. You can do it from an app or an online academy without leaving your home or even your room. In the past, you mostly had books and expensive in-person academies.

> The opportunities and doors that open up when you can have a fluent conversation with people from other countries who share the same interests as you, or who are even in a better position, allowing you to learn from that connection.

> Training: You don’t need to be obsessive about it. A couple of times a week is enough to keep you focused.

> Moments of disconnecting: Recognize when you’re doing something to disconnect and when you’re doing something to escape from your problems. Be honest with yourself. If you go fishing with friends to disconnect, that’s perfectly fine. But if you go fishing because you don’t want to face your problems, you should seriously reconsider a few things.

If you have a friend you can help with this, share it.

title: 存款不到 100 万的年轻人，请直接照做这张生存清单
authorName: 在香港的宁夏三娃老父亲阿星
body:
前几天刷到一张 X 状态，标题很扎眼："存款不到100万请直接照做"。

我盯着那29条清单一条一条往下看，越看越觉得熟悉，这不就是我这几年折腾香港公司、开海外账户、跑通AI出海的路线图吗？

从注册美区ID到开盈透证券，从学Claude到做自己的小产品，每一条我几乎都踩过坑、花过冤枉钱、也拿到了结果。

但光有清单不够。

清单告诉你"做什么"，没告诉你"为什么做"和"按什么顺序做"。

今天我把这张清单拆开，配上我自己踩过的坑，给你一个能直接上手的执行策略。

## 一、先搞清楚：你到底在为什么焦虑

我以前总觉得，焦虑是因为钱不够多。

直到我见过月薪五万还在焦虑的人，也见过收入不高但睡得特别香的人。

后来才明白，焦虑的根源不是钱少，而是收入来源单一、抗风险能力为零、对未来没有掌控感。

你每个月的工资到账，扣完房贷车贷生活费，剩下的全靠公司明年还愿不愿意给你发。

公司裁员、行业下行、身体健康出问题，任何一个变量出问题，整个系统就崩了。

这不是你不够努力，这是结构上的脆弱。

真正的安全感，不是银行卡里的数字，而是你有多少条腿在走路。

所以这张清单的底层逻辑，不是教你怎么暴富，而是教你怎么从"单腿站立"变成"多腿走路"，从单一工资收入，变成工资+投资+个人品牌+产品收入的多元结构。

## 二、第一阶段：工具基建，30天搞定

很多人一上来就想做个人IP、想做产品、想赚美元。

别着急，先把基础设施搭好。

就像盖房子，你得先通水通电通路，才能开始砌砖。

这些工具看起来都是小事，但每一件都在拓宽你人生的边界，你能接触到的信息、你能调动的资源、你能参与的游戏，都不一样了。

必做清单（按优先级排）：

1. 设备：苹果手机非国行版本 + MacBook。

不是崇洋媚外，是整个跨境生态对苹果最友好，美区ID、海外支付、AI工具，苹果生态是最顺的一条路。

2. 账号：注册美区ID和香港ID，下载X（原Twitter）。

不是让你刷八卦，是让你直接看一手信息，AI圈的最新动态、海外创业者的讨论、英文世界的真实讨论，都在X上。

3. 通讯：一张香港手机卡和美国 esim 手机号。

这是你进入全球金融系统的钥匙，很多海外银行、券商的验证，内地手机号根本收不到。

4. 银行：香港众安银行卡

https://l.za.group/qV99a  或

starryblu 新加坡借记卡

https://sg.starryblu.com/x/NSFHxKQj

+ 汇丰或者渣打银行卡「50 万达标全球理财」+ 美国 Amex 信用卡。

有了香港账户，你才能自由兑换港币和美元，才能买全球的股票和基金。

5. 券商：盈透或者致富，嘉信等证券账户。

这是个人投资者能开到的、全球投资品类最全的券商账户，美股、港股、ETF、期权，一个账户全搞定。

6. AI工具：Claude、ChatGPT、Gemini、DeepSeek，至少深度用熟一个。

不是让你聊天玩，是让它帮你写代码、做表格、写文案、查资料，把它当成你的24小时助理。

这一阶段的核心是：先拥有入场资格。

很多人一辈子都在岸上看，从来没下过水。你花30天把这些搞定，就已经超过90%的人了。

## 三、第二阶段：能力建设，90天见效

工具有了，接下来练本事。

这一阶段的目标只有一个：让你一个人就能干以前一个团队的活。

AI时代最大的红利，就是个人能力被指数级放大，一个会用工具的人，顶得上以前十个人。

具体做什么：

1. AI深度使用：学会用AI写作、做表格、做PPT、写代码和做视频。

不是"知道有这个功能"，是真的能用它产出工作成果。

拿Codex写一个简单的工具出来，哪怕只是一个自动处理Excel的小脚本，比如像我写一本书去 kindle 卖。

或者在线免费阅读的小说：

https://ai.xingjia.xyz/company

2. 编程入门：学会用GitHub，能看懂优秀项目。不用你成为算法工程师，但你得能看懂别人在做什么、能抄作业、能改一改自己用。

3. 英语捡起来：每天花1小时，坚持用英文搜索和阅读。不用背单词，就直接搜你感兴趣的东西，AI工具怎么用、海外怎么创业、美股怎么投。用着用着就会了。

4. 知识库搭建：用Notion或Obsidian，最容易的就是付费的得到笔记 App  建一个自己的知识库。你看过的文章、踩过的坑、学到的经验，都分门别类存进去。这是你以后个人品牌和产品的原材料仓库。

5. 信息源升级：每周读一份行业报告，把刷短视频的时间换成YouTube上的干货视频。一手信息和二手信息的差距，比你想象的大得多。

这一阶段的核心是：用工具放大你的产出能力。

以前你一天只能干一件事，现在能干十件。

效率提升10倍，你的收入天花板自然就抬高了。

## 四、第三阶段：

## 资产与现金流，长期主义

能力有了，接下来是最关键的一步，把能力变成资产，把劳动收入变成现金流。

这是大多数人一辈子都没跨过去的坎。

他们一直用时间换钱，从来没想过怎么让钱替自己干活、怎么让产品替自己干活。

具体路径：

1. 指数基金定投：持续买入标普500和纳斯达克100。这是普通人能拿到的、风险收益比最好的投资品，没有之一。不用选股、不用择时，每个月工资到账先买一笔，买了就忘掉。

2. 多元货币配置：建立美元资产意识，不要只了解人民币资产。港币、美元、人民币，至少持有三种货币的资产，对冲单一货币的风险。

3. 个人IP起步：运营一个X账号和一个国内自媒体账号，每天输出一篇内容，不管有没有人看，坚持一年。

这不是为了当网红，是为了建立你的个人供给，让别人知道你是谁、你能做什么、愿意为你付钱。

4. 做一个自己的小产品：小网站、小工具、小课程都行。产品是睡后收入的载体——你做一次，它能卖无数次。不用追求完美，先做出来再说。

比如星佳的付费产品

https://books.xingjia.xyz

5. 攒第一桶金：每个月存下收入的30%，学会记账，知道每一分钱花去了哪里。第一桶金不是用来花的，是用来生钱的本金。

这一阶段的核心是：从"出卖时间"转向"拥有资产"。

资产的特点是，你睡觉的时候它还在帮你赚钱。当你的资产性收入超过工资收入的那一天，你就真正自由了。

## 五、最后说几句掏心窝子的

我把这张清单和网友总结的"八荣八耻"放在一起看，发现说的其实是同一件事：

以指数纪律为荣，以奢侈品撑场面为耻；

以跨境通行能力为荣，以一代人积蓄换学区信号为耻；

以个人供给可定价为荣，以职位代替能力为耻；

以多元货币收入为荣，以单一工资裸奔为耻；

以掌握源头信息为荣，以二手观点代替求证为耻；

以深度输入代替空转刷屏为荣，以拒绝新工具重复低效为耻；

以工具放大产出为荣，以负债满足虚荣为耻；

以现金流、睡眠和可支配时间为荣，以透支身体换钱为耻。

所有扰乱你情绪、消耗你、拖慢你的人和环境，都要斩立决。每天看一遍，绝对不能扰乱圣心。

这不是鸡汤，这是一个普通人在这个时代能拿到的最实在的生存策略。

你不需要全部做到，从第一阶段的30天基建开始就行。

买个美区ID、开个香港账户、装个Claude 或者 ChatGPT

这三件事，做完你会发现，世界好像比以前大了一圈。

如果你也在走这条路，或者准备开始走，评论区留个脚印，路上的人多了，就不孤单了。

title: 手把手教你用 Opus 5.5 / Astra + Tripo 制作 3D 游戏
body:
本周，我用 Opus 5.5 + Tripo + Blender，把《小王子》中的星际旅行做成了一款可以亲自探索的 3D 游戏。发布后，全网累计收获近 300w 浏览。

很多朋友都非常喜欢这个游戏。而从场景搭建、人物制作，到代码开发和调试，背后的主要制作工作，都交给了 AI 完成。

于是，我决定把这次的制作流程公开出来，结合实际案例和可参考的提示词，手把手带大家入门 AI 3D 游戏制作，让你也能开始搭建自己想象中的世界。

本篇文章主要分为三个部分：

1、游戏开发流程和制作准备

2、场景构建

3、角色构建

## 1、游戏开发流程和制作准备   

游戏开发流程：  Fable 5.1 负责 PRD 的制作，梳理游戏核心场景、人物以及剧情故事线  + Image 2.5 生成场景和人物图片 + Tripo 生成核心 3D 资产 + Opus 5.5 搭建核心代码 +  Astra 迭代优化以及 bug 修复  

游戏工具配置：   

- Blender: 下载Blender CLI，用于优化tripo生成的3D模型并完成游戏整体的3D建模；安装付费Auto-Rig pro插件，用于人物的绑骨蒙皮，方便动作交互制作  

- Unity：安装Unity App（https://unity.com/），作为游戏引擎将场景、人物、交互动效打包成完整游戏；安装 Unity CLI，并在项目中装 Pipeline 包，让 Claude 通过官方 Unity MCP 直接操作 Unity 项目  

接下来，这篇文章将着重讲解场景构建和人物制作。

## 2、场景构建  

简单来说：Image 2.5 生成场景图 — 拆解 3D 资产并在 Tripo 中生成 — Opus 5.5 操作 Blender+Unity 进行场景建模 

详细步骤如下👇：

  (1) 使用 GPT Image 2.5 生成场景参考图，把想法变成明确的画面

根据前面整理的游戏需求，使用 Image 2.5 生成场景参考图，确定整体画风、配色，以及主要物体的位置。

建议先确定一张满意的场景效果图，再围绕它补充其他角度（特别是对于有室内和室外的场景）。其中，俯视图主要用来说明场景布局，斜侧视图用来补充物体的高度、造型和层次关系，当然也可以直接生成一张如下的整体视图：

可复用参考提示词：

> 基于上传的场景参考图，帮我生成一张该场景的全面貌参考图片，包括整体环境的多视角视图以及局部细节的展示。

(2) 让 AI 拆解场景资产，筛选出需要在 Tripo 中单独生成的模型  

有了参考图之后，可以直接使用 AI 判断场景中哪些资产需要在 Tripo 中单独生成，哪些可以交给 Opus 5.5 在 Blender/Unity 中搭建。

参考提示词

> 我现在要进行游戏开发，我的技术栈是 Tripo + Blender + Unity。你根据我们上述生成的场景参考图，帮我去深入分析哪些资产适合用Tripo 生成，而哪些资产适合用 Blender 直接进行搭建。
将需要Tripo生成的资产在图片中标注出来，方便我来确认。

而对于Tripo里场景道具3D资产的制作，建议使用H3.1模型，其能保证资产的高精度细节。

(3) 通过专业的提示词让 Opus 5.5 操控 Blender、Unity 开始建模，建模的关键是给予详细的参考图以及多机位的进行迭代

在 Tripo 中生成并导出需要单独制作的 3D 道具后，将这些资产和第一步的场景参考图交给 Opus 5.5，让它操控 Blender + Unity 搭建整体环境，并按参考图摆放道具、调整比例和位置。

完成后，从正面、侧面等不同角度检查场景，结合截图反馈逐步调整布局与细节。

参考提示词如下：

> 根据上传的场景内外景多视角参考图以及生成好的Tripo 3D资产，你来对照参考图进行完美级的复刻。要求实现和参考图一样的惊艳质感和细节还原。
在实现完成后，派一个独立的审查 agent进行进行多机位的场景盲审。如果发现有和参考图差异的地方，就不断地进行迭代完善。

## 3、人物建模  

Image 2.5生成人物图 — Tripo 中生成人物 3D 模型 — Blender的Auto-Rig pro插件进行绑骨蒙皮 — mixamo 动作接入 — 复杂交互在blender里进行二次调整（可选）

这里我们以小王子的设计为例来做具体讲解 

 (1) 使用Image 2.5生成人物的多视角参考图

根据人物形象和设定，首先使用Image 2.5生成小王子的 T-pose 四视图，并确保各视角的人物细节统一。

(2) 使用 Tripo 的 Smart Mesh P2.0 模型生成 3D 人物资产

Smart Mesh P2.0 是一个专门面向游戏和交互内容的 3D 生成模型，其特点是能生成面数可控、便于编辑的人物结构，方便后期的绑骨和动画制作

我们在Tripo当中选择「多视图生成3D」并依次上传四视图，拓扑默认四边形，精度可拉到最高，选择P2.0模型并开始生成

之后若发现初步生成的白模网格整齐无误，就可以点击「Texture（纹理）」生成模型贴图；若网格形状不合理，则可以选择「edit mesh」进行局部再生成

(3) 在Blender里利用Auto-Rig pro插件对人物进行自动绑骨和蒙皮

配置好该插件后，直接在Claude上传人物模型，并输入下面这个经过我反复调试总结出的提示词进行高效绑骨与蒙皮👇：

> 使用 Auto-Rig Pro 为人物完成绑骨和蒙皮，确保骨骼位置与人物关节对齐。完成后测试抬手、弯腿、转身等基础动作，检查并修正明显的变形、拉扯和穿模问题。

(4) 去mixamo下载人物需要的动作文件，并让Opus 5.5适配到对应的人物骨骼

根据游戏设定，去mixamo（https://www.mixamo.com/）按照关键词搜索小王子需要的动作，并下载对应的FBX动作文件

之后我们便可以让Opus检查相关动作是否匹配小王子的真实骨骼，并完成接入

(5) 在Blender中调整特殊动作与接触细节（复杂交互动作需要）

对于「小王子提水壶」这类涉及人物与道具接触的复杂交互，往往mixamo并没有完美适配的动作。我们可以先选一个接近的基础动作，再让Opus 5.5在blender里反复进行细节的迭代调整

提示词参考如下：

> 请参考提供的 Mixamo 动作，保留其中适用的部分，并使用 Auto-Rig Pro 的手臂 IK 控制器调整手臂姿势，配合手指握持和水壶位置的细节修正，补全提水壶动作。确保手掌与把手接触稳定、提起过程自然，避免穿模、握持脱离或水壶悬空。

下周我将在GitHub中开源游戏的全部代码以及更加完整的制作细节，欢迎大家持续关注！

ps. 大家如果也想要尝试用Tripo进行自己的3D创作，可以走我的链接注册，可以免费获得500 credits：
https://studio.tripo3d.ai/home?invite_code=H2DB1X&utm_source=X&utm_medium=kol&utm_campaign=kol_Saccc

title: Jev Engineering: Full 10-Step Roadmap to Set Up and Use a New Brain for AI (from scratch)
body:
The Jevons Paradox (he's on picture) is a rule stating that an increase in the efficiency of a resource's use does not reduce, but rather increases, its overall consumption

- That's the global problem for AI: LLMs and Agents 

And Jev by @typesafeai is built to save 101% of your money, time and will improve your efficiency of using AI

So trust me - this is the 2030 setup that you need to install right now
before the alpha -  subscribe to my substack for more fresh alpha - https://substack.com/@0xcodila

"Browser Use put Jev inside an agent that found flights in 7 seconds for $0.0039"

That gets interesting when you look at what your Chief of Staff does all day: choose a worker, check a result, decide whether to continue. Each fork can become another model call before any useful work happens

> Jev gives those decisions their own model

 Your writing agent keeps writing. Your research agent keeps researching. The small judgments between them become a separate component you can inspect, price, and change.

Start with a standalone task router: enter a job, let Jev choose its destination, and save the handoff on your computer. 
Then run Browser Use's complete browser agent. (The first needs one API key; the browser project needs two)

## 01. Find the part of your agent Jev can take over

Jev is TypeSafe AI's System One model: you provide information and predefined questions, it returns typed answers with probabilities. It cannot write your briefing, generate code, or explain its reasoning in prose. TypeSafe's launch essay

Start with a job like this:

> Research three new AI-agent tools and draft tomorrow's briefing. Save the draft for my review.

That job contains several decisions: Do we have enough sources? Which worker goes next? Is the draft ready for review?

Those are candidates for Jev. Fetching sources, writing paragraphs, and saving files still belong to your tools and generative models. An exact rule, such as stopping after ten actions, belongs in code.

For a GrokBot-style Chief of Staff, the saved handoff can feed an existing worker. Connecting that worker comes after the standalone setup below; you can complete the first run without an agent team.

## 02. Give it one decision in the Playground

- Open the TypeSafe Playground. Sign in and complete the access process if your account requires it.

Use this as your state:

Add a Choice question: "Which worker should act next?"

Define three options: research for missing evidence, write for drafting from sufficient evidence, and review for unclear requests or completed work.

Run it. Then replace the completed-work field with actual research notes and compare the decision. This is the basic interaction described in the official Quickstart.

## 03. Connect the API once

You need a TypeSafe account with API access enabled and a key from key settings. API calls are billed to that account. 

Install Python 3.12 or newer, then open Terminal on macOS/Linux or PowerShell on Windows.

macOS / Linux:

Windows PowerShell:

These commands create an isolated environment and install the official Python SDK. Keep your key outside source files; the script below asks for it privately.

Using a coding agent? With Node.js/npm installed, add TypeSafe's official skill:

Select your supported agent when prompted. The skill gives it integration instructions; Jev itself runs through the API. Official repository

## 04. Turn a request into a saved handoff

Create chief.py inside jev-starter, outside .venv. Use a plain-text editor and save the exact filename, not chief.py.txt.

Run on macOS/Linux:

Run on Windows:

Paste your API key when asked - the terminal hides it. 
For Goal, enter Compare three AI-agent tools for tomorrow's briefing. For Completed work, enter No sources collected yet.

Your result: a Saved handoff: message with a full file path. Open that JSON file: it contains your request, progress, Jev's choice, confidence, and destination. 
Each run creates a new file under queue/research, queue/write, or queue/review. These are local task queues; a saved job waits for a worker to consume it

The API call and error handling follow the SDK usage guide. I set the initial review threshold to 0.85 - adjust it using labeled examples from your workflow. Confidence is not an accuracy percentage. Confidence guidance

## 05. Ask questions that lead somewhere

Three answer types cover different jobs:

Jev gives you three question types, each built for a different kind of decision:

- Choice selects one option from a list. Use it for questions like: "Who should work next?" It returns the selected option, its probability distribution, and confidence.

- Score evaluates something against a scale you define. Use it for questions like: "How relevant is this source?" It returns a value on that scale, plus probabilities and confidence.

- Noul answers a yes-or-no question. Use it for questions like: "Does this request require publishing?" It returns the probability of “yes” from 0 to 1.

Define a relevance Score with three descriptions: unrelated, partially relevant, directly addresses the question. Its numeric result runs from 0 to 2, including fractions. A Noul near 0.5 means uncertainty about yes/no. Score · Noul

A useful detail: Jev does not see your question ID. Naming a field safe_to_publish contributes no instructions. Put the actual requirement in the question and describe each option clearly. Choice documentation

Also supply evidence. "The researcher finished" tells Jev less than the sources, findings, and remaining gaps. Keep those fields separate from the original request. State documentation

## 06. Steal Browser Use's best idea: rebuild the menu

A browser's available actions change after every click. Browser Use builds a fresh list of observed controls and lets Jev choose from that list. A small LLM generates text when an input field needs filling. Decision implementation

Apply that design to your Chief of Staff. Build the choices from workers that exist and are available now. Include the current source IDs when selecting research material. Refresh the options after a tool changes the state.

- Otherwise your decision model is choosing from yesterday's menu.

For large candidate lists, filter obvious mismatches in code, score the remaining items, then choose among the shortlist. Choice supports up to 255 options; TypeSafe describes this scoring-then-selection approach in its launch examples

## 07. Stop paying for questions to wait on each other

Your dispatcher may need a worker, an urgency score, and an approval check. 
If all three can inspect the same state, send them together.

TypeSafe supports parallel questions and speculative branches: ask about possible next actions, then use only the answer relevant to the selected branch. 
Questions cannot read one another's answers. If a decision needs a fresh search result, perform the search first. Parallel evaluation pattern

The browser example exposes another bottleneck. Its optimized runtime reduced median browser protocol calls from 1,092 to 101, while median task time fell 25% across three matched pairs. Both versions used the same models.

The changes included collecting the page state in one read and avoiding fresh predictions for irrelevant animations. Inspect repeated tool calls before paying for a faster model. Performance report

## 08. Give overnight work somewhere to stop

For a morning briefing, I'd allow source collection and draft creation, then stop at review. Publishing should require a separate permission check.

The application also needs an action limit, a spending limit, and saved progress. 
After an interruption, it should inspect the last completed action before repeating anything. A confident answer cannot prove that a file was saved or a message was sent.

Browser Use independently checks the outcome after Jev selects DONE. Borrow that separation for your own completion checks. Agent loop

Once the local router works, use this brief to connect your existing agents:

> Read the TypeSafe skill and inspect my worker interfaces. Connect chief.py's JSON queues to existing research and writing handlers. Prevent duplicate processing. Save progress after each action. Add call and spending limits, review on uncertainty, and a draft-exists completion check. Keep publishing behind approval. Identify missing connectors explicitly.

If the starter fails, use the error to choose the fix:

- Python command missing: finish Python installation and reopen the terminal.

- Module missing: repeat the SDK install with the same .venv interpreter.

- 401: replace the API key and rerun.

- 422: check the named request field against the pasted code.

- 429 / 529: allow backoff; retry later if rate limiting or overload persists.

The SDK supplies retries; the script stops if an API error remains. API reference

## 09. Know what the headline price actually buys

Jev 1.13 costs $0.042 per million input tokens, with no output-token charge. At 1,000 billed input tokens per decision, 10,000 decisions cost $0.42 for Jev inference. Pricing

The flight demo's reported $0.0039 fits its recorded 90,558 Jev input tokens plus the text helper's reported charge. 
Browser costs sit outside that calculation. Its roughly seven-second clock starts after the initial page observation and excludes fresh post-run verification

- So it finds flight results; it does not book tickets. Run measurements

For a different workload, Vercel's fx team reported roughly 5-18x faster safety classification than GPT-5.6-luna, alongside improved accuracy. 
That comparison concerns the classifier, not the duration of an entire agent run. Original benchmark

Track the bill per completed task. A cheap decision that sends a worker down the wrong branch can cost more than the decision itself.

## 10. Examples of Use

After the basic setup, Jev can already read the state of a task and choose between predefined options. Now you only need to decide which repeated decision to automate.

1. Control a Browser

Browser Use used Jev to select the next action and the correct page element. The agent found flights in 7 seconds for $0.0039.

Open the code

How to repeat it: run the official project, add your TypeSafe and OpenRouter keys, then give the agent a website and a goal. Jev selects the action and target, while the browser executes the decision.

2. Classify Research

Hassan used Jev to classify 1,018 AI research papers. The entire classification cost $0.08, with 256ms median end-to-end latency per paper

How to repeat it: send the title and summary of each paper to Jev, then define your topics as Choice options. Save the selected category and send the strongest papers to your writing agent.

3. Triage Your Inbox

Riley Brown demonstrated how Jev can classify incoming emails and decide what should happen next.

How to repeat it: pass each email as the state, then add reply, research, wait, and review as Choice options. Connect each answer to the corresponding folder or email agent.

4. Route Tasks Between Models

LangChain uses Jev to choose between cheaper and more capable models based on the task

Open the LangChain guid

How to repeat it: connect several models, describe what each one is best at, and send the incoming request to Jev. Route simple tasks to a cheaper model and complex tasks to a reasoning model.

And other cases: 

## The shift

> An LLM creates the work → Jev decides what happens next.

Jev is not another chatbot

It is a fast decision layer that reads the current state of your system and chooses between the options you define

And the real alpha is not the 7-second flight demo or the $0.08 paper classification

The real alpha is realizing how many expensive LLM calls inside your agents never needed generation:

- Let the LLM research, plan, and write

- Let Jev route, score, approve, or escalate

- Let code execute the decision

That split changes the entire agent stack

You now have the setup, the working decision router, and four real ways to deploy it. Start with one repeated decision. Measure it. Then replace the next one.

Most builders will keep spending frontier-model tokens on every yes, no, route, and score

The few who separate thinking from deciding will build faster agents at a fraction of the cost.

> Bookmark this playbook before your next agent  → @0xCodila

title: The "Stealth" Bear Market: A Historic Opportunity.
body:
We receive thousands of questions per week. But recently, one has been the most common of them all. Oil prices are above $100/barrel, borrowing costs are at 2002 levels, and inflation is nearly double the Fed's 2% target. So, HOW is the S&P 500 trading ~2% away from a record high?

What if we told you that the S&P 500 can trade near record highs, while simultaneously being in a bear market?

That is exactly what we believe is happening. And we believe it represents one of the most significant opportunities in today's market.

We are now witnessing a historic market paradox: The "Bull-Bear" Market.

Below, we explain exactly what we mean.

## The Iran War - Day #229

Today marks the 229th day of the Iran War. Since the start of the Iran War, the S&P 500 is up +900 points. And, since the March 30th bottom, the S&P 500 is up nearly +1,500 points, adding +$14 trillion of market cap.

The world is also a vastly different place than it was 229 days ago. Inflation has nearly doubled, the Fed is hiking interest rates, and we are in the midst of the biggest energy crisis in world history. And, we are also in the midst of the biggest technological revolution in world history. 

Yet, if you ask most investors, the current sentiment is that the current fundamental backdrop has deteriorated compared to where it was 8 months ago. 

## The Macroeconomy - A Historic Shift In Expectations 

At the start of 2026, the Fed was expected to CUT rates at least 3 times, for a total of 75 basis points this year. 

This was a major component of the bullish thesis for equities, with investors expecting cheaper capital, more investment, and record CapEx by technology companies.

Today, the Fed has already hiked interest rates once this year and markets see another 3 interest rate hikes by June 2027, for a total of +100 basis points including September's rate hike. That's a +175 bps swing in rate expectations. Yet, the S&P 500 is still trading at record highs.  

Driving this shift has been the historic surge in oil prices, with diesel now up over +80% from its low seen in January 2026 and Brent crude oil trading at $106/barrel. 

Borrowing costs have surged as inflation doubled, the Fed is hiking rates, and the US is running a near-$2 trillion deficit. But still, the S&P 500 is at record highs. 

So, what is happening? 

## Most Of The S&P 500 Is Struggling: 

The reality is that the vast majority of the S&P 500's constituents are not trading anywhere near record high territory. Take a look at our analysis below.  

As indicated in the chart above, 84% of S&P 500 stocks are now trading at least -10% below their all-time highs. 

Real Estate leads the drawdown, with 97% of stocks down at least -10%, followed by Materials at 96%, Utilities at 94%, and Consumer Discretionary at 92%. 

Furthermore, 59% of S&P 500 stocks are down at least -20% from their highs, 41% are down more than -30%, and 17% are down more than -50%.

Now, take a look at return contribution since the March 30th bottom: 

Just 10 stocks have driven 70% of the S&P 500’s gain since March 30th.  These stocks have added +16 percentage points to the index’s +23% gain over this period. Nvidia, $NVDA, has contributed the most, accounting for 13% of the S&P 500's gain, or +3 percentage points.

This is followed by Micron, $MU, Apple, $AAPL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, each accounting for 9% of the S&P 500’s advance, adding +2 percentage points. Return contributions by AMD, $AMD, and Alphabet, $GOOGL, have been 8% and 7%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the remaining 490 stocks have accounted for just 30% of the S&P 500's gain since March 30th, adding +7 percentage points. 

The reality is that the MAJORITY of S&P 500 components are, in fact, in a bear market. In our view, for the S&P 500, this is in fact bullish, or at worst, does not matter for now. 

We explain why, next. 

## The S&P 500 Should Be Above 9,000: 

Without the Iran War, the S&P 500 could be at 9,000+. 

This is arguably the most resilient market in history. If the S&P 500 is 2% away from a record high despite inflation nearing 4%, gas prices on the rise, and the Fed HIKING rates, just imagine where the S&P 500 would be if the Iran War ended, oil prices came back down, and rate cuts returned. Or, if it never even happened.

Earnings growth just over the last 7 months of the Iran War has been historic, with the S&P 500 posting +52% blended earnings growth in Q2 2026.  

This marks the highest growth rate since Q2 2021, a period where the global economy was emerging from a historic lockdown and the US government handed out $4 trillion in stimulus. 

In other words, in the midst of a global energy crisis and a rate hike campaign, we are now seeing growth on par with $4+ trillion in stimulus and a global economy that restarted from an effective halt. 

The reality is that the AI narrative is even stronger than most people realize: the earnings growth is there to support it, even as inflation has been above 2% for 67 consecutive months.  

Take a look at Nvidia's P/E ratio over the last 12 months. Even as the stock is up +21% over this period, the company's P/E ratio is down -46%. The stock now has a Forward P/E ratio of ~24x, nearly in line with the S&P 500's 22x, even as $NVDA has risen +900% in 5 years. 

This is the story for MANY large-cap technology stocks, the very names that are carrying this market. 

As shown below, the S&P 500 and the S&P 500 Information Technology sector are now seeing nearly identical Forward P/E ratios. Historically, these stocks have almost always traded at a premium to the broader S&P 500.  

In our view, the very names that have been driving the equity market higher, most large-cap technology stocks, actually have deep discounts priced-in to their stocks, even as they trade at or near record highs. We believe these stocks would be trading MUCH higher if it were not for the macroeconomic factors that we have seen over the last seven months. 

Combine this with the fact that over 80% of S&P 500 stocks are down -10% or more from their record highs, and our thesis is even stronger. If market breadth were to widen even slightly, buying pressure increases rapidly. 

And, even without this shift, the large-cap technology stocks that are driving the majority of price action appear relatively "cheap" compared to the S&P 500. 

This is why we said for the S&P 500, market concentration is bullish, or at worst, does not matter *for now.* 

## March 30th Was A Gift To Investors: 

The thesis we outline today has been a central part of our investment strategy in our premium research since March 30th. Below is the front page of The Kobeissi Letter as published on March 30th, 2026.  

As the S&P 500 fell below 6,400, we initiated a strong buy signal on the index and the equity market more broadly. Below is our note on the S&P 500 from March 30th.  

We noted that the bond market was a central part of our thesis along with the fact that the technology stocks that were driving the broader equity market lower were being sold with seemingly irrational price action. 

The result was a "V-Shaped" recovery in the S&P 500, after which we continuously raised our S&P 500 target to 7,800, and we also called for bond market intervention by the Trump Administration. 

Every Sunday, we update the above analysis in our weekly research and we also provide daily updates on our private X feed. If you are not already a client, consider subscribing to receive analysis like this in real-time here.

Today, the Trump Administration is intervening in the bond market, so far unsuccessfully, but further attempts at intervention are inevitable in our view. 

Ultimately, however, our thesis today is rooted in our view expressed on March 30th, which has only gained more momentum as we look ahead to 2027. 

## Investors Want More Assets: 

On top of the discount that is already priced-in to equity markets as discussed above, investors are keen to own assets amid the persistent inflation we are seeing in the US. 

US CPI inflation has now been above the Fed's 2% target for 67 consecutive months. The last time inflation was below 2% in the US was in January 2021, amid a global economic lockdown. 

Over this period, the value of the US Dollar has declined by -22.5%. In other words, it now costs $129 to purchase the same goods and services that cost $100 in 2021. Hence, investors want more stocks and hard assets over the long-run, not less. 

Therefore, if there were to be any indication of the Iran War ending and the global energy crisis subsiding, this would lead to a domino effect in the bullish direction. 

Energy prices would drop, inflation expectations would follow, the Fed could pivot more dovish, the "discount" in technology stocks would be priced-out, and the market's rally would broaden. 

All while the AI Revolution continues to accelerate and many large-cap technology stocks become cheaper on a forward earnings basis, even as their stock prices rise. 

And in the background, the demand for asset ownership is historically robust.

## In Conclusion: The "Bull-Bear Market." 

In summary, we believe the S&P 500 is in a bear market, within a bull market.  

Even as the S&P 500 hits year #5 of its bull market, we believe a steep discount is currently priced into equities. This discount has functioned as a "stealth" bear market, suppressing equity valuations in the world's largest and fastest-growing companies. 

This backdrop has the ability to catalyze a violent rally in the S&P 500 if and when it is ultimately priced-out. 

We expect a highly eventful 2027.

An objective and systematic approach is what has led to our outperformance of market benchmarks.

title: Designing MCP Gateway Uber's MCP Management Platform
body:
# Introduction

Uber’s rapid adoption of AI agents has fundamentally changed how teams interact with code, data, and operational systems.  Early ad-hoc integrations with the MCP (Model Context Protocol) showed clear value: agents became dramatically more capable when they could access live business context, query internal services, and take meaningful actions on behalf of users. These early wins validated MCP as a powerful abstraction for building agentic systems inside Uber.

However, as adoption accelerated, significant challenges emerged. Individual teams independently built integrations, leading to fragmentation in tooling and duplicated infrastructure. MCP tools were hard to discover, difficult to operate reliably, and tightly coupled to specific services or agent implementations. While these approaches worked at a small scale, they didn’t meet Uber’s needs as hundreds of teams began exploring agentic workflows. Without a unified architecture, scaling MCP would increase operational complexity, security risk, and developer friction, ultimately limiting its impact.

To unlock MCP’s full potential at Uber’s scale, we needed a centralized, scalable solution to standardize how AI agents interact with existing back-end systems while preserving flexibility for teams. This solution needed to abstract protocol differences (HTTP, gRPC™, TChannel), enforce consistent security and observability guarantees, and make MCP tools easy to create, discover, and reuse across the company.

We built the MCP Gateway to address this need. It’s a foundational microservice that powers all MCP interactions at Uber, serving as an orchestration and routing layer between AI agents and existing back-end services and native MCP servers. By centralizing MCP logic into a single gateway, we provide a consistent execution model for agent-to-service interactions while eliminating the need for teams to reinvent core infrastructure. Existing APIs can be seamlessly exposed as MCP tools, governed and operated in one place, and consumed by multiple agents in a uniform way. MCP Gateway unlocked a scalable, fast, and consistent path to building AI agents within Uber and is currently hosting over 800 MCP servers and over 5000 tools.

In this blog, we review the design of the MCP Gateway, covering the Proxy Layer (translation of MCP to existing protocols and back), Discovery Layer (MCP Registry and API crawling), and its control plane (authoring).

## The Gateway

MCP Gateway follows a microservice-based architecture, with the gateway acting as the central integration point between AI-enabled systems and Uber’s back-end services. The platform comprises two primary components: the MCP Registry, which serves as the control plane, and the Proxy Gateway, which forms the data plane.

The MCP Registry maintains a catalog of hundreds of MCP servers backed by internal services, along with thousands of MCP tools. These tools range from no-code definitions that expose existing APIs as MCP tools to fully native implementations built explicitly against the MCP specification. The registry provides a single source of truth for discovery, ownership, and enablement across the ecosystem.

The Proxy Gateway is responsible for executing MCP requests at runtime. It translates MCP protocol calls into HTTP, gRPC, or TChannel requests, forwards them to the appropriate back-end service, and converts the responses back into MCP-compatible results. This translation layer allows AI agents to interact with existing systems through a consistent MCP interface, without requiring changes to the underlying services.

## Control Plane

Uber uses a microservice architecture and runs thousands of internal services that expose APIs over HTTP, gRPC, and TChannel. These APIs provide valuable context to an AI system, but asking teams to manually author an MCP server would be slow and painful. To solve this problem, we built AutoCrawler, which continuously scans Uber’s IDL registry for APIs, translates them, and updates them in the registry. It also queries native MCP servers and adds them to the registry.

AutoCrawler: Discovery Engine

Autocrawler is a Cadence-powered distributed workflow system subscribed to Uber’s IDL registry and internal service signals. On a fixed schedule, a cron job triggers a Cadence workflow that scans for newly added services, APIs, and schema changes.

For every discovered entity, AutoCrawler is responsible for:

- Creating or updating MCP server representations

- Generating or fetching tool definitions and schemas

- Registering tools in the MCP Registry in a disabled-by-default state

This shared foundation enables MCP discovery to scale across thousands of services while keeping service teams off the critical path.

Discovery for IDL-Backed Services

For traditional back-end services defined through Protobuf or Thrift IDLs, AutoCrawler derives MCP servers and tools directly from the IDL Registry. For each service: API group, AutoCrawler performs the following steps:

- Upsert MCP server: Creates or updates a virtual MCP server corresponding to the discovered service.

- Parse IDL definitions: Parses the associated protobuf or Thrift files to extract method names, request and response schemas, and documentation comments.

- Generate tool descriptions: Uses an LLM to generate enriched, agent-friendly MCP tool descriptions based on the extracted schemas and comments.

- Schema translation: Translates protobuf or Thrift schemas into MCP-compatible JSON-RPC 2.0 schemas.

- Upsert MCP tools: Registers or updates the generated MCP tools in the MCP Registry in a disabled-by-default state.

Discovery for Native Servers

In addition to IDL-backed services, the MCP Gateway also supports native MCP servers—services that implement the MCP protocol directly and expose agent-optimized tools.

MCPFx is the framework Uber uses to build native MCP servers. Each native MCP server emits a heartbeat metric that signals its presence and readiness. AutoCrawler continuously monitors these heartbeat signals to automatically discover new native MCP servers. When a native MCP server is discovered, AutoCrawler follows a different discovery path:

1. It makes a listTools call to the native MCP server to retrieve the tools it explicitly exposes, along with their schemas.

2. It creates a virtual proxy MCP server in the MCP Registry that contains all discovered tools and their schemas, in a disabled-by-default state.

3P MCP Servers

The MCP Gateway serves as the centralized orchestration layer for all MCP interactions across Uber, extending seamless support to third-party integrations such as Jira and Google.

Provisioning third-party MCP servers relies on the co-operation of two key components:

1. MCP Gateway: Relays the caller's user token downstream while enforcing essential gateway capabilities, including authorization, rate limiting, and sensitive data redaction.

2. Third-Party MCP Service: Exchanges the internal user token for a corresponding third-party authentication token before dispatching the request to the external MCP server.

Authoring and Enablement

While we may create MCP servers without involving the service team, ownership and control of the MCP server must reside with the service team. A core design principle of the MCP Gateway is that discovery doesn’t imply exposure. Every MCP server and tool starts in a disabled state and must be explicitly reviewed and enabled by the owning team. Service owners can review and refine the generated tool definitions before enabling them.

Every change to the tool description triggers a config change diff, which must be approved by server owners. Owners can approve and deploy the config change, and, if needed, roll back to a previous known version.

## Data Plane

The MCP Gateway data plane is the core runtime service responsible for executing MCP requests. It continuously consumes server and tool configurations from the control plane and refreshes its in-memory state at a fixed cadence, allowing configuration changes, such as tool updates or enablement changes, to take effect in real time without service restarts or redeployments.

Based on this configuration, the data plane dynamically materialises virtual MCP servers. For each virtual server, the Gateway exposes a single /<service-name>/mcp endpoint that serves as the entry point for AI agent execution. Incoming requests are resolved to their corresponding server handlers through a built-in proxy server.

Protocol Translation and Execution

Protocol translation in the MCP Gateway is handled by server handlers within the Proxy Gateway. Each server handler is tool-aware and downstream-aware, allowing it to correctly route and execute MCP requests at runtime.

Security

MCP Gateway provides built-in authorization and redaction for all servers at tool-level granularity. MCP Gateway uses Uber’s internal Access Control System to apply different charter policies configured on detected caller actors  (humans, services, and agents). Charter policies are created at the server level with optional tool-level overrides if required.

MCP Gateway also does out-of-the-box redaction for any PII or sensitive data from the tool responses.

IDL-Backed Downstream Services

For tools backed by existing back-end services, the server handler maintains an in-memory mapping that describes the downstream destination, such as HTTP endpoint config or gRPC/TChannel procedures.

When an MCP request arrives, the handler:

1. Translates the incoming JSON payload into the appropriate wire format.

2. Serializes the request into Protobuf or Thrift bytes.

3. Forwards the request to the downstream service.

4. Translates Protobuf or Thrift byte responses back to MCP-compatible JSON and returns them to the calling agent.

The actual downstream request is executed via Muttley, Uber’s service mesh sidecar that runs alongside all back-end services. By delegating request execution to Muttley, the MCP Gateway automatically benefits from existing service-to-service routing capabilities.

Native MCP Servers

Native MCP servers are also registered as virtual servers in the MCP registry, which acts as a proxy to the original server. At runtime, ‌native MCP requests are transparently proxied to the downstream server, and responses are proxied back to the caller.

## Benefits of the Gateway

By building the MCP-Gateway, Uber has achieved a scalable and unified approach towards building agentic systems, with the most impactful benefits coming from:

- Easy discovery and installation

- No-code approach towards existing APIs

- Built-in observability and security

- Centralized ownership and governance

## Extending the Gateway

Scaling MCP Gateway to hundreds of servers and thousands of tools revealed problems that don’t exist at small scale. Context Bloat and Excessive Cost

Runtime Discovery

MCP has no native concept of cross-server search. An agent has to already know which server to talk to before it can ask what tools are available. Configuring an agent to use an MCP server requires explicitly wiring up the server URL, credentials, and tool list. Doing this for hundreds of servers doesn’t scale, as all this context would eat up the model context limit. We solved this problem with the following

- Omni MCP  - A single proxy server that allows MCP clients to access any of the MCP Gateway’s servers with a gradual discovery pattern, which also unlocks context/token optimization via incremental discovery.  Omni MCP exposes these tools.

- discover_server - discover MCP server based on the query intent

- discover_tools - lookup tools for a server

- get_tool_schema - get the json schema for a tool

- invoke_tool  - invoke a tool

Together, these tools enable incremental discovery and access to all MCP servers, with built-in access control and the rest of the gateway features.

- Response Projection - MCP Gateway also offers Response Projection, a GraphQL-like calling pattern for MCP tools. It works by injecting a new field in the tool request schema, which instructs the gateway to request only the needed fields, not all. The LLM reads and injects the fields with an array of nested paths of only required fields. The Gateway then trims the response in runtime by only keeping the projected fields. This has allowed us to scale the API schema compatibility for MCP at the enterprise level.

- Code Mode - Coding agents often operate in shell environments where writing tool output directly to files is more efficient than loading full responses into model context. Code Mode serves this pattern through aifx, Uber's CLI for agentic operations, routing MCP calls through the gateway without requiring any MCP server to be installed. It helps agents discover correct MCP tools for the job without the MCP definition being present in context. aifx exposes three commands:

- aifx mcp list - list available MCP servers

- aifx mcp search - search for tools across all MCP servers

- aifx mcp call - invoke an MCP tool through MCP Gateway

Agents can chain these in a single command and write output to files, which filesystem agents grep selectively, loading only what they need into context. Code Mode is now the company default for MCP tool use in coding agents.

# Conclusion

Building the MCP Gateway has fundamentally changed how AI agents operate at Uber. What began as a fragmentation problem, with dozens of teams independently wiring up MCP integrations with inconsistent tooling, no shared security guarantees, and duplicated infrastructure,  is now a unified, scalable platform that any team can plug into in minutes.

The core insight driving our design was simple: existing APIs are the fastest way to provide tools to an agent. Rather than asking teams to rewrite their services for an agentic world, MCP Gateway meets them where they are—translating HTTP, gRPC, and TChannel calls into MCP-compatible interactions transparently, through Muttley, with zero changes to downstream services.

If you’re building agentic systems at scale, the hardest part isn’t the AI. It’s building the connective tissue the discovery, the security, the reliability  that makes agents trustworthy enough to act on behalf of real users in a production environment. MCP Gateway is our answer to that challenge, and we hope the design decisions documented here are useful to others facing the same problem.
