title: 【必备技能 | 伸手即用】AI 人物一致性控制 - 角色卡制作 Skill
body:
无论是出图还是做视频，AI 人物长期一致性控制都是一个很重要的课题，对作品的留存率、形象感有显著的影响。也是打造 IP 必备的技能。

它本质上是一张角色视觉定义图，把脸、身材、发型、表情、服装和不同视角一次性固定下来。

# 一、确定角色结构 

很多人初次见到角色设定提示词可能会感到困惑。其实，这可以视为一项简单的任务。

这一步的关键在于固定角色的结构：通过正面、侧面和背面的视角，确保锁定角色的脸部特征、比例以及整体造型。稳定这一部分后，后续的生成就不易出现问题。（适用于真人角色）

# 二、增强表现力

角色的表情、微表情、姿态变化和手部动作等元素有助于传达角色的动态特征和情绪表达。这样生成的人物会显得栩栩如生，而非僵硬呆板。

# 三、细节说明

对头部结构、服装细节和材质等方面的说明，有助于AI更精准地理解。例如，发型的分层方式、衣物材质和金属质感等。

这一步决定了角色的质感和高端感，使生成的视频内容更加可控。

# 四、操作步骤

选择一个图像生成工具，准备一张角色图片，然后在节点中选择图片输入。

将提示词复制到窗口，根据需要进行调整，整个过程非常灵活。

# 五、核心原则

所有的小图实际上都是为中心的“主形象图”服务。

理解了这一点后，整段提示词内容就变得清晰简洁。

目标是为AI提供一份“角色说明书”，而不仅仅是生成一幅美观的图像。

title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
body:
Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available today for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.

Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains, ranking #1 on the Vals Index, which measures model performance across critical economic sectors like finance, coding, legal, and tax work.

The model launches today at an introductory price* of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (with cached input tokens at 95% off).

*After the introductory period expires on November 30, 2026, the price of $4 per 1M input tokens and $20 per 1M output tokens will apply. Applies to the Argon model intended for public access only.

Teams at Google, across enterprises, and in the research community have already been using Argon to land significant impact across fields:

- To solve major engineering problems like large codebase refactoring and optimizations

- To optimize business workflows across domains like legal, finance, and science

- To find and patch critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities

- To enable novel breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and life sciences

## Solving complex engineering tasks

At Google, we’ve been using Argon on our hardest engineering problems. Over the past few weeks, software engineers have been shipping high-quality code faster than ever. Argon in Antigravity has helped teams increase agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third.

- Untangling browser feature code in Chrome: Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome's billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes.

- Optimizing a production Python codebase in hours: Argon in Antigravity is helping the team behind Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), a framework powering enterprise agents, push their performance engineering further. The team gave Argon their .agents/skills rulebook and a one-paragraph goal to eliminate framework overhead without breaking existing apps. Working autonomously overnight, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python, that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21%. Read the engineering deep dive to learn more.

- Quantum chemistry open-source package optimization: xTB (Semiempirical Extended Tight-Binding) is one of the most-cited open-source quantum chemistry packages for molecules. Scientists use it to predict molecules' 3D shapes and to screen large numbers of drug and materials candidates. Using Argon in Antigravity, our researchers made xTB up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search. The changes have been contributed to the official xTB repository on GitHub.

- Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast: Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes.

- Delivering complex 3D visualizations: Argon brings major improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding compared to previous Gemini models. Using slash commands like /goal and prompting for multi-agent loops with custom skills in Antigravity, Googlers are using Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations in vanilla code that can be rendered directly in the browser.

## Transforming critical business and professional workflows

Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded domain knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities across legal, finance, science, and coding to help with high-stakes professional workflows. It communicates clearly, keeping you in the loop, and follows style instructions better than any of our previous Gemini models. Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses.

Enterprise customers and startups in our early access program are already seeing strong wins with Argon.

Using its advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities while maintaining strict grounding, Argon excels in deep multimodal document comprehension, longitudinal data analysis, and interactive analytical sandboxes.

# Accelerating real-world impact with researchers and domain experts

Researchers, engineers, and security specialists are already using Argon to push the boundaries of cyber defense, science, math, and robotics. It’s helping cyber defenders and researchers test hypotheses, autonomously audit critical codebases and formal proofs, and catch subtle zero-day vulnerabilities and logic flaws.

## Bringing state-of-the-art cybersecurity capabilities to more trusted defenders

Starting today, we’re beginning expansion to hundreds of additional Fairwind Program partners.

Wiz is already using Argon for its "Scan for Good" initiative, which protects critical infrastructure for the public good and for free. With early access to the model, Wiz has demonstrated Argon's real-world impact across multiple high-stakes sectors:

- Securing sensitive government data: As part of a long-standing cyber resilience program and in collaboration with a federal agency, Argon helped to proactively identify and remediate a gap that risked exposing sensitive data and government infrastructure. This effort helped prevent against the exposure of critical security sector development details and unauthorized access to specialized models.

- Protecting critical healthcare infrastructure: Wiz also used Argon to protect vital healthcare infrastructure. By chaining complex vulnerabilities, the model helped the team discover and quickly fix a public file download bypass that exposed a master key and granted administrator access. Argon went beyond spotting a vulnerability to proactively safeguarding hundreds of thousands of private patient records.

## Unlocking new scientific breakthroughs

Argon is already having real-world impact across the scientific community — enabling novel discovery for scientists and experts across multiple domains.

- Quantum computing: Argon is helping our researchers accelerate progress across both quantum error correction and algorithm design. To help error decoders keep pace with quantum hardware in real-time, Argon translated an internal version of AlphaQubit, our ML quantum error correction decoder, into a single, highly optimized hardware kernel — nearly doubling its inference throughput so we can deploy larger, more capable models and scale to larger quantum devices, while continuing to meet strict real-time thresholds. Argon is also reducing spacetime costs for quantum subroutines. For arcsin, a building block in recent quantum simulation algorithms, an implementation written by Argon and formally verified in Lean cuts spacetime cost by more than 100x compared to a published quantum CORDIC baseline, a step toward a standard library of optimized quantum circuits.

- Nuclear fusion: Stellarators are incredibly complex machines that represent a leading candidate for limitless clean fusion energy, but optimizing their 3D magnetic fields is famously difficult. Since 1967, a long-standing hypothesis known as “Grad’s conjecture” assumed that finding exact mathematical solutions for these fields was impossible, until recent counterexamples were found, including by Professor Matt Landreman (University of Maryland). Now, a team at Google alongside Professor Landreman has discovered a broader class of counterexamples to Grad's conjecture. These new solutions give the fusion community reliable benchmarks to test their stellarator simulations codes, which are valuable tools for future designs.

- Rare disease research: Researchers at Gamow Labs used Argon to analyze de-identified genomes from newborns with rare developmental lung disorders. In one case, Argon pinpointed a chromosomal rearrangement that routine software missed for years, and explained why it went undetected. On private Gamow Labs evals derived from real clinical and lab data, Argon topped on RareBench (57% on assistance with rare-disease diagnosis) and LabBench (52.2% on wet-lab reasoning). These advances point to faster diagnosis for families facing rare conditions. See blog* for more details.

- Enzyme design: Engineering enzymes with precise reactivity is notoriously slow, often demanding months of bespoke model tuning and candidate screening. Serine esterases are a class of enzymes that cut ester bonds on targeted molecules, widely used in recycling, and the manufacture of pharmaceuticals, biofuels and detergents. Our scientists worked with Argon to design serine esterases, targeting the benchmark molecule 4MU-acetate that glows under UV light once its ester bonds are broken. In a matter of hours, Argon assembled relevant data, performed model tuning and identified multiple biochemistry-inspired filters to get to a final set of five novel designs. Subsequent laboratory testing confirmed robust catalytic activity across these designs. The speed and ease of successful enzyme generation demonstrates the potential for rapid acceleration in enzyme engineering in fields such as biomanufacturing, green chemistry, and drug development.

To further advance the pace of research, we’re offering 10,000 scientists the highest usage tier in Google Antigravity free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. Applications are now open.

*Views in this blog are of the external party and do not represent Google's views.

## Speeding up robotics development

By bringing together advanced visual-semantic reasoning, deep physical understanding, and autonomous code generation, Argon unlocks new workflows across the robotics stack and accelerates progress toward physical AGI. This leap in capability is reflected in Argon’s performance on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark, which tests a model's ability to understand and solve physical, spatial problems in 3D environments. Relying on pure reasoning, Argon outperforms all other frontier models, with an 87% score.

To demonstrate these capabilities in action, we tested Argon’s ability to learn an out-of-distribution physical skill simply by watching. In an internal test, Argon watched a raw video of a human playing cornhole, mapped the spatial coordinates of the environment, and calculated the required whole-body joint movements. It then autonomously built the simulation code. When transferred onto Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid, the robot quickly sank seven consecutive shots in a real-world trial.

This "Video-to-Sim-to-Real" pipeline compresses weeks of manual simulation modeling into a few hours, transforming ordinary videos into a scalable, infinite training ground for robotics.  Learn more about how this accelerates the pace of development in robotics in our developers blog.

## Developing Argon responsibly and safely

Safety and security are foundational to model development at Google. Because Argon is a highly capable model, we collaborated with a variety of third-party partners on measurement of certain model capabilities and safeguards. Gemini 4 Argon represents our most comprehensive safety and security stack yet:

- Misuse & jailbreak defenses: The same coding and scientific capabilities that help defenders patch hospital software or accelerate bioengineering also require strong safeguards against malicious actors. Under our Frontier Safety Framework, we evaluated Argon’s enhanced capabilities across several domains, and deployed a multi-layer defense stack combining jailbreak resistance, monitoring, and enforcement. This greatly improved our robustness — for instance, external bio red teaming could only unlock less than 1% of bio sub-tasks we test for. Further, when it comes to dangerous requests — from writing exploit code to helping with dangerous biological materials — Argon is significantly better at not fulfilling harmful requests than our previous models. On an adversarial set meant to stress test the model, violations reduced nearly 2-fold — also significantly better than previous Gemini models.

- Agent alignment & real-time monitoring: As agents become more capable problem solvers, we have to ensure they don’t get overly eager to finish a task by taking unauthorized shortcuts when they hit a roadblock, like a permission error or a failing test.

- First, we trained Argon to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly, and pause for human confirmation before taking irreversible steps. On coding benchmarks where models have no incentive to hold back, shortcut attempts dropped to just 2% on Gemini 4 Argon, our best performance compared to previous Gemini models.

- Second, as a defense-in-depth layer, we built an automated misalignment monitor that reads the agent’s step-by-step reasoning and actions to catch and block unintended workarounds in real time. We used this monitor across internal deployments, capability evaluations, and reinforcement learning training runs — while strictly avoiding penalizing the model’s thoughts during training so its reasoning remains transparent and monitorable.

- Prompt injection resistance: When agents browse webpages, read emails, or inspect code, they can encounter hidden malicious instructions designed to hijack their task. Through adversarial training and automated red teaming, Argon leads the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) benchmark, cutting attack success across 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%.

For more information, see the Gemini 4 Argon Model Card.

## Get started today

Argon works longer and harder to solve highly complex scientific, coding, and agentic problems. This is enabled by an industry-leading 1M unified input-output token limit via the Gemini API. Read through our documentation for developers and enterprises to learn about the new continuation protocol and ensure the appropriate setup for your needs. Argon is rolling out today globally:

- For developers: Build with the Gemini API paid tier in AI Studio and Android Studio, and if you’re a Google AI Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity and AI Studio.

- For enterprises: Try it in Gemini for business, the API, and in Google Antigravity.

- For everyday users: Try it starting today in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search if you’re a Google AI Ultra or Pro subscriber.

- For scientists & researchers: Apply for a chance to get access to Google Antigravity’s highest usage tier free of charge for 6 months (onboarded on a rolling basis), subject to eligibility, capacity, and selection. Applications are now open.

- For cybersecurity defenders: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access to Argon without cyber guardrails on a rolling basis.

Gemini 4 Argon is just the beginning. We’re looking forward to bringing you the rest of the Gemini 4 family.

title: How to use Claude Opus 5.5 for SEO so well it feels illegal
body:
THIS IS THE ARTICLE IS WAS NOT GOING TO PUBLISH. It's the most in-depth course you will get on doing SEO with AI (and i'm sharing it all for free).

## TLDR:

1. How to pick the keywords that pay.

2. Build pages better than the top 3.

3. Earn links, free first and paid last.

4. Get named by others so ChatGPT cites you.

5. Repeat every week, because the order matters more than any single tactic.

So I took everything I've published, cut what aged, fixed what I got wrong, and put it in the order we actually run it.

Last thing, if you want me to continue doing these, I need your support.

So a like, a quote or a bookmark would help me continue 🙏

Back to the course 🔥

## Before we start: what AI can and cannot do for your SEO

AI does not know your search volumes. It does not know your rankings.

Ask Claude which keyword to target and it guesses from its training. Ask it where your site ranks and it cannot know. Everything downstream of a guess is a guess.

What Claude is great at:

- Reading Search Console exports and finding the patterns you would miss

- Writing 30 pages that follow one structure without drifting

- Adding internal links to every old page you own, which no human does twice

- Writing structured data, titles and meta descriptions at scale

- Running the same check every Monday without forgetting

What it cannot know on its own:

- Search volume and keyword difficulty

- Your rankings, clicks and impressions

- What Google shows on the results page today

- Which competitor pages are taking your traffic

So the job splits in three.

- Claude is the hands. Opus 5.5 in Claude Code if you have a repo. Sonnet 5.5 in a Claude Project if you don't. It plans, writes, edits, runs the routines.

- ChatSEO is the brain. Through its MCP it brings your Search Console, keyword volumes, the live SERP, competitor pages scraped to the source code, and a process built from how a consultant actually works.

- You approve. Anything that touches a live page, or leaves under your name.

Setup takes five minutes. Create a ChatSEO account, add your site, connect Search Console. Skip that last step and half of what follows runs blind. Then in your terminal:

claude mcp add --transport http chatseo https://api.chatseo.app/mcp

Open Claude Code, type /mcp to log in once. In the Claude app, add https://api.chatseo.app/mcp as a connector instead (the MCP is on the Pro plan).

Every prompt below that says "Using ChatSEO" assumes this connection. The ones that say "skill" are files: save them as .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md in your repo and Claude Code picks them up.

One more thing before Part 1.

GEO is not a separate discipline you start after SEO. When ChatGPT doesn't know the answer, it searches Google. If you have no SEO, you have nothing for the model to find.

-> Good GEO needs great SEO first. That is why GEO is Part 4 and not Part 1.

# Part 1: Pick the money before you write a word

Most SEO traffic is vanity.

"What is SEO". "CBD benefits". Your Search Console curve goes up, you feel great, and nobody buys.

Paul, my co-founder, puts it bluntly: is that traffic for your ego or for your business?

## Module 1: Target the card in hand

The only keywords worth your first six months are the ones where the searcher already has the card in hand.

"SEO consultant Paris". "Coffee table". "Shopify SEO agency". "Alternative to Mangools".

You do not need a tool to read intent. Google already did the testing. Type the keyword and look at what ranks.

- Blog posts and a definition box at the top: informational. Skip for now.

- Landing pages, service pages, category pages with prices: commercial. That is your target.

Low volume is not the price of admission. "[Competitor] alternative" might do 90 searches a month. All 90 of those people are shopping for a replacement today.

## Module 2: A keyword gets you a page. A pattern gets you a machine.

A pattern is a set of keywords with identical intent, where Google returns the same type of page every time. Only one word changes.

- "[Tool A] vs [Tool B]"

- "Best SEO tool for [ecommerce]"

- "SEO consultant [city]"

- "[Service] [city]"

- "[Product type] [material]"

One pattern is dozens of pages. You never pick a topic again. You pick the next row.

The free way to find them is Google Suggest. Type your seed, then add a * at the end, then at the start. Each one surfaces a different batch. Google Ads' Keyword Planner adds the volumes.

The fast way is to let Claude ask the analyst.

Step 6 is there for a reason. Claude will happily fill a blank column with a plausible number. The analyst exists so it never has to.

## Module 3: If you sell software, there are 9 page types. Write them in this order.

The order is by intent and by how hard the SERP is.

1. Alternative pages. Alternative to X, free alternative to X, cheaper alternative to X. Highest intent on the list. No company writes a page helping you leave them, so the incumbent cannot compete. Write these first.

2. Comparison pages. X vs Y, X or Y, X vs Y vs Z. Two vendors and a pile of affiliate content is the whole field. Be honest about the rows where you lose. It is the only thing that makes the rest believable.

3. Integration pages. Your tool + Slack, + Stripe, + Shopify. You borrow the search volume of somebody else's brand and almost nobody fights you for it. Twelve integrations is twelve pages.

4. Constraint pages. Without subscription, without credit card, open source. Binary filters, not opinions. If you match the constraint, you win the page outright. If you don't, don't write it.

5. Pricing pages. People search price before product. Directories already sit on most of these, so do them once you have some authority.

6. Use case pages. Tools to generate leads, to automate prospecting. You rank for the job instead of the category. Slower to land.

7. Problem pages. The reader doesn't know your category exists yet. Weak competition, low intent, real payoff at month six.

8. Feature pages. Only for features you genuinely lead on. Otherwise you are publishing a directory listing about yourself.

9. Company size pages. For freelancers, for SMEs. I would mostly skip these. They are almost always the same page with three words swapped, and Google has a name for that pattern.

Local business? Your patterns are "[service] [city]" and "[category] [city]". Part 2 has the full local system.

## Module 4: Pick the SERPs you can actually win

Most beginners burn their first months on keywords they can't rank for.

Two filters, and the first one kills most projects:

- The SERP is beatable at your current authority. We could not rank "Semrush alternative" when we started. Too competitive. Versus SERPs were thinner, and the reader was already comparing tools with a card in hand. That trade was deliberate.

- The intent is commercial. Module 1.

On a young site, go small and specific. A plumber in Austin should not start on "plumber Austin". The list underneath is where you win first: "emergency plumber Round Rock", "water heater repair Cedar Park". The suburbs pay the same rates as downtown.

The mistake that cost us the first months

Before ChatSEO, Paul and I ran a business plan generator.

The SEO opportunity was real. Thousands of programmatic queries. Low competition. Obvious buyer intent.

So we launched fast and published fast.

It never ranked. Not slowly. Never.

The pages were not the problem. A brand new domain, zero brand searches, zero backlinks, and a publishing rate that looked exactly like every site Google files under "generated at volume".

-> We were nobody, showing up loud. Google had no reason to spend crawl budget finding out whether we were the exception.

Everything in Parts 2 to 5 exists so you don't repeat that.

# Part 2: Build pages that deserve to rank

The most expensive SEO mistake is writing a page you already had.

The second most expensive is writing one that adds nothing to the nine results already there.

## Module 5: One keyword, one page. Decide before you write.

Here is the check Paul does by hand. Search Console, Performance, filter on the exact query, then the Pages tab.

- A page already gets clicks for it: optimise that page.

- A page gets impressions but few clicks: it is already somewhere in the top 10. Optimise it.

- Nothing: create a new page.

Get this wrong and you build cannibalisation. Two of your pages fight for the same query and Google cannot choose. Paul's example: both sit 7th and 8th, when one page would have been 3rd.

Then the part most consultants skip: secondary keywords. Take whoever ranks 1st for your keyword and list every other query that exact URL ranks top 5 for. That list is what Google already considers the same page. Target it all with one URL.

It all lands in the title.

The title is the page's identity card, the strongest on-page element you have. One word decides whether a page ranks for one query or five. "SEO Consultant Paris (Freelance)" covers two patterns at once. If pixels remain, spend them on the click.

The meta description barely moves rankings. Its job is to sell the click.

When Paul ran this live on his Lyon consultant page, ChatSEO flagged a canonical tag he had never noticed. He has been doing SEO since 2021. That is what the analyst is for.

## Module 6: Build what the top 3 are almost building, plus one thing they don't have

Open the top 3 and put yourself in the searcher's head.

Someone typing "SEO consultant Paris" wants to know why you, what it costs, how it works, and how long until results. Answer those, in the order the SERP answers them, and you are level.

Then do it better. Paul's teardown of a competitor ranking 1st: no photo of the person you would hire, no way to self-qualify. Add the face. Add a three-question quiz.

That last part is not decoration. It is your spam defence.

In March 2024 Google added scaled content abuse to its spam policies, and the wording matters. It applies no matter whether the content came from automation, humans, or a mix of both. What it targets is large amounts of unoriginal content that gives readers little to no value.

-> Volume is not a violation. Unoriginal content is.

Google's guidance on AI content says the same from the other side. They "focus on the quality of content, rather than how content is produced".

So for every page, one question: what is here that the other nine results do not have?

- A quiz that routes the visitor to the right answer

- A calculator or a simulator

- Your own data, or a table with numbers you actually pulled

- Real photos of the job, the team, the place

- Video

One of them on every page, or do not ship the page.

The rest of on-page is mostly noise:

- One H1 with your primary keyword. The H2 and H3 tree takes care of itself.

- Structured data. One instruction to Claude at publish time. Agencies hate it because half the fields only exist once the page is live, final URL, publish date, author. Claude publishes the page, so it has all of them.

- Internal links are a threshold, not a lever. Google discovers pages by following every link from your homepage. A page nothing links to barely exists. Paul's floor is five internal links to every new page, from pages on a close topic, inside body text.

-> A link in a sentence tells Google what the next page is about. A link in a menu tells it nothing.

## Module 7: Give Claude a template and a process file, not a prompt

Left alone, Claude ships black text on a white background.

Technically a page.

Step 1: Rebuild one page you already like as the template

Open a page from your own site. View source. Paste it into Claude Code:

Rebuild this page as the template for every SEO page on this site:
same design, title pattern, meta description, H1, FAQ block,
interactive element and CTA placement. Save it and use it for every
new page.

One shot the first time, two or three fixes after. Works even if the page was built in Elementor. Under the hood it's all code, and Claude reads code.

Step 2: Write the SEO process as a file

A markdown file Claude reads before every page. Two lines per rule is enough. Ours:

```
SEO process: read before every page

- Build on the template. Never invent a layout.
- Add at least 5 internal links to the new page, from the body of
related pages. Anchors match the target keyword of the new page.
- Translate to French and link the two with hreflang.
- Add the structured data that matches what is actually on the page.
- Update the sitemap on every publish.
- Request indexing in Search Console.
```

The internal links rule is the one that pays. Claude can open every page you own, including the old ones, and add the links itself. A human never does that consistently. I certainly did not.

The sitemap trap

The second you let Claude publish, you have left your CMS.

Paul found out the hard way. He was testing a ChatSEO feature that reads a site's sitemap, and it kept ignoring a page he had published the day before. The page was live. The sitemap had not moved since he stopped relying on his plugin.

Nothing warns you. Your site just quietly stops telling Google what exists. That is why "update the sitemap" is in the file.

The day Claude deleted the one thing that mattered

We asked Claude Code to duplicate one of our comparison pages for four new competitors.

Everything transferred. Titles, meta descriptions, structured data, table of contents, the FR and EN pair.

The quiz was gone. Both pages. No error, no warning, nothing in the output.

The quiz was the one original element. The exact thing the scaled content policy is written about.

Then it happened to Paul. Claude rewrote his city pages and dropped the "best SEO consultants" ranking tables. He found out live, recording a podcast.

An agent that can edit your site can quietly remove the one thing the page existed for. So our ship skill has a gate.

Step 4 is the whole lesson. The day it catches nothing is the day you stop needing it, and that day does not come.

## Module 8: Duplicate the pattern, slowly

Once one page in a pattern is right, the next forty are the same page.

Consultant + Lyon has the same intent as consultant + Lille. So you build page one by hand, take the full hour, and duplicate from there.

You are about to multiply this page by twenty. Every weakness multiplies with it.

The trap: a page where only the city name changes and nothing else does. That is a template with a find-and-replace. Google's spam policy calls it doorway abuse, and its example is literally "pages targeted at specific regions or cities that funnel users to one page". Every variant needs something only that variant can say. City facts, prices, examples, testimonials.

The cadence is the strategy

Our blog runs on one sentence, twice a week:

Take the last article we published, and do the next keyword in the
pattern.

Claude Code checks which variants exist, picks the next one, gets the brief and the article from ChatSEO, builds it on the template, translates it, links it, updates the sitemap and asks Google to index it.

2 articles in English, 2 in French. Four pages a week. A person reads every one before it goes live.

A year ago the ChatSEO blog got close to zero visits from Google. Today it gets about 3,000 a month.

The curve was not a straight line. It climbed to about 1,500 in the spring, fell by half, then came back to 3,000. We kept publishing 2 a week through all of it.

-> A site that publishes 30 pages on Monday and nothing for a month looks like a content bomb. A site that publishes 2 every week for a year looks like an editorial team.

If I were Google and wanted to separate editorial teams from people bombing content, publishing volatility is the first thing I would look at. Pick a number. Hold it. One page a day is the ceiling on a new site.

Going multilingual

The hour is already paid. A second language costs almost nothing.

Check your domain first. On a .fr, a .de or a .co.uk you are not doing multilingual SEO, no matter how clean the implementation. Paul tested it on his .fr. The country domain is too strong a signal. Use a .com with subdirectories.

Then two checks: a language switcher that goes to the equivalent URL and not the homepage, and correct html lang plus hreflang. Get hreflang wrong and your two versions compete with each other instead of covering two markets.

## Module 9: Before you publish more, fix what you have

The fastest traffic is already on your site.

On a 50-page blog I went from 1,500 to 15,000 monthly clicks in three months without publishing a single new article. Three moves, in this order.

Move 1: Cut 15 to 20% of the pages

Pages that sat there for months with no clicks, written because I thought I should be publishing. Every one diluted the signal about what the site was about.

The filter: zero clicks and negligible impressions over 90 days, excluding anything published in the last three months. New pages haven't had time to prove anything. Cutting them is impatience.

Using ChatSEO, show me every page with zero clicks and under 50
impressions in the last 90 days, excluding anything published in the
last 3 months. For each one, tell me whether I should delete it,
merge it into another page, or rewrite it.

Move 2: Repoint pages at the keywords Google already gives them

This moved the most traffic, and almost nobody does it.

For each page, look at which queries it actually gets impressions for. Not the keyword you wrote it for. The keyword Google decided it was about. On most pages those were different.

So stop arguing with Google. Four changes per page:

- H1 rewritten around the new keyword

- Meta description rewritten around it

- First 100 words rewritten so it appears naturally and early

- The body checked so the page genuinely answers that query

That last one is the one people skip. Swap the H1 and leave the article answering a different question, and you've made the page worse.

One check first. High impressions and low clicks has two causes with opposite fixes:

- Position 8 to 15: striking distance. Repointing moves it.

- Position 1 to 3 and clicks still falling: an AI Overview is probably answering the query above you. Rewriting the title won't fix that.

Using ChatSEO, list the pages getting impressions for keywords they
are not optimised for. For each page: the keyword I targeted, the
keyword Google ranks it for, current position, CTR. Then give me the
new H1, meta description and first 100 words.

Move 3: Regroup into silos

Every remaining page grouped by topic, a hub page per group, and the pages inside each group linked to each other. 40 pages in a pile became four or five clear clusters.

Slower to pay off. It compounds rather than spikes.

Cut first, because there is no point optimising a page you're going to delete. Repoint second, because those pages already have proven demand. Restructure last, on a clean set.

Never let a model make the irreversible call

Daniel Agrici built Jev SEO, an open source audit skill for Claude Code. In his own evaluation file, the model suggested removing substantial posts. Twice. Not thin pages. Real articles.

The fix was not a better prompt. It was a line of code: removal is blocked for any page of 600 words or more, whatever the model says.

-> Let the model rank. Let code, or you, hold the veto on deletes.

## Module 10: If you're local, rank the profile, not the website

Local SEO is not regular SEO in a city.

When someone searches "plumber Houston", Google shows a map with three listings on top. Those are not websites. Those are Google Business Profiles. Fourth place is page two. Nobody scrolls the map.

Google picks those three on three factors:

- Proximity. How far the searcher is from your address. You cannot change it.

- Relevance. How sure Google is that you do this exact service. Content fills it.

- Authority. How much the web trusts you. Links fill it.

Most competitors filled in their profile once, three years ago. One category. Zero services. They ignore the only two factors they control.

Step 1: Measure before you touch anything

A rank map checks where your profile ranks from a grid of points across your city, 13 by 13 is common. Green is positions 1 to 3, yellow 4 to 10, red is Google not believing you do this service there.

Turn it into one number: your top-3%, the share of grid points where you're in positions 1 to 3. Position 4 is worth zero.

```
Attached is a rank-map export for my Google Business Profile on
[KEYWORD]. Columns: point, latitude, longitude, position.

1. Compute my top-3%: points in positions 1 to 3, divided by all
points. Show the division.
2. Describe where the green is and which direction is weakest.
3. List every point in positions 4 to 6 separately. Those are the
cheapest wins.
4. Use only the numbers in the file.
```

Step 2: The 30-minute profile audit

The same three mistakes on almost every profile.

- One category. Google allows up to 10. Every category opens another set of searches. Aim for 2 to 4 minimum, each one true.

- Five services. You want 20 minimum, 30 to 40 in a competitive city, each sitting under the category it belongs to.

- Empty boxes. Description at the full 750 characters, 20 photos minimum, every attribute ticked, a post every week.

This is where Sonnet fails, and it fails quietly. Ask it for categories cold and a few of the ten it hands you do not exist in Google's list. Same confident tone as the real ones.

The fix: never let it choose from memory. Get the real list (the GMB Everywhere Chrome extension shows what your competitors use), paste it, then:

```
Here is the full list of Google Business Profile categories: [PASTE].
Here are the categories my top 3 competitors use: [PASTE].

1. Pick 1 primary and 2 to 9 secondary categories for my business.
Choose ONLY from the list above, spelled exactly.
2. For each, one line on which searches it opens up.
3. Reject any category that describes a service I don't offer.
4. If nothing on the list fits, say so. Do not invent a category.
```

Then reviews. The text of a review matters. A 5-star review that says "fixed our water heater same day in Austin" tells Google more than ten that say "great service". When you ask for a review, ask the customer to mention what you did.

Step 3: The page your profile points to

On most single-location businesses that is the homepage. Seven checks:

1. Title tag: primary category + city

2. H1: primary category + city

3. A Google Maps embed of your profile

4. Your secondary categories as H2s

5. A widget showing your Google reviews

6. The address, character for character as on the profile

7. The phone number, character for character

Most local homepages have "Home" as the title. That is free ground.

Step 4: The Core 30

Your site mirrors your profile, page for page. 3 to 4 categories and 25 to 30 services give you about 30 pages: one homepage, one page per category ("drainage service Houston"), one per service ("water heater replacement Houston").

Every level links down from inside a paragraph. Order the 30 by real search volume, pulled from ChatSEO, highest first. That is your writing order.

Step 5: Let one number pick the next page

30 days after launch, rank-map your keyword again, then rank-map the 3 or 4 businesses that dominate it. The leader's top-3% is your ceiling. Your threshold is 25 to 50% of it.

- Below it: Google doesn't believe you're an expert yet. Build topical pages that answer the questions your customers ask.

- At or above it: push outward. Build pages about the places in your yellow zones, neighbourhoods and landmarks Google Maps already names.

Write each place page about the place, not about you. The housing, the problems common there, the route your team drives. A page that only swaps the name is the doorway pattern from Module 8.

# Part 3: Earn the authority

A perfect page on a weak domain ranks 40th. Nothing in Part 2 fixes that.

Google does not give a new site the time of day for roughly six months. It has no reason to index every site Claude can generate in an afternoon. Authority is how you get past that.

Every score for it is an estimate. Ahrefs has DR, Semrush has Authority Score. None of them is Google. Someone once told Paul, worried, that their DR dropped from 70 to 65. His answer: look at your Search Console. More clicks? On business keywords? That is the scoreboard.

Here is ours, in Ahrefs.

Domain rating under 10 a year ago, around 55 today.

There are 13 ways to get there, in five tiers, from free to paid.

Most founders start at the bottom. They open a link marketplace, pay €50, and wonder why nothing moves.

Start at the top. The cheapest links are the ones nobody can sell you.

## Module 11: Claim the links you already earned

You are not asking for a favour here. You are fixing an omission.

- Unlinked mentions. Someone wrote your name and didn't link it. Roundups, newsletter archives, forum threads, podcast show notes, "tools we use" pages. Acceptance is high because the person already decided you were worth writing about.

- Links pointing at dead sites. Find sites in your niche whose domain lapsed, list every page still linking to them, and email those pages: the link is dead, here is a page that replaces it. Their page currently sends readers into a 404. You're offering to fix it.

Axel, a ninja-linking consultant we had on the podcast, found the second one by being on the receiving end of it.

We find both with one prompt:

Using ChatSEO: I would like to find free backlinks. Please tell me
what I should do.

## Module 12: Ask for the links nobody sells

There is a whole class of links no marketplace can reach.

Email the sites already ranking where you want to be

Take the queries you want links from. Look at who ranks. Pull an email off the contact page. Send a version of this:

I liked your article on [topic]. We have one that complements it:
[URL]. Would you link to it?

Axel picked up links this way from photographers, local businesses, a town hall and a département website. None of those are for sale. Not at €50, not at €5,000. That is exactly why the link is worth something.

Ask to be added to the lists you're missing from

Filter before you send, or it's spam:

- The article ranks top 20 for a term you care about

- It was updated in the last 12 months

- It already includes at least one competitor

The third one matters most. The writer has already decided your category belongs.

Your list covers [what it covers] well. None of the [N] tools
[the thing yours does]. Here's a free account, no card.
Judge for yourself, and if it doesn't belong in the piece,
ignore this email.

The floor outcome is a mention without a link. Not a waste. Those roundups are what ChatGPT reads when someone asks which tool to use. Part 4 is built on that.

Steal your competitors' linkers

Anyone linking to three of your competitors already believes your category deserves a link.

Using ChatSEO: find my 3 best competitors at my level, not the
industry giants. Analyse the backlinks they have, then find the
contact emails of the people linking to them. One table: site, page
linking, competitor linked, contact email. Never invent an email.

The machine that sends all of it

1. Leads. Claude lists who ranks, who links to competitors, who mentioned you.

2. Mailboxes. A sending tool like Instantly, on a lookalike domain, never your main one, warmed up for about 20 days.

3. Sequence. One email, a follow-up a few days later, a second follow-up. That's enough.

4. Replies. Claude reads them every day, sorts them, drafts the answer. You approve.

Paul's bar: five emails a day, every day. Axel lets Claude Code send through his Gmail, capped at 10 an hour, business hours only. 500 emails go out over three days instead of one afternoon.

-> Most link deals die because the yes sat unanswered for a week.

## Module 13: Trade links that make both pages better

Once you have pages that rank, you stop asking. People come to you.

Publish your own listicles. Best tools in your category, alternatives to the incumbent. Include competitors honestly.

At first they do nothing. Then a few start ranking and the dynamic flips. You have a page with traffic that other people want to be in.

Then you swap. You list them in your ranking. They list you in theirs.

The policy line: Google's link spam policy lists excessive link exchanges as spam. The test I use: would I include this business if they had nothing to offer me? If no, skip it.

A handful of swaps between businesses that belong together is an editorial decision. Fifty reciprocal links across a ring of sites is a footprint.

## Module 14: Earn links with something worth citing

A homepage is not citable. A writer needs something specific to link to.

Ranked by how hard they are to copy:

- A free tool. Good, but a competitor clones it in a week.

- An infographic. Works only if the stat underneath is yours.

- Your own data. Nobody can copy your numbers. No audience yet? Publish your numbers first.

Then the places you post rather than pitch:

- Reddit, YouTube, Medium, LinkedIn articles. They rank on authority domains you don't own.

- One review platform. Trustpilot for SaaS and e-commerce, Google Business Profile for local. One strong profile beats three weak ones.

- Events. A brand runs an event, local press shows up and writes about it. Motoblouz got covered by regional papers like La Voix du Nord this way. Press links point at your homepage though. They won't push the one page you need to rank. You need both.

- Bylines. Antoine, who runs the agency SEO Monkey, wrote for Les Echos Solutions for a year. The trap: bylines depend on one person. Paul's Journal du Net links stopped the day the editor who approved them left.

We never ran a link campaign for ChatSEO. Our DR came from exactly this kind of footprint: a sponsored article on Medium, a Reddit thread, a review of the tool on an authority site.

And under all of it, the base. People wrote about ChatSEO because there was something to write about. An SEO agent that connects to Search Console and acts on it was a story. Another keyword tool with a chat box would have been nothing to say.

-> Every method in this part is a multiplier. If the product gives people nothing to say, you are multiplying zero.

## Module 15: Buy last, and read the footprint

Read the policy first.

Google's link spam policy says links that pass ranking credit in exchange for payment violate it, on both sides. A compliant paid link carries rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow", which removes exactly what you paid for.

-> Anyone selling you a "safe dofollow placement" is selling a policy violation with a reassuring name.

The usual outcome is not a penalty. It's a link that gets discounted, and you paid for nothing.

We bought some. They were the weakest thing we did, and they stopped compounding the moment we stopped paying.

If you buy anyway, buy outside the link economy. If the site could sell you a link, the link is worth less.

Five checks before you pay:

1. The traffic curve. 12 months up and to the right. Declining means you're buying right before it hits zero.

2. Real, on-topic traffic. Top pages and keywords adjacent to yours.

3. The page, not the domain. A DR 70 site with a page that gets zero visits passes almost nothing.

4. The homepage tell. "Featured article" across ten unrelated categories means it exists to sell slots.

5. The price. €50 means someone else paid €50 a hundred times.

Google is not counting your links. It reads the shape.

Pull the SERP you want. If the top three have between two and four backlinks each and you build twenty, you haven't outworked them. You've announced yourself.

The anomalies that make a profile look built, from Axel:

- 100% exact-match anchors. From outside, real people link with your brand, your URL, "here", "this tool". Exact match only from your very best links. Inside your own site, exact match is fine.

- One TLD. A bilingual site with only .com links stayed stuck in France until it got .fr and .org links.

- 100% WordPress. The default stack of link-selling sites.

- Zero nofollow. A real brand collects nofollow forum links and spam without trying.

-> A profile that's too clean is the anomaly.

The number nobody screenshots

Over our lifetime we picked up 4K backlinks across 787 referring domains. Live, at the last count, it was 1.4K and 651.

Roughly two thirds of every link we ever earned was already gone. Without anyone doing anything wrong.

Whatever you build this quarter, price it against the share of it that will still exist next year.

# Part 4: Get named where Google and AI look

Ask ChatGPT who the best SEO consultants in France are.

Paul is in the answer.

The source is not his website.

## Module 16: Target the query ChatGPT types, not the prompt your customer types

You will never know the prompt. You can know the search behind it.

Jacky runs Links Garden, a French link-building platform. His team types the same 1 million prompts into ChatGPT every month and had done it for five months when he came on the podcast. 5 million answers, every brand in them extracted.

What his data says:

- Two kinds of answers. With sources, ChatGPT searched the web. Without sources, it answered from training data.

- Training data lags. Roughly a year and a half between the web and the model. A brand launched this year is not in there. Search is the only way in.

- It searches Google. And what it types tracks Google's rankings closely.

- Sources rotate. One prompt draws on about 50 sources over time, 10 to 15 per answer, reshuffled every month.

- Authority is not the filter. Jacky found a site with 5 referring domains cited 200 times, and one with 200 referring domains never cited.

That last point is the hopeful one. GEO rewards being on the right page, not having the biggest site.

The fan-out

When ChatGPT decides to search, it rewrites the conversation into two to five short Google queries.

Jacky's example. Someone tells ChatGPT they hurt their back at judo a month ago, saw their doctor, rested, and still hurt when they sleep. ChatGPT doesn't search "judo doctor back pain sleep". It searches "best mattress back pain 2026".

This kills the main objection to GEO. Every prompt is different. The fan-outs converge.

The shapes they take:

- "Best + money keyword + year + country." The dominant pattern for about a year. Best because the user wants a recommendation. The year because the model wants fresh sources.

- Two languages. A French prompt gets searched in French and in English.

- "Reviews + your brand", "alternative to + your competitor". The families closest to a purchase, per Antoine.

- site: on authority domains. The newer pattern. In some niches, one to three fan-outs now go straight to government sites and Wikipedia.

So GEO starts as a keyword list, built from your money keywords from Part 1.

Step 4 becomes the prospect list for the rest of Part 4. Every listicle ranking on a fan-out query is a page ChatGPT is likely to read.

What not to waste a week on

Google's documentation on AI features is blunt: "There are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary." You don't need new machine-readable files, AI text files or markup to appear there.

So if your agent proposes an llms.txt sprint, say no. The levers are the boring ones. Be cited by the pages the engines already cite. Keep the facts on your own pages current, in text, crawlable.

## Module 17: Stop ranking yourself first

Putting yourself 1st in your own ranking was the cheapest GEO trick there was.

Paul did it for years. "Best SEO consultants in Paris", with Paul at number one, on his own site. ChatGPT cited the page, and cited him.

Then the source changed.

He was still in the answer. The page cited was now someone else's ranking.

Everyone ranks themselves first. The model has learned that, and discounts it.

Paul had Claude rewrite every ranking where he put himself first. His consultant site, its .com twin, and the ChatSEO blog, where we had ranked our own tool first. It burned through a day's worth of Claude usage in a few hours.

This is a trade-off, not a rule:

- For classic Google, a self-ranked page can still win. Paul still sees rankings like his at the very top of results.

- For GEO, it no longer gets you named.

- For your reader, it costs trust.

Paul removed his. If your rankings bring in clients from Google, test before you rewrite all of them.

Step 3 protects your revenue. Never trade a page that sells for a citation you might get.

## Module 18: Get ranked by others

A ranking on someone else's site is worth more than ten on yours.

A restaurant saying it is the best convinces nobody. A Paris guide naming it first does. Same for the model.

The ranking swap

Paul's rankings of agencies get him email. Agencies want in. He asks for no money. He asks for one thing back: a ranking on their own site that lists him, or ChatSEO.

Convertix is the live example. They published best SEO consultant in France, best SEO MCP. Paul published best Google Ads agency, best Meta Ads agency.

When Paul tested it live on a podcast, logged out, ChatGPT named him among the best SEO consultants in France. The source in the citations was Convertix's ranking.

Two rules make swaps compound:

- Recency. Refresh every year, with the new year in the title.

- Volume. Antoine thinks most businesses have at least 20 queries worth a swap.

Your half of the swap is a page. Run it through page-brief and ship-page like any other. We never appear in a ranking of our own category.

The ladder

Not every placement is a swap. Antoine sorts the rest into four rungs.

1. Cheap network links. Small blogs that will publish a ranking without blinking. Antoine's math: if a €7 link holds your GEO query for a month, it paid.

2. Guest posts on businesses. Sites in your niche that sell a product, not visibility.

3. Digital PR on pure players. Online-only media with authority in one niche, before any national paper.

4. Become an author. Your byline on a domain the model trusts.

The cheap citation is not worse

Read this twice before you pay for a big media mention.

Jacky sees clients pay €1,000 to €2,000 for a single citation in a big media. It gets cited for one to three months, then drops out of the rotation.

A €10 to €20 placement does about the same.

-> In the citation game, the label "PBN" scares people more than it scares the model.

The outreach machine from Module 12 sends all of this. Same leads, same sequence, same five emails a day.

## Module 19: Find the Reddit threads the model is reading

Reddit is cited constantly. But check your engine before you commit a quarter to it.

Published breakdowns put Reddit at roughly 46.7% of Perplexity's top sources and about 3% on Gemini. And in Jacky's French ChatGPT data, Reddit's share fell from about 30% to 9% in July, then to about 5% in August.

-> Whatever is overused gets turned down. The model rotates.

If your buyers live where Reddit is cited, here is the method.

Step 1: Write 10 prompts, not 10 keywords

The actual sentence a buyer types at 11pm when they're annoyed. Ask ChatGPT for 50 questions your customer would ask, pick 10.

"Cheapest alternative to Ahrefs for a solo founder." "Is it worth paying for an SEO tool if I only have 20 pages."

None of them contain "SEO software". Buyers describe their problem. Marketers describe the category.

Step 2: Run them logged out

A logged-in account is personalised by your history. You want the answer a stranger gets.

Step 3: Read the sources, not the answer

Click the sources and read what the model built the answer from. Across 10 prompts you'll usually find four or five Reddit threads.

If a competitor is quoted in three of them and you're in none, that is not a content problem. That is the whole problem.

Step 4: Run the fan-out too

Ask the model to list the sub-questions it would need to answer first. Run those, check their sources. Those threads are less contested, because nobody optimises for a query they can't see.

Step 5: Comment as yourself

Say who you are in the first line. "I build one of these (ChatSEO), so discount me accordingly."

Then answer properly, including where your product is the wrong choice. For a 20-page site with no traffic yet, ChatSEO usually is. Saying that costs me nothing and it's the reason the comment survives.

One thread every two or three days. Not ten in an afternoon.

Which subreddits

Don't pick them by size. Pick the ones Google already ranks on your best keywords.

Using ChatSEO: find my 10 best traffic generating keywords. Then tell
me if a subreddit is ranking on each of these keywords. If so, give me
the URL of the subreddit.

Warm the account up before anything promotional. 10 karma, five quality comments a day for three days, rules read before every post.

## Module 20: Your domain gets 2 slots. Your brand can take 6.

On the keywords that make money, your domain gets two listings at most and no amount of good SEO buys a third.

So stop trying to rank the page. Occupy it.

Type a comparison query in your category and count what's on the first screen. A video pack. A Reddit thread. A listicle from a site that doesn't sell in your category. A LinkedIn post.

-> Rank the queries by how many non-website results the SERP already shows, not by how many people type them.

The layers:

- One video per keyword. YouTube ranks very well inside Google. You film once, you're indexed twice. Title shape for review queries: "{Tool} Review {Year}: Features, Pricing & Alternatives". The description is not a caption, it's the text Google indexes. 200 words minimum, the query answered in the first two lines.

- Three Shorts per video, three different queries. Then the same files to TikTok, with the caption rewritten for how people type in TikTok search. On my last consumer app, 99.3% of TikTok views came from search and 0% from the For You page.

- The listicle you want to be in, posted on LinkedIn or X. Indexed posts rank. Write the first line as the exact query.

- A comment in the thread you will never outrank. With the disclosure.

Then the rest of the footprint:

- Social: your niche picks the network. Cosmetics and food on Instagram and TikTok. Services and B2B on LinkedIn, X, Reddit. Software on X, YouTube, GitHub, Reddit. Three or four at most.

- Reviews: one platform. Trustpilot for SaaS and e-commerce, Google Business Profile for local.

- Wikipedia: don't ask. Antoine submitted a request once. Refused, with the moderator's username on the refusal. The way onto Wikipedia is to build enough presence elsewhere that someone else decides you belong.

The trap on every one of these: the video that reads as an ad. Someone who typed a competitor's name came for a verdict on that product. The video has to be the best answer to the query, including where the competitor beats you. That admission is the only reason the pitch at the end survives.

# Part 5: Run it every week, and never faster

GEO is not a ranking you hold. It is a rotation you stay in.

SEO is the same, slower.

## The loop, the waits and the rules

Google deliberately delays the effect of changes. You cannot reverse-engineer it in a week.

- After a change: a dip is normal. Give it up to two months. Reverting in a panic is how you teach Google you're testing it.

- Before buying links: three months on a page you know is good.

- On a new domain: six months before anything feels like it's working. Then a pivot, where new pages rank top 5 on arrival. That's when you turn the drip up.

The Monday review:

Paul's own site now takes him about ten minutes a week.

The first Monday of the month, the GEO check. Rerun geo-queries, compare with last month, and check every third-party ranking you're listed in is still listing you. Then test 10 of your queries by hand, logged out, and note cited yes or no.

That last step stays manual on purpose. Jacky's team scrapes ChatGPT logged out because the API returns different sources than the web app. Ten queries by hand once a month is honest data. A dashboard built on the API is not the same thing.

Put both on a routine with /schedule in Claude Code and the reports wait for you.

Last, the rules your agent runs under, written before its first task:

```
ALLOW
- Read Search Console, analytics and ChatSEO
- Create drafts, write to the SEO log

REQUIRE MY APPROVAL
- Publish a page, or update a live one
- Change a title on a page that gets clicks
- Add or change a redirect

BLOCK
- Delete any page
- Edit robots.txt or canonical tags
- Send any email outside the company
- Buy anything
```

And every time you reject something, say why, and have the agent write the reason in a "SEO standards" file it reads before every draft.

-> That file becomes your editorial line, written by your own rejections. It outlives the tool.

## Where I am wrong, or at least lucky

We started with an audience. Paul is one of the best known SEOs in France and has been doing it since 2021. Agencies email him to be in his rankings. Some of our links came because people already knew the name. A fresh domain with no brand starts slower than we did.

Most of the methods are not ours. Jacky, Antoine, Axel and Daniel are named where the method or the number is theirs. Jacky's numbers are French data on ChatGPT. Gemini and Claude may weigh things differently.

The local system is not our case study. ChatSEO is not a local business. Module 10 is what local agencies run for their clients, rebuilt so Claude does the writing.

We pick easy fights. Most of our patterns are low-competition queries. On a fresh domain going after commercial head terms, this exact process produces pages that rank 40th. The skills don't fix authority. They make sure you don't waste it.

It ages. The fan-out patterns already shifted once this year. Reddit's share of citations moved by a factor of six in a few months in Jacky's data. Some of Part 4 will be wrong by spring.

One company. Our blog, Paul's sites, a handful of customers. An anecdote, and I would rather say that than have it said in the replies.

The part I am confident generalises is the order. The part I am not confident generalises is the speed.

## What I would do with a fresh domain tomorrow

- Connect Search Console to ChatSEO and run money-keywords before writing a single page

- Fix what already exists: cut, repoint, regroup

- Build one reference page per pattern by hand, with page-brief and ship-page

- Write the template and the process file, then publish 2 pages a week and never skip a week

- Claim every unlinked mention, then email 5 sites a day that rank where I want links

- Publish my own roundups, and trade placements once they rank

- Start geo-queries in month three, once there are pages worth citing

- Run weekly-seo every Monday and never touch a page edited in the last 60 days

In that order, because each one only works if the previous one exists.

Pick the money. Build better than the top 3. Earn the links. Get named by others. Wait. Repeat every week.

Thanks for reading!

title: 🔥 Muse 终极玩法：全自动撸 Claude 账号！！「完整教程」
body:
> 本文适合第一次用 Muse 的新手。全程 Muse 自己操作，你只需要回答它几个问题。

先看录屏，整个过程不到两分钟👇🏻

## 🤔 Muse 是什么？

Muse 是 Meta 前几天刚发布的个人 AI Agent。

和普通聊天机器人最大的区别是：它不只是回答问题，而是真的能替你把事做完。

按官方介绍，Muse 有自己的电脑（文件系统 + 终端）和一个完整的浏览器，可以：

- 搜索、浏览网页，填表、提交

- 生成文档、表格、网页等文件

- 同时处理多个任务，关掉 App 也能在后台继续

- 付款、发消息这类关键操作，先弹卡片找你确认

注册账号这种「一步一步点下去」的活，正好适合交给它。

> 💡 官方介绍👉🏻 How We Designed Muse

Meta 发布公告👉🏻 Introducing Muse

## 📋 前置条件

1. 一个 Muse 账号（网页、桌面端、手机 App 都行，本文用 Mac 桌面端演示）

2. 一个还没注册过 Claude 的邮箱，能正常收信

3. 能正常访问 claude.ai 的网络环境

> ⚠️ Muse 目前首发面向美国，iOS、Android、网页端都支持。你的账号现在能不能用，以注册页面的提示为准。

> 🚨但是今天实测已经全面开放了，可能在灰度中。

## 🔧 第一步：登录 Muse

打开 muse.ai 或者桌面端，按提示登录，给你的 Muse 起个名字、选个头像。

我的叫 Jarvis😄

> 💡 第一次用建议先发一句合作规则，后面它会一直记着：

我是中文用户，时区 Asia/Shanghai（UTC+8）。
涉及提交表单、下单、付款或修改账号时，先告诉我要做什么，等我同意再执行。

## 🎯 第二步：一句话下任务

在聊天框里直接说：

我录屏里就是这么一句话。Muse 会在右边开一个浏览器，自己打开 claude.ai 看注册流程。

> 💡 想更稳一点，也可以把边界一次交代清楚，它中途就不会乱选：

## 💬 第三步：它问什么，你答什么

接下来就没你什么事了，等它来问你就行。实测一共问了这几次：

1. 用哪个邮箱？ 把邮箱发给它，它会自己填好、点 Continue with email

2. 验证邮件里的链接 / 验证码：去邮箱找 Anthropic 发来的邮件，把登录链接或验证码发给它。也可以自己在邮箱里点开链接完成验证，再告诉它「验证完了，继续」

3. 人机验证怎么处理？ 弹出 hCaptcha（「点击所有由布料制成的物品」这种 3×3 图片题）时，它会先停下来问你：是授权它来点，还是你自己接管。我选了让它来点，一次就过了✌🏻

4. 同意条款吗？ 页面上是消费者条款、使用政策和年满 18 岁确认，自己看一眼再让它点 Create account

5. 个人用还是团队用？ 回「个人」

6. 选哪个套餐？ 回「免费」，Free（$0）先体验就够了

7. 数据训练开关要不要关？ 「允许将聊天记录用于训练模型」默认是开的，它会建议你关掉，按自己的习惯回就行

8. 名字填什么？ 随便一个昵称

> 💡 想看它具体在干嘛，点 「打开浏览器」 就能看到实时画面。想自己动手点 「控制浏览器」 接管，点 「停止」 就能让它停下来。

> 🚨 如果人机验证它连续点不过，别让它反复刷新，直接接管自己点完，再跟它说「验证通过了，从当前页面继续」。反复刷容易触发更严格的风控。

## ✅ 第四步：验证

最后跟它说一句：

它会给新账号的 Claude 发一条「你好，请简单介绍一下你自己」。

看到 Welcome, xxx! I'm Claude.，而且 Claude 正常回复了，就说明账号注册成功了👏🏻

注册完自己再扫一眼：

- 左下角是不是 Free，有没有误开订阅

- 数据训练开关是不是你想要的状态

- 如果临时给 Muse 连了邮箱，用完可以在 Muse 的 Settings 里断开

## 💰 想升级 Pro / Max？

注册完默认是 Free。需要升级的，可以看我之前的两篇：

- 🚀礼品卡充值教程👉🏻 

- 🔥银行卡订阅教程👉🏻 点这里

## ❓ 常见问题

Q：Muse 一直在解释，没打开网页？

补一句明确的动作：「现在打开 Claude 注册页面开始操作，需要我介入时告诉我具体做什么。」

Q：一直收不到 Claude 的验证邮件？

先看垃圾箱，再确认邮箱地址没填错。链接和验证码有时效，过期了回页面重新发。尽量别用一次性临时邮箱，很容易被拦截。

Q：不知道 Muse 做到哪一步了？

点一下它的头像，能看到活动记录。也可以直接问它：「现在做到哪一步了？卡在哪？需要我补什么？」

Q：注册完想改数据训练开关？

在 Claude 的 Settings → Privacy 里可以再改。

Q：能让 Muse 一次注册很多个吗？

不建议。批量注册违反 Claude 的服务条款，很容易被风控连带封号。正常注册一个自己用就好。

以上只是建议，你可以不听😄

其实可以使用域名邮箱（通过 Cloudflare ）实现批量注册！自己研究吧，低调点😄

> 🚨 登录链接、验证码就等于你的账号钥匙，只发给你自己的 Muse，别贴到别的地方。自己录屏、截图发出去之前，记得把邮箱和登录链接打码。

## 📚 历史文章汇总

1. 别让素材吃灰！手把手教你搭建「爆款视频创意生产线」

2. 一部手机装下所有终端 Agent，是什么体验？

3. 大模型本地部署完整指南

4. Hermes Agent 实战指南：从刷 X 焦虑到自动沉淀

5. 程序员防脱指南

6. Hermes 接入 iMessage

7. Hermes 接入 X Premium

8. Hermes Agent 完全指南

9. Hermes Agent 入门指南之辅助模型

10. Hermes Agent 入门指南

11. Hermes Agent 进阶指南

12. Hermes Agent 不完全指南

13. 尼区 Claude Pro 订阅完全指南

14. 尼区 Apple ID 注册教程

15. 土区半价订阅 ChatGPT Plus

16. 美区 Apple ID 注册

17. Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini 支付宝订阅

18. Mac 本地部署大模型完整教程

19. IP 质量检查

20. 为什么豆包不推荐你的品牌

21. 怎么和你奶奶解释豆包说的不是真的

想系统上手 Muse 的，推荐看 @0xlangeai 的这篇，写得很细👇🏻

附官方介绍：How We Designed Muse

> 📢 有问题欢迎评论区留言，我看到都会回。

如果这篇教程对你有帮助，欢迎 关注 + 收藏 + 转发 👏🏻

关注 @Lonely__MH，持续分享新手友好的教程和 AI 工具使用心得。

title: 别他妈闭门造车了！产品出海第一步：选择比努力重要 100 倍，快速完成比完美重要 1000 倍
body:
绝大部分做独立开发和产品出海的人，从第一天起就注定死透了。

为什么？

因为典型的程序员思维在作祟： 闭门造车憋大招，花 3 个月写出架构无比优美、组件封装无比严谨、UI 调得比 Apple 还性感的“完美产品”。

上线发推，祈求全网来围观，结果只有 3 个点击，其中 2 个还是自己刷的。

最后把自己感动得痛哭流涕，长叹一声“出海都是骗局”。

醒醒吧，这就是纯粹的自嗨！

在这个时代，做产品出海必须刻进骨髓的两条铁律：

选择比努力重要 100 倍！

快速完成比完美重要 1000 倍！

公网上的真实用户根本不在乎你的代码写得有多高深，他们只在乎当下正在爆发的需求，有没有一个页面能立刻解决他的痛点。

2026 年 3 月，我加入出海圈子仅两天半，甚至连那个英文词是什么意思都没搞懂，凭着一个 2 小时用 AI 搓出来的简陋静态页，24 小时干下了 26 万曝光、10 万真实海外点击。

单日广告进账 200 美元，当月2200美金。

这一篇，不讲虚头巴脑的宏大叙事，全是我自己经历的真实干货。带你手把手走一遍出海全流程：从 Trends 抓风口到二次挖词 -> 搜词知意与扒竞品 -> 域名三大打法与 5 刀低成本基建 -> 外链到底怎么堆 -> 中前期四大赚钱方向与避坑心得。

📑 本文实战导航目录（建议先赞后看，常读常新）

## 一、选词：如何在公网挖出能暴击的“黄金词”？

千万不要坐在家里拍脑袋想“我要做一个什么牛逼的产品”。

永远先看市场在搜什么，产品永远排在搜索需求后面！

1. Google Trends 实时抓取潜伏风口

做产品出海，Google就是最大的市场，打开 Google Trends（谷歌趋势），范围选择全球，我当时搜索的关键词是“ai”，它是近几年一直高热度的词。

日期建议选择过去一周，不要只看大盘的热搜新闻，去看热度上升的查询。

重点盯那些突然从第二页悄悄爬上来的生词。

拿我当时那个词为例：周日上午还在相关搜索第二页，周一上午窜到第 8，中午直接杀进第 4！

这就是肉眼可见、正在呈指数级爆发的真实流量风口。

当然这里有巨大的运气成分，但是更多的坚持去检查。

有的大佬直接做个监控插件，有变化后通知。

💡 实操小细节：TrendsBar 插件与“顺藤摸瓜”

如果你英语没那么好，或者觉得网页一页页看很慢、想批量导出数据，我推荐：

1. Chrome 插件利器：TrendsBar： 装上 TrendsBar 插件，可以直接把 Trends 页面上的飙升词、热度数据一键批量下载到本地 Excel。一目了然，完全不受语言障碍影响。

2. 二次搜索（顺藤摸瓜）： 下载完表格千万别停下！把第一批导出来的热词，当成新的词根，再扔进 Trends 搜一次！ 这样你就能顺藤摸瓜，挖出更深层、更垂直、竞争极小但意图极强的“二级长尾词”。

这招能帮你直接避开正面战场，捡到蓝海词。

2. 搜词知意：查清含义、过滤泛词、判定真空竞争度

从 Trends 抓到上升词之后，千万别无脑闭着眼睛建站，第二步必须是：搜词知意！

① 查清真实含义，不相关的果断枪毙

立刻把这个词扔进 Google 搜索前几页，阅读对应的维基百科、论坛解释或相关新闻，搞清楚它到底代表什么业务、解决什么问题。如果这个业务技术太复杂、甚至涉及法律红线，或者跟你能交付的东西八竿子打不着，果断放弃。

② 警惕巨头盘踞的“大泛词”，死磕垂直与蹭词

像ai tools、crypto这种超大词叫做“泛词”，权重全在巨头老站手里，新手碰一个死一个。优先抓两类高转化意图：小游戏相关、在线实用小工具相关。敏锐蹭词，精准截流：比如前段时间大火的jev或jav衍生词，随手一搜，网上已经有海量站点围绕这些词在疯狂收割海外流量。

出海初期在没有品牌心智时，不要羞于蹭词，能截到精准流量就是硬道理！

③ 判定结果页真空期（千载难逢的入场信号）

在 Google 搜索结果页，如果能同时满足以下 3 点，立刻买域名动手：

1. 搜索结果全是一堆论坛碎屑；前两页几乎都是 Reddit 讨论帖、X（Twitter）吐槽、Quora 问答；几乎没有一个正经的独立产品站！

2. 官方供给极弱、甚至动作迟钝：我当时发现对应这个词的官方网站才注册不到 7 天，权重极低，甚至连主流域名（.com）都没抢占。

3. 域名主流后缀大量闲置：打开query.domains查一圈，除了官方那个奇怪的小众后缀，主流后缀居然都还空着！

这就是供需严重脱节的真空窗口！海量老外在狂搜，全网却没有一个正经网页给他们交付。这时候必须分秒必争抢下生态位！

3. 选词进阶大杀器：Ahrefs、Semrush 与 Similarweb

如果你想把选词做到更科学、更量化，公网有三大顶尖工具必须了解：Ahrefs (ahrefs.com) 、Semrush (semrush.com)、Similarweb (similarweb.com)：

    1. Ahrefs (ahrefs.com) & Semrush (semrush.com)： 把关键词扔进去，大白话就看 3 个数：

- 月搜索量（Volume）：看每个月到底有多少人在搜；

- 竞争难度（KD）：新手强烈建议找 KD < 10 甚至 KD < 5 的词，这种就是软柿子，上几个基础外链就能轻松杀上首页；

- 每次点击广告值多少钱（CPC）：如果一个词点击一次值好几美金，说明商业价值极大，挂广告都能赚爽。

    2.  Similarweb (similarweb.com)： 竞品偷窥狂神器！看到别人出海赚到钱的网站，直接把网址扔进去，一键看透它的月总访问量、流量主要靠搜索还是社交网络、主要访客来自哪个国家。照着高手的成熟打法抄，是最稳的捷径！

但是注意：对小白用户来说不是必须的，他们的成本也不便宜，一个月闲鱼上也要100多。只是更好的辅助我们，没有也没有关系，Google Trends（https://trends.google.com/） 、google ads keyword planner （https://ads.google.com/aw/keywordplanner/home）。还有 https://ahrefs.com/keyword-difficulty 免费查KD（关键词难度，新手建议30以下） 绝对也是够用的

4. 搜不到突发热词？祭出哥飞“词根法”（Seed Keywords）

如果在 Google Trends 上碰巧遇上公网平淡期，没有突发热词怎么办？ 那就用哥飞方法论中的“词根法”进行穷举联想。

核心逻辑：以极强交易/工具意图的词根（Seed Keywords）为基准，组合垂直行业需求，批量挖掘长尾低 KD 词。

经典工具类词根组合：

- [功能] + generator（生成器：比如 bio generator、prompt generator、palette generator）

- [格式A] to [格式B] + converter（格式转换：比如 webp to png、pdf to docx、pdf 2 img）

- [行业] + calculator（计算器：比如 cagr calculator、macro calculator）

- [大牌工具] + alternative（竞品替代：比如 notion alternative、canva alternative）

小游戏/娱乐类词根组合（可以在 Roblox 上去找灵感）：

- [游戏名] + unblocked / play [游戏名]（免拦截版/在线玩，海外学生搜索量巨大）

- [游戏名] + online

- [游戏名] + tools / wiki

- [主题] + simulator（模拟器类）

注：小游戏类词往往搜索量极大，通常通过挂广告展示来快速变现。


学会这套词根穷举法，能让你彻底摆脱“看天吃饭”的焦虑，源源不断地挖出几百个蓝海建站机会

## 二、极速上线：域名实战法则、极低成本基础设施与系统复用

很多人出海死在“准备工作”上：选框架、搭脚手架、配数据库、挑设计系统……等你折腾完两个月，风口早他妈凉透了。

当热度按小时狂飙时，你的窗口只有半天！

1. 域名选择的实战军规与灵活变通

- 军规一：域名与核心关键词保持高度一致（Exact Match Domain, EMD）： 如果关键词是xyz tool，域名最好就直接是xyztool.com，搜索引擎权重倾斜极其明显，海外用户一眼看到也是天然信任。

- 军规二：坚决使用国际通用域名： 我们做的是海外产品出海，赚的是老外的钱！国外普通用户根本不知道比如.cn是什么，点击率直接暴跌。

- 军规三：万事不绝对，多层级替代方案：如果 .com 被占了，去找 .net、.org、.pro、.app，或者加词缀如 xyz-tool.com，核心是方便老外记住。关于大火的 .ai 域名：有预算直接冲没问题，自带科技光环，但门槛高（通常要买 3 年起），基于自己的情况来。

域名购买神器推荐：Spaceship (spaceship.com)： 别再去 GoDaddy 或 Namecheap 忍受复杂的加价套路了。通常最便宜，解析速度快，没有任何乱七八糟的隐形扣费。你有更便宜的选择，优先你的方式。

2. 系统复用与极低成本基建（作者私藏武器库）

很多技术人每次做新站都要从零写一套鉴权、排版、支付，累死累活。真正的出海老鸟，全靠“系统复用”！

① 系统代码库复用（一套模板，极速裂变）

当你完成过第一个合格的站点后，把它的通用骨架（前端响应式布局、多语言 SEO 标签、深色模式、用户鉴权、Stripe 支付组件、API 转发接口）抽象成一套内部脚手架。下一个新词出现时，直接 Clone 现有工程，换上新的关键词、文案和核心功能，1 到 2 个小时直接发布！这种工业化流水线的复用速度，能把竞争对手打得找不着北。

不一定非要框架，买模板，你手搓绝对能搓出来。GitHub上有开源项目，拿来改造完全够用。你想省麻烦，10分钟就上线先登录注册、多语言、api、生图、生视频的能力，又没有复用模板， 我推荐 @idoubicc 的shipany和 @indie_maker_fox 的mksaas。

我自己用的是mksaas，我买的原因是当时赚钱了，买这些没有压力，后面对模板魔改的也很厉害。

② 极低成本部署神器：Cloudflare（强烈推荐！）

部署网站不要傻乎乎去买昂贵配置的独立云服务器。强烈推荐直接用 Cloudflare（Pages / Workers）！它是目前全球 CDN 加速和部署成本最低的方案，抗 DDoS 攻击能力极强。性价比炸裂：作者目前买的是5 美金/月的套餐，一口气跑了6 个出海独立网站，丝滑流畅，全球秒开，几乎零运维成本！

③ 数据库搭配：Neon (Serverless Postgres)

如果网站需要存储数据，直接接入Neon (neon.tech)。 Serverless 架构，根据请求自动伸缩，自带连接池，其免费额度（Free Tier）对于中前期的出海工具站来说完全够用，基本处于零成本运行状态。

④ 数据监控不用学了，直接让 AI 当牛马！

以前很多人卡在 GSC（Google Search Console）和 GA4（Google Analytics 4）埋点上，看几十页文档折腾两三天。现在根本不需要学了！把前端代码扔给 Claude / Cursor：“帮我把 Google Search Console 和 Clarity 验证文件配置好，把 Google Analytics 4 的测量 ID 埋进去”。

同时安装clarity，这样当用户浏览我们的网站的时候，我们可以查看用户使用行为，便于复盘优化网站。

AI 2 分钟写好代码，你直接推到 Cloudflare 部署，秒完成全站流量监控！代码可以糙，数据监控一秒都不能缺！

## 三、流量的死穴：外链的本质是“投票”，狂堆外链拉开差距！

你的网站上线了，为什么是个公网孤岛？为什么排名会往下掉？ 很多人以为是在跟 Google 算法斗智斗勇。

大错特错！实际上，添加外链根本不是在跟 Google 竞争，而是在跟你的竞争对手竞争！

外链的底层逻辑：公网的“民主投票”我们可以把 Backlinks（外链）粗暴地理解为公网用户对你投的一张赞同票。

如果你和竞争对手做了同一个词，一个用.com，一个用.net，甚至你们两家的网页代码和内容长得一模一样，Google 凭什么把排名给谁？

Google 只会认谁拿到的投票多！

投票也有“健康票”与“垃圾票”之分：

- 用机器批量刷的垃圾农场站外链，就是作弊票，Google 一旦发现直接惩罚降权；

- 找真正的大牛博客、高权重权威媒体给你的链接，相当于一张顶一万张的超级赞同票。

通俗类比：就像你在 Twitter/X 上发了一条帖子：

- 只有几个机器人水军回复，算法根本不理你；

- 底下有大量真人真实评论，算法开始推流；

- 突然有两个万粉科技大 V 给你转发背书，你的推文直接全网爆火！外链就是公网世界里的大 V 转发背书！

1. 冷启动期：暴力堆外链，快速拉升域名信任度

海外导航站 / Directory 全网轰炸： 批量提交到 Product Hunt、Toolify.ai、There's An AI For That (TAAFT)、Futurepedia 以及各种垂直细分 Directory（搜submit your tool/ai directory list）。这一步能迅速为你沉淀几十到上百个高权重的 DoFollow/NoFollow 投票，让 Google 爬虫几小时内完成全站收录。

【避坑警示】：不要一天就把所有的干完了， 考虑到有些外链需要审核，建议是一周5-15个外链，这个没有标准，反正我是这么干的， 然后坚持，坚持永远是最难的， 我是停更了1个多月，又慢慢的开始。

高权重 Web 2.0 与社媒埋链： 在 Medium、Dev.to、Hashnode 撰写使用指南并自然内嵌链接；去 Reddit 相关的 Subreddit、X 垂直标签分享实用心得。

付费外链加速： 在 Upwork 上挑选高 DR（Domain Rating > 40-50）的海外科技类博客发 2-3 篇相关的 Guest Post。有对应社群，有些大佬也会分享他们自己的渠道，可以学习。

【避坑警示】：千万别买 Fiverr 上“$5 发 5000 条”的垃圾 PBN 外链，那种不健康投票会被 Google 判定作弊，整个域名彻底报废！

2. 中后期：精细化外链的精细活（你的长期护城河）

三大精细化外链搞法：

1. 竞品外链逆向工程：用 Ahrefs 或 Semrush 扒光竞品前 3 名的所有外链，看他们都在哪些博客被推荐，顺藤摸瓜找站长发邮件做内容置换。

2. 死链替换法（捡漏神技）：排查老牌权威博客里失效的 404 工具链接，发邮件提醒博主换成你的新工具，成功率极高。

3. 打造外链磁铁：在网站上免费开源一份独家数据表或好用小插件，海外博主写文章时会为了引用数据主动免费帮你打广告。

坦白讲：我的第一个网站其实还没做到这一步，因为当时运气好赶上了热度爆发。

但我想说明的是，这一步才是真正拉开我们做产品出海距离的胜负手！这一步我也在做，也还在深度学习中。

3. 心态与坚持：哥飞的“网站遗忘法则”

做精细化外链，最难的从来不是技巧，而是心态和坚持。 特别是针对处在初期阶段的朋友，你会陷入这种周期律：不停地兴奋 -> 疯狂坚持 -> 几天看不到效果 -> 失落、怀疑、恐惧 -> 偶尔来点流量再次兴奋……

在这个磨人过程中，一定要保持极好的心态。哥飞总说过一句话：当你把这个网站做到你认为合格之后，做好它的外链建设，然后把它忘掉，隔五六个月再去看！

你会惊讶地发现，搜索引擎的沙盒期过后，这个网站自然发展的成果，可能比你想象中要好得多！

## 四、中前期做站的四大黄金方向

做网站出海，对于中前期的小伙伴来说，到底有哪些具体方向能跑通变现？

总结下来主要有四类：

1. 小游戏资讯站 / 游戏工具站（正反馈最快）

特点：极易得到正反馈，非常容易拿到你的第一个订单或第一笔美金（比如 1 美元、2 美元）。

变现：主要通过流量广告接入广告商（如 AdSense、Adsterra 等），这正是我第一个网站跑通盈利的核心模式。

2. 实用工具站（积分与轻量订阅）

特点：像 PDF 转文档、网页转图片、格式转换、计算器等刚需小工具。

变现：用户为了免除限制或高频使用，会购买额度积分，或者成为轻度订阅用户。

3. AI 工具站（客单价高，容易拿到大订单）

特点：这是目前最卷但也最具爆发力的方向。说“容易”，是指相比于几十美分的广告，AI 工具更容易拿到大金额的高客单价订单！

现状与思考：这个方向需要更深度的思考与产品壁垒。我目前也正在全力重构和深耕我的AI 工具站，中间踩了极其多的坑，但这也是真正能赚到持续大钱的资产。

4. 代充站（中间商赚差价，公网高爆方向）

特点：虽然严格来说不属于纯软件出海，但属于当前非常火爆的变现渠道。

模式：现在海外有很多成熟的开源代充网站系统，你只需要找到可靠的上游批发供应商，搭建好网站获取真实用户，帮他们在你的网站下单或代操作，纯赚差价，流水极大。

## 五、除了做网站，出海还有哪些坑？写给新手的大实话

产品出海是一门真正的综合商业实践。除了上述的选词和建站，还有很多深水区的实操细节：

- 海外收款与合规结汇：如何低成本注册海外公司与 Stripe 账户，如何通过合规渠道把美金安全换回国内人民币；

- AI 接口防护防白嫖：做 AI 工具站，如何防止前端 API Key 泄露、如何做并发风控和限流，防止被黑客薅秃破产；

- 付费广告投放前沿尝试（正在实测）：除了等自然 SEO，我们最近也正在实测付费广告投放（Google Search Ads、Twitter Ads、Reddit 针对性投流），通过精准测算客单价与获客成本（CAC），测试正向投产比（ROI）；

- 科学定价策略：是定 9.9 美元还是 29.9 美元？如何设置免费试用额度（Freemium）和付费墙（Paywall）才能把转化率拉到极致？

这些更深度的实操细节，以及更多进阶的找词黑科技，我最近都在亲自踩坑、重构和测试，后续也会在我的账号上逐步复盘拆解。

给小白出海者的掏心窝子话：正反馈大于一切！

最后，我想针对很多第一次尝试产品出海的小白朋友，说几句极其掏心窝子的大实话：

1. 第一次做产品出海，其实做什么都不重要，重要的是把流程完整跑通一次！不要在赛道选择上内耗一个月，严格按照这套 SOP：找词 -> 2 小时上线 -> 秒接监控 -> 狂堆外链 -> 接入变现，哪怕是一个极其粗糙的小页面，只要你完整跑通了全流程，你的认知就会发生质的飞跃。

2. 尽可能找圈内前辈请教，确认方向没有大偏移： 出海最忌讳闭门造车在死胡同里撞得头破血流。多去推特、社群向拿到过结果的前辈、老鸟虚心请教，让他们帮忙看一眼你的选词逻辑和网站结构，确认你的打法和方向没有根本性的偏差。

3. 宁愿选一个能快速拿正反馈的“简单小词”，也绝不要碰耗死人的“老词大词”！很多新手心比天高，一上来就想挑战行业大词，结果折腾两三个月，后台点击还是 0。相信我，在长期没有正反馈的漫漫黑夜里，那种失落、怀疑和自我否定是极度痛苦、极度消耗心智的，绝大多数人就是在这个阶段被活活熬死的！宁愿去找一个竞争极小、看似不起眼的简单词、冷门小词！只要能看到真实的海外点击涌入，哪怕第一周只赚到 1 美元、2 美元，这种真真切切的正反馈，给你建立起的第一个信心就是无价之宝！也可以找朋友一起抱团取暖，有了信心，你才能在出海这条路上一直活下去！

在这里，推荐大家去关注 @gefei55 哥飞老师和 @hezhiyan7 赫兹大哥。有兴趣的朋友可以去翻看他们的微信公众号，以及他们在 X 上的干货复盘。按照我的亲身体会，你基本上把哥飞和赫兹公开发布的帖子、文章认真研读一遍，就完全足够你独立搞定一个网站、完成基本的产品出海，这没有任何问题！绝对能让你少走几个月的弯路。

最后，真正拉开人与人差距的，从来不是什么不传之秘。最核心的，永远是去执行、去验证、去复盘、去坚持，在实战的泥潭里干中学！

## 💬 后续分享预告

如果你对产品出海、AI 搞钱、选词实战、以及正在尝试的海外广告投放与定价测算感兴趣，欢迎关注我！ 

我会把我做出海Ai产品 踩过的每一个坑、每一个真实的海外订单数据毫无保留地复盘发出来，一起赚美刀。
